Please review the following job description:

Truist Corporate Finance originates, structures and executes complex financing and capital structure transactions across the Commercial Bank, including leveraged buyouts, acquisition financings, recapitalizations and other transformative transactions involving founder and private equity owned companies. The team works across the full transaction lifecycle, from early-stage idea generation and evaluation through underwriting, diligence, internal approval, documentation and closing.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Following is a summary of the essential functions for this job. Other duties may be performed, both major and minor, which are not mentioned below. Specific activities may change from time to time.

  • Conduct industry and company research using available resources to source prospect names, develop and refine prospect lists in coordination with industry coverage team and partners
  • Develop pitch materials including industry specific and general economic information
  • Contribute industry relevant material for internal deal discussions i.e. org calls and credit screens and take leadership role in such calls
  • Generate customized industry-specific content for internal and external purposes
  • Take ownership of basic client follow up activities as appropriate
  • Track calling and marketing efforts to clients and prospects, reinforce proper use of CRM system with the coverage team, assisting as needed
  • Develop enhanced understanding of the market, credit, and products; continue to develop relationship management skills with appropriate autonomy
  • Demonstrate a continuously increasing knowledge of assigned industry, proactive creativity around idea generation, and a growing level of comfort with client interaction
  • Effectively work with partners and teammates with little oversight, able to take ownership of projects
  • Provide strategic perspective around industry expertise and initiatives that drive business growth

Required Qualifications: Associate I

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Three years of related financial services work experience
  • FINRA licenses: Securities industry Essentials Exam (SIE), Investment Banking Series Exam (79) and the Uniform Securities Agent State Law Exam (63) or ability to attain within 120 days of start date.
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Competitive drive and high work ethic, self-starter, team-oriented
  • Solid leadership and interpersonal skills
  • High level of adaptability and flexibility with strong organizational and time management skills
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Four years of related financial services work experience
  • FINRA licenses: Securities industry Essentials Exam (SIE), Investment Banking Series Exam (79) and the Uniform Securities Agent State Law Exam (63) or ability to attain within 120 days of start date.
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Competitive drive and high work ethic, self-starter, team-oriented
  • Solid leadership and interpersonal skills
  • High level of adaptability and flexibility with strong organizational and time management skills
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Minimum GPA: 3.0

title: Cardiology Technician (EKG) - per diem
description:
Welcome to Montage Health’s application process!

Job Description:

Position Summary

Under the leadership of the department director and assistant director, the Cardiology technician provides care to patients of all ages. Services include performing EKG’s, assisting with stress testing (stress echoes, Dobutamine stress echoes, nuclear stress tests, pharmacologic stress tests) and ambulatory recordings (holter monitors, event monitors, ambulatory blood pressure monitors). Duties include reporting to the interpreting physician any findings important in the delivery of necessary urgent care. Duties include but are not limited to attending in-services and continuing education as deemed necessary by the department supervisor and providing clerical assistance to the department. Participating in an on-call rotation is a requisite.

Experience

Excellent communication/interpersonal skills, both verbal and written.

Previous experience with independent performance of 12-lead EKG prior to hire required.

Stress testing experience in an acute care facility.

Experience with cardiovascular information systems (CVIS) to include data query, building of tables, monitoring performance by operator and physician. This includes stress test systems, EKG systems and their relationship to a house-wide CVIS.

Experience with monitoring/adjusting/coding for automated MD payment systems.

Education

High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent education and work experience in related field.

Licensure/Certifications

American Heart Association Healthcare Provider BLS certification is required. Must take and pass the CCI (Cardiovascular Credentialing International) EKG registry exam within 12 months of hire.


Equal Opportunity Employer

title: Local Clinical Project Manager
description:
The Local Clinical Project Manager (Sponsor dedicated) will be leading Local Study Teams at country level to deliver committed components of clinical studies according to agreed resources, budget and timelines complying with Sponsor Procedural Documents, international guidelines such as ICH-GCP as well as relevant local regulations.




In addition to leading the Local Study Teams, the Local Clinical Project Manager may perform site monitoring as needed to support the flexible capacity model. The Local Clinical Project Manager is responsible to ensure that sites are identified, site qualifications performed, set up, initiated, monitored, closed and documentation archived.





Main Responsibilities:


  • Has the overall responsibility for the study commitments within the country and for timely delivery of data to required quality.

  • Leads Local Study Team consisting of CRA(s), CSA(s), for assigned studies.

  • Leads the performance of the Local Study Team at country level ensuring compliance with Sponsor Procedural Documents, ICH-GCP and local regulations.

  • Ensures that clinical and operational feasibility assessment of potential studies is performed to the highest quality.

  • Coordinates the site selection process by identifying potential sites/investigators, performing initial Site Quality Risk Assessment, and conducting Site Qualification Visits to evaluate suitability and quality risks.

  • Ensures timely submission of application/documents to EC/IRB at start up and for the duration of the study. Works together with Regulatory Affairs to ensure timely delivery of application/documents for submissions to Regulatory Authority for the duration of the study, and in line with local regulations.

  • Ensures timely preparation of country financial Study Management Agreement (fSMA) and maintains accurate study budget in Sponsor clinical studies financial system.

  • Ensures timely preparation of local Master CSA (including site budget) and amendments as needed.

  • Ensures timely preparation of country level Master Informed Consent Form (MICF) and subsequent site level ICFs, including any relevant translations.

  • Ensures all country and site level trial essential documents required by ICH-GCP prior to study start have been collected.

  • Plans and coordinates applicable local drug activities (from local purchase or reimbursement to drug destruction).

  • Sets up and maintains the study in CTMS at study country level as well as local websites as required by local laws and regulations.

  • Oversees, manages and coordinates monitoring activities from site activation through to study closure at country and site level in accordance with the Monitoring Plans.

  • Reviews monitoring visit reports (as required and following Sponsor SOPs) and pro-actively advices the monitor(s) on study related matters.

  • Performs any required co-monitoring, Accompanied Site Visits/training visits with study CRAs.

  • Proactively identifies risks and facilitates resolution of complex study problems and issues.

  • Organises regular Local Study Team meetings on an agenda driven basis.





Required Skills and Qualifications:


  • Bachelor degree in related discipline, preferably in life science, or equivalent qualification.

  • At least a year of experience in Clinical Project Management at Local level.

  • Very good knowledge of Oncology therapeutic area.

  • Proven ability to lead and motivate cross functional teams to deliver clinical trials according to or ahead of time plan, budget and with required quality.

  • Excellent understanding of the Clinical Study Process including monitoring.

  • Excellent project management skills.

  • Strong ability to prioritize and handle multiple tasks, attention to details and negotiation skills.

  • Very good knowledge of spoken and written Portuguese and English language.

  • Good ability to learn and to adapt to work with IT systems.

  • Ability to travel nationally and internationally as required.





Please note: due to sponsor requirements for the role only candidates based in the listed location/s will be considered. Any applications from candidates based outside of these locations will not be considered.

title: Dutch/English Speaking L1 Service Desk Support Agent
description:
What success looks like in this role:

This role is responsible for providing high-quality customer service, accurate issue logging, initial diagnosis, and efficient resolution of incidents and service requests. The Level 1 Agent ensures timely ticket handling, documentation, and escalation when necessary, and contributes to continuous improvement through knowledge sharing and proactive user guidance.

Incident and Service Request Management

  • Log and raise tickets for incidents and service requests received through various contact channels (phone, web, chat, email).
  • Manage and resolve auto-generated tickets, ensuring end-to-end accountability and closure.
  • Strive for First Contact Resolution (FCR) by leveraging knowledge bases and troubleshooting resources.
  • Escalate unresolved issues to Level 1.5 or Level 2 support or additional resolver groups with all relevant diagnostic information.
  • Assign incidents requiring on-site intervention to Field Support (Level 1.5) for validation.
  • Conduct follow-up activities to confirm resolution and customer satisfaction before ticket closure.
  • Achieve defined Service Level Agreements (SLAs), Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and quality standards.

Customer Support & Communication

  • Serve as the single point of contact (SPOC) for end users throughout the incident lifecycle.
  • Provide courteous, efficient, and effective technical support for software, hardware, and network-related issues.
  • Deliver clear communication regarding ticket progress, estimated resolution times, and next steps.

You will be successful in this role if you have:


  • Minimum 2 years of experience in a service desk role or other similar technical role.
  • Language proficiency in English and Dutch at the C1 level or equivalent is a must.
  • Proficient in IT troubleshooting across software, hardware, Windows operating systems, Microsoft 365, and network environments.
  • Experience working with ticketing tools such as ServiceNow or similar ITSM platforms.
  • Strong customer service orientation and communication skills.
  • Ability to multitask and manage workload in a fast-paced environment.
  • Detail-oriented with excellent documentation and follow-up abilities.
  • Collaborative mindset with a focus on knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.
  • Critical thinking, diagnostic reasoning, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ownership mindset with a commitment to delivering a positive end-user experience

Unisys L1 IT support Specialist Team is for you if you would like to:

  • join an award-winning service desk team recognized for delivering excellent customer support
  • be part of a passionate team focused on customer solutions, collaboration, and continuous improvement
  • experience a truly diverse and international working environment
  • be a trusted team member with the support of experienced leaders and colleagues
  • work in an ethical and inclusive company culture where you can be yourself
  • build your career through our internal development and growth opportunities
  • work with a wide range of technologies and customers, giving you the opportunity to continuously learn and develop new skills
  • have access to online learning platforms to strengthen your technical and professional capabilities
  • contribute ideas, share knowledge, and help shape better ways of working
  • leverage modern technologies, including AI-powered tools and knowledge platforms, to work smarter and deliver an outstanding customer experience

What do we offer?

  • Full-remote working is supported
  • Monthly gross 44.200 HUF cafeteria - regardless of your weekly working hours
  • Fixed extra language allowance
  • Private Health Insurance - Premium Package provided for all Unisys associates after 6 months of tenure
  • Home office allowance
  • Last and foremost, a great team, as well as a lot of learning and training opportunities

title: Automotive Parts Associate
description:
7154 - Austin - 13300 North I-35 Service Road South, Austin, Texas, 78753

CarMax, the way your career should be!

Position Overview

As an Auto Parts Associate at CarMax, you’ll be the backbone of our service department, ensuring technicians have the right parts to keep vehicles running smoothly. This role combines precision, efficiency, and customer care, making you an essential part of delivering an exceptional automotive experience. You’ll manage inventory, assist with part identification, and maintain compliance standards—all while providing outstanding customer service. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment and enjoy problem-solving, this is your opportunity to join a team that values integrity, innovation, and growth.

Why CarMax?

At CarMax, we are the nation’s largest retailer of used cars with stores from coast to coast, and we are still growing. We’re rethinking the way people buy cars – and our associates help us do just that. We believe work should feel meaningful and rewarding, with opportunities to make an impact every day. Whether you’re advancing your career or growing your skillset, we are here to drive you forward.

Role Responsibilities

  • Identify and provide accurate parts for internal and external customers to ensure timely vehicle service.
  • Receive, stock, and maintain inventory with precision, including cycle counts and proper stocking levels.
  • Process shipments and returns, including incorrect or defective parts, ensuring vendor compliance.
  • Control supplies to minimize waste and maintain cost efficiency.
  • Allocate parts using CarMax systems for seamless workflow and accurate documentation.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service through clear communication and problem-solving.
  • Follow CarMax Environmental, Health and Safety (EH&S) requirements and maintain a clean and orderly work area.

Required Qualifications

  • Ability to read, interpret, and record data accurately for inventory and transactions.
  • Intermediate PC skills, including spreadsheet proficiency.
  • Strong collaboration skills to work effectively across departments.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
  • Physical capability to lift up to 50 lbs and work on your feet for extended periods.
  • Effective verbal communication skills for customer and team interactions.
  • Completion of CarMax-provided training in all parts processes.

About CarMax

At CarMax, we revolutionized the used car buying experience over 30 years ago by introducing transparency and integrity into the process. Our commitment to customer experience, innovation, and community has made us the nation’s largest used car retailer. With over 250 store locations and over 30,000 associates, we are proud to have been recognized as one of the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® and are committed to helping our communities thrive.

As an associate, you are part of an innovative movement to empower the modern customer and drive progress. Your work fuels change—sparking ideas, overcoming challenges, and shaping what’s next. Join us in creating a better future– for our company, our customers, and the communities we call home.

CarMax is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The hourly rate for this position is:

$17.00 - $27.20

Benefits:

Except as otherwise required by state law, CarMax Associates are entitled to the following paid sick, vacation, and holiday time.

Associates that are considered full-time hourly or commission/incentive eligible:

  • To earn up to 48 hours of sick time per year accrued on a per pay period basis and between 80 hours and 200 hours per year of vacation time after a 90 day waiting period depending on years of continuous service with the Company.
  • For 8 hours of pay for each of a total of 6 paid scheduled holidays per year plus 1 floating holiday. If such an Associate does work on a scheduled holiday due to business need, they are eligible for Holiday Premium Pay.

Associates considered full-time salaried are entitled to paid time away with no specified limit as needed for sick, vacation, bereavement, jury duty, holidays, floating holiday, etc. subject to manager approval.

For more details about benefits, please visit our CarMax Benefits website.

title: Manager, Physical Security Systems Operator - EPIC and Lab Security
description:
Who We Are


Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.


What We Offer


Salary:

$106,000.00 - $146,000.00

Location:

Santa Clara,CA

You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.

We are seeking a highly experienced and well-rounded Security Specialist to manage security projects, coordinate budget planning, prepare leadership presentations, and support security-related events across Applied Materials locations throughout California.

Applied Materials is growing at a pace that is driving significant increases in headcount and critical facilities. As a result, we expect over the next five years to have the most exciting and active R&D and manufacturing infrastructure pipeline in our history. The Global Security Operations (GSO) team is responsible for strategic development, risk oversight, and execution of security operations across all company locations. Supporting California Security Operations, this role will translate security priorities into coordinated project plans, financial forecasts, leadership materials, and organized stakeholder engagements statewide.

The Security Specialist is responsible for managing cross-functional security projects across California, including HQ and the EPIC Center. The role defines project scope, develops schedules, coordinates resources, tracks budgets and dependencies, and drives deliverables through completion and handoff to designated operational owners. Additional responsibilities include annual budget planning, spending forecasts, executive slide deck preparation, project governance, and coordination of security meetings, workshops, and events. This is a project-focused role and does not include daily security operations, guard force supervision, screening equipment operation, incident response, or investigations.

This is a new position based in the greater Sunnyvale/Santa Clara area. You will partner with local business unit leaders, Real Estate, Facilities, EHS, BCP, IT, Finance, Legal, Employee Relations, Procurement, vendors, and other stakeholders to align project requirements, funding needs, timelines, and deliverables. The role provides structured planning, financial analysis, presentation development, and event coordination to support California Security Operations leadership and statewide security initiatives.

This position reports to the Director, California Security Operations and is based in Santa Clara, CA. The role does not require travel.

Key Responsibilities

California-wide Security Operations Project Management

  • Manage Security Operations projects across California sites, from requirements gathering and planning through implementation, closeout, and transition to ongoing operations.
  • Develop project scopes, work plans, schedules, milestones, and responsibility assignments in partnership with site security leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Coordinate security technology implementation, facility readiness projects, process improvement initiatives, and cross-site standardization efforts, with operational execution retained by designated site teams.
  • Maintain project trackers, action logs, risk and issue registers, and dependency maps; escalate barriers and decisions to California Security Operations leadership.
  • Coordinate vendors, Procurement, Finance, Real Estate, Facilities, IT, EHS, and business partners to align deliverables, resources, implementation schedules, and operational requirements.
  • Track project costs against approved budgets, validate vendor deliverables, and coordinate scope or schedule changes through appropriate approvals.
  • Provide leadership with concise project status reports covering milestones, costs, risks, decisions, and next steps across the California project portfolio.
  • Coordinate readiness reviews, acceptance criteria, documentation, training, and operational handoffs; capture lessons learned and promote consistent practices across California sites.
  • Maintain an integrated California security project roadmap; support prioritization based on business needs, funding, resource availability, and dependencies, and facilitate documented scope and schedule change control.

Project Governance & Documentation

  • Develop and maintain project charters, requirements documents, responsibility matrices, implementation plans, and closeout records.
  • Develop dashboards and reporting tools to track milestones, deliverable completion, budget health, open risks, and stakeholder actions across the project portfolio.
  • Maintain version-controlled project records, decision logs, approval documentation, and consistent templates; track deliverable acceptance and lessons learned.

Vendor & Stakeholder Coordination

  • Coordinate project vendors and internal stakeholders on statements of work, proposals, deliverables, implementation dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
  • Facilitate project reviews, confirm milestone commitments, document decisions, and follow up on vendor and stakeholder actions.
  • Communicate professionally and effectively with client leadership, site management, and cross-functional partners.
  • Represent security project priorities in cross-functional planning forums and coordinate dependencies with facilities, research, technology, and business teams.

Presentations & Slide Deck Preparation

  • Prepare executive-ready PowerPoint slide decks for project reviews, budget proposals, quarterly business reviews, and California Security Operations leadership updates.
  • Translate project, financial, and security information into concise narratives, roadmaps, charts, dashboards, and clearly framed leadership decisions.
  • Gather stakeholder inputs, validate source data and financial figures, and maintain consistent messaging, formatting, and version control across presentation materials.
  • Develop executive summaries, briefing notes, talking points, and pre-read materials; coordinate reviews and incorporate leadership feedback before distribution.

Event, Workshop & Meeting Coordination

  • Plan and coordinate security workshops, leadership meetings, project kickoffs, stakeholder briefings, and security awareness events supporting California initiatives.
  • Develop event plans, agendas, schedules, invitations, attendee communications, and run-of-show documents; coordinate venues, audiovisual needs, materials, and vendor logistics.
  • Track event budgets and deadlines, coordinate presenters and rehearsals, and partner with designated site teams on visitor and access arrangements without assuming operational security duties.
  • Capture meeting decisions, action owners, and due dates; distribute follow-up materials, gather event feedback, and track commitments through completion.

Skills, Knowledge, Experience & Education

The ideal candidate will have the following:

  • 5+ years of experience in security project management, program coordination, or related project delivery, preferably in a laboratory, R&D, high-security, or technology environment.
  • Experience developing budgets, cost estimates, spending forecasts, variance analyses, and funding requests in partnership with Finance and Procurement.
  • Strong cross-functional project leadership skills, including facilitating meetings, negotiating priorities, and driving deliverables without direct supervisory authority.

Welcome to the future of banking. At Capital One, we believe your bank should be as mobile, intuitive, and human as the rest of your life. We are reimagining the way people interact with their money by creating community hubs where technology meets human empathy.


As a Branch Ambassador, you are the heartbeat of our space. You don't just "process transactions"—you embody our culture of outstanding hospitality. You are a relationship-builder who blends friendly, attentive service with cutting-edge digital innovation. Whether you’re helping a client navigate our latest tools or empowering them to reach their financial goals, you are the face of an exceptional, human-centric experience.


We are looking for curious, empathetic, and tech-savvy individuals who thrive in a fast-moving environment. You are someone who doesn't wait to be asked; you anticipate needs, solve problems before they arise, and have a genuine passion for helping people thrive in an evolving digital world.


What You’ll Actually Do

  • The Guardian of Trust & Accuracy You are the bedrock of our environment’s safety and integrity. You’ll execute high-volume cash transactions—including deposits, withdrawals, and complex negotiable instrument processing—with 100% accuracy. You maintain a "compliance-first" mindset, ensuring all security, audit, BSA/AML, and federal regulatory standards are met with precision to keep our customers' assets safe.

This isn't just a job—it’s work with a mission. title: Local Trial Manager - Sponsor Dedicated
description:
The IQVIA sponsor-dedicated Clinical Functional Service Partnerships (Clinical FSP) department is supporting our client’s project team in the execution of clinical trials. Joining the team provides the opportunity to work with one single client and to manage clinical research projects in different therapeutic areas.

We currently offer the exciting opportunity to join the FSP team as Local Trial Manager (full-time) in Czech Republic.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Services rendered will adhere to applicable company’s standard operating procedures (SOPs), work instructions, policies, codes of Good Clinical Practice (GCP), local regulatory requirements, etc.

  • Prepare or contribute to high level budget estimate in response to Request for Service’s followed by detailed budget proposal. Ensure overall contract management, including review and approval of external service provider (ESP) contracts, change orders and ensure services are delivered per contract.

  • Act as primary company contact for assigned trial at the country level and ensures local/country team is tracking project progress against planned timelines and monitors patient recruitment rate to ensure that target enrollment will be met across the allocated countries.

  • Drive study compliance by maintaining and updating trial management systems, using study tools and management reports available to analyze trial progress. Participates in preparation for and conduct of Health Authority (HA) inspections and internal Quality Assurance audits.

  • Contribute to site level recruitment strategy and contingency planning and implementation in partnership with other functional areas to achieve clinical research target.

  • Deliver competent vendor management at the country level to support the study and may submit requests for vendor services and support vendor selection.

  • Contribute to patient understanding of protocol and patient safety by contributing to the review of country specific informed consent in accordance with procedural document/templates.

  • Ensure trial subject safety in that all AEs/SAEs/PQCs are reported within the required reporting timelines and documented, as appropriate.

  • Ensure Inspection readiness by maintaining complete, accurate and timely data and essential documents in systems utilized for trial management (e.g. CTMS and VTMF) according to expectations (metrics) and archiving retention requirements where applicable.

  • With focus on quality, work closely with Global Trial Lead, Clinical Project Lead to ensure CAPA is implemented for audits/inspections or any quality related issues or concerns.

  • Ensure accurate finance reporting and trial delivered within budget by adhering to finance reporting deliverables and timelines. This includes forecasting and proactive management of country/local trial budget. If applicable, may assist in negotiation of trial site contracts and budgets.

  • Keep the trial in compliance with local regulatory requirements by organizing and ensuring IEC/HA approvals, if applicable.

  • May contribute as a mentor, champion, or representative of functional area in process initiatives, as required and if applicable.

Qualifications:

  • Master’s or higher-level degree in life science.

  • Minimum of 5 years of clinical research experience in the pharmaceutical industry or CRO plus 1-3 years of local clinical trial management experience.

  • Therapeutic area expertise in the field of Oncology or Hematology is preferred.

  • Strong working knowledge of applicable clinical research regulatory requirements, i.e., Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and International Conference on Harmonization (ICH) guidelines.

  • Fluent languages skills in Czech on at least C1 level and good command of English.

  • Strong IT skills in appropriate software and company systems.

  • Excellent decision-making and strong financial management skills.

  • Flexibility and ability to manage study teams in a virtual environment.

  • Willingness to travel occasionally for business meetings.

title: Project Design Lead
description:
Closing Date

2026-11-06

Job Title: Project Design Lead

Location: Hybrid working between Falmer (approximately 2 days pw) and home.

Contract Type: Permanent

Hours: 37 hours per week, Monday - Friday

Salary: Up to circa £55,000.

About the role

We’re looking for a Project Design Lead to join Southern Water, playing a key role in the technical assurance and delivery of engineering design across Wastewater projects.

You’ll lead and coordinate design activity from early needs identification and optioneering through to outline design, detailed design, construction and commissioning. A key part of the role will be making sure that the lowest whole-life cost solution is selected, without compromising on safety, quality, environmental outcomes or long-term operational performance.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced engineering professional who enjoys working in complex, regulated environments and wants to influence the delivery of major water and wastewater investment programmes at scale.

What you’ll be responsible for:

  • Providing authoritative technical input across the identification of needs, optioneering, design, construction and commissioning stages
  • Assuring the quality of design deliverables across multiple projects, ensuring designs are technically robust, compliant and fit for purpose
  • Leading in-house outline design and optioneering activity to support the selection of lowest whole-life cost, best-value solutions
  • Managing and coordinating multi-disciplinary design teams, including Southern Water colleagues, suppliers and delivery partners
  • Ensuring designs comply with Southern Water technical standards, health and safety requirements, environmental expectations and relevant regulations, including CDM
  • Holding yourself and others to account for strong health, safety and environmental behaviours throughout the design process
  • Driving consistency, rigour and efficiency across design delivery, including the use of standardisation, digital design concepts and best practice
  • Managing design scope, cost, quality, resources and change control across your projects
  • Preparing design plans, design cost estimates and monthly cost forecasts, working closely with Project Managers and Programme Design Managers
  • Working with Asset Strategy & Planning, Operations and delivery teams to develop practical solutions for emerging needs, operational incidents and business planning activity
  • Providing early warning of design risks, blockers, cost pressures or programme delays, and working with senior stakeholders to resolve them
  • Supporting continuous improvement by challenging existing standards and ways of working where better, safer or more efficient solutions are possible
  • Coaching and mentoring junior colleagues, helping create an environment where people feel able to challenge, innovate and learn
  • Ensuring customer, regulatory and environmental expectations are properly reflected in design decisions and delivery outcomes

What you’ll bring to the role:

Essential

  • Strong experience in an engineering design, design management or technical assurance role within a complex project delivery environment
  • Experience supporting or assuring design across infrastructure and/or non-infrastructure projects, ideally within the water, wastewater, utilities or wider regulated sector
  • Strong technical engineering judgement, with the ability to review, challenge and assure designs rather than simply produce them
  • Experience coordinating multi-disciplinary design teams, including internal teams, suppliers, contractors and delivery partners
  • Good understanding of project delivery, contract management, design governance and change control
  • Strong awareness of health and safety standards, environmental requirements and CDM regulations
  • Ability to assess technical options and support decisions based on safety, whole-life cost, deliverability, sustainability and operational performance
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain technical ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Good financial and commercial awareness, including the ability to monitor design costs, support budget decisions and understand value-based delivery
  • Confidence working with ambiguity, balancing competing priorities and making timely, well-reasoned decisions
  • A collaborative approach, with the ability to work effectively across project, programme, operations, asset strategy, supply chain and senior stakeholder groups
  • MEng, BEng, BSc, HND or HNC in an Engineering, Environmental or numerate science-related subject
  • Membership of an appropriate professional institute, either Chartered or working towards Chartership

Desirable

  • Experience working in the water or wastewater industry
  • Knowledge of water and wastewater regulations, including requirements linked to the DWI, Environment Agency, WINEP, WRMP or DWMP
  • Understanding of risk and value processes, procurement strategy and working with framework contractors
  • Experience using or promoting standardisation and digital design approaches
  • APM Project Professional Qualification
  • Managing Successful Programmes practitioner certification
  • NEC for Project Managers
  • Knowledge of Southern Water systems and procedures for the management of cost and programme

About Southern Water

Southern Water is at the forefront of transforming Britain’s water industry, investing significantly to enhance resilience, sustainability, and service excellence. With £7.8bn planned investment for 2025-30, this is an unparalleled opportunity to join a business committed to delivering a generational shift in the way water services are managed.

You will be joining at a time of significant change, working alongside a highly skilled leadership team with a clear vision for the future. We offer an environment where senior professionals can make a meaningful impact, influence major strategic decisions, and drive long-term value creation.

Our mission is to protect and enhance life through water and we need passionate people to help us achieve it. If you’re inspired by our purpose and believe you can contribute, apply today. You don’t need to meet every criterion; what matters most is your drive to make a difference.

If this role isn’t quite what you’re looking for but are keen to be contacted about opportunities at Southern Water, you can register your details here: Introduce Yourself (myworkdaysite.com- Introduce Yourself)

Our Commitment to Diversity

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. We do not discriminate based on race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, or any other protected characteristic. If you need reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know.

Additional information

In line with Southern Water’s security requirements, successful candidates will be required to provide evidence of their identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record check (DBS) and verification of their employment and/or education history for the past three years.

Appointment to this role is subject to the successful completion of all pre‑employment checks, including security vetting.

title: Calibration Technician II
description:
Join the Pharmaceutical Calibrations and Instrumentation (PCI) team! We are seeking a Calibration Technician II that can perform calibrations onsite at our client pharmaceutical facilities in South San Francisco, CA and other sites as needed. If you prefer working at a fast pace, "on the go" instead of at a desk, have a passion for performing quality work, and have a strong electronics or instrumentation background, this position may be just for you! Up to 50% travel is required based on project and client needs. At this time the role is minimal travel outside of the San Francisco area but could change in the future.

This position will focus on performing preventive maintenance, qualifications, relocations and calibrations on a variety of instruments such as electronics, temperature devices, pressure gauges, centrifuges, incubators, balances, and others as found in pharmaceutical manufacturing and laboratory environments.

The Calibration Technician reports directly to the Team Leader, Manager, or Director depending on the organizational structure. This is a full time, hourly position. Typical hiring range is $38-$44 per hour.


Expectations:

Calibration Technicians complete calibrations, qualifications, and PMs with accurate and timely GxP documentation, following PCI and/or client specific policies and procedures. They are expected to take a proactive role in supporting the Team and in providing client support and are expected to build a high level of trust with internal and client personnel. This trust is developed through consistently upholding PCI Values and demonstrating Honesty, Integrity, Pride, Accountability, Teamwork, and Commitment. the Tech II is expected to have a broader knowledge base of instrumentation and regulatory compliance. They will continue to train on new instrumentation areas and build an understanding of pharmaceutical and FDA requirements. Increased client interaction will occur and the Tech II will develop a deeper understanding of PCI’s services and how clients can expand the use of these services.


Responsibilities/Assignments include but are not limited to:

  • Completes calibrations, maintenance, qualifications, commissioning and troubleshooting/repairs in a safe, timely, and accurate manner, following PCI and client specific policies and proposals.
  • Works to understand client needs and requirements through effective communication and develops client relationships through excellent customer service.
  • Maintains a neat and professional PCI work area and projects a professional image at all times.
  • Is attune to potential new opportunities for PCI when at a client site or interacting with a client and relays this lead back to Leader/Manager.
  • With minor supervision, completes calibrations, qualifications, and PMs with accurate and timely GxP documentation, following PCI or client specific policies and procedures, and in a safe manner.
  • With guidance, able to perform flow, conductivity, pH, mass and dimensional calibrations.
  • Is attune to potential new opportunities for PCI when at a client site or interacting with a client and relays this lead back to Leader/Manager.
  • Completes timesheets with correct labor code charges (weekly) and assists other PCI Associates in proper coding of time and expenses.
  • Responsible for proper handling and maintenance of PCI and client equipment, including testing and standards equipment.
  • Learning to troubleshooting and perform repairs, but the majority of work will continue to be scheduled calibrations and maintenance events
  • Able to identify and report any safety issues at the work site, including educating peers on safety practices.

title: Control Room Operator
description:
Who we are

For more than 40 years, Reworld has been a leader in sustainable waste solutions, providing our customers with innovative solutions that help them achieve carbon-negative outcomes.

Our Vision

Reworld is leading the charge to a carbon-negative future through revolutionary sustainable materials management solutions that reduce, reuse, recycle and reimagine waste for the benefit of society and the environment.

Our Business

Reworld partners with businesses by offering cutting-edge engineering and innovative solutions, to help customers reduce, reuse, recycle and recover value from waste streams and meet or exceed their sustainability goals.

Our Value

Reworld's differentiator comes from our ecosystem of technology, facilities and partnerships, trusted by the world’s largest organizations to reimagine waste management for a smarter, more sustainable world.

All that we’re missing is you. Apply today!

About the role

The Control Room Operator leads and directs employees who, under the direction of the shift Supervisor, oversee and direct the operation of the facility. This position is responsible for monitoring the status of all plant systems on a continuous basis. Will respond to alarms by taking appropriate corrective actions and execute plant shut-down and start-up procedures and ensure that the plant meets it’s generating requirements while operating in a safe and environmentally efficient manner.

Position Responsibilities:

  • Ability to demonstrate how your actions support Reworld Values and Behaviors, including Safe and Inclusive Workplace, Delivering Results through Trust and Building Breakthrough Capabilities.

  • Maintains required logs and calculations; observes these logs for indications of faulty operation; notifies supervisor of abnormal system conditions.
  • Provide guidance to Crane, Auxiliary, and Back Plant Operators to maintain a safe and efficient operation
  • Effectively monitor Reworld operations systems and have strong working knowledge of boiler, turbine, and auxiliary equipment operations
  • Experienced in reading blueprints, P&ID’s, and schematic specifications
  • Manage critical events and prioritize tasks for completion at times during emergency, providing clear directions in operational, safety and environmental tasks
  • Respond to operational alarms, taking immediate corrective action
  • This position will be required to be in the field during outages.

Position Requirements & Qualifications:

title: Sr. Coordinator, AP Operations - Merch Pay
description:

CarMax, the way your career should be!

Job Title

Senior Coordinator, Accounts Payable - Operations

About this job

CarMax is seeking a Senior Coordinator in Accounts Payable at our Home Office in Richmond, Virginia. The Senior Coordinator position is responsible for supporting the team with general ledger management activities related to researching escalated or complex open items. With limited guidance, this role is responsible for the daily analysis of outstanding liabilities to determine the appropriate next steps. Daily, this position will need to blend both successful execution of their own deliverables as well as ensuring critical functions performed by other Accounts Payable team members and internal business partners are completed both accurately & timely. Additionally, this position is responsible for month-end accounting duties such as journal entries, account reconciliations, and business area specific reporting.

What you will do – Essential Responsibilities

  • Drive day-to-day procure to pay process execution including analyzing and resolving complex exceptions.
  • Provide the team with guidance on how to resolve outstanding liabilities. Help facilitate the resolution of complex variances and open items as well as identify root causes or trends that need to be addressed.
  • Perform weekly trend analysis as needed or requested by leveraging established key performance indicators (KPIs) to make recommendations to Accounting Leadership for workload balancing with respect to specific business areas/general ledger accounts.
  • Perform a variety of accounting functions, including recording expenses, reconciling general ledger accounts, and preparing journal vouchers monthly.
  • Adhere to state, federal, and local laws as well as various regulations, company policies and SOX Controls regarding account management as well as business area specific processes.
  • Communicate sensitive and complex information to customers, internal teams, and external partners.
  • Serve as a point-of-contact to resolve questions for internal customers including team members, other internal departments, CarMax store associates, as well as external partners.
  • Initiate process improvements based on root cause analysis to enhance and accelerate the funding and/or refund processes to mitigate compliance risk.
  • Represent the team as needed or requested to support cross-functional projects or initiatives. Communicate updates to the team and Accounting Leadership.

Qualifications and Requirements

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

· Engage with customers to actively understand needs and deliver on customer commitments.

· Proven self-starter capable of delivering exceptional results focus, problem solving skills and attention to detail with minimal direct supervision.

· Communicate complex messages both written and verbally to a wide variety of audiences both internal & external as well as through varying communication channels – e.g., phone, system update, email, and/or letter.

· Ability to provide “win-win” solutions while resolving escalated issues in a professional manner that is also timely and positive.

· Build and maintain relationships with internal and external business partners.

· Thinks logically, quickly as needed, applying past experiences and available resources, to form a thought process that is tailored to the situation; knowing when to partner with Accounting Leadership.

· Ability and willingness to adapt to change.

· Must be able to sit onsite, as requested, at CarMax’s Home Office in Richmond, Virginia.

Education and/or Experience

· High school diploma or equivalent required; Bachelor’s degree in business a plus

· 3+ years of business-related experience required, including 2+ years account reconciliation experience and managing accounts receivable or accounts payable highly preferred

· Strong accounting skills including general knowledge of generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) highly desirable

· Experience in Cloud ERP solutions (e.g., Oracle) a plus

· Intermediate level of Microsoft Excel required (e.g., Filtering, VLOOKUP, Subtotals, Shortcuts, Pivot tables)

· Proficient in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook required

About CarMax

CarMax disrupted the auto industry by delivering the honest, transparent, and high-integrity experience customers want and deserve. This innovative thinking around the way cars are bought and sold has helped us become the nation’s largest retailer of used cars, with over 200 locations nationwide.

Our amazing team of more than 25,000 associates work together to deliver iconic customer experiences. Along the way, we help every associate grow their career and achieve their best, at work and in their community. We are recognized for our commitment to training and diversity and are one of the FORTUNE 100 Best Companies to Work For®.

CarMax is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The annual salary for this position is:

$48,100.00 - $67,300.00

May be eligible for bonus and equity.

Associates that are considered full-time hourly or commission/incentive eligible:

title: Commerce Media Senior Strategist, Amazon Search
description:
Who we are:

Tinuiti is the largest independent full-funnel marketing agency in the U.S. across the media that matters most, with $4 billion in digital media under management and more than 1,200 employees. Built for marketers who demand growth and accountability, Tinuiti unites media and measurement under one roof to eliminate waste—the biggest growth killer of all—and scale what works. Its proprietary technology, Bliss Point by Tinuiti, reveals the truth around growth and waste, and how to capitalize on it. With expert teams across Commerce, Search, Social, TV & Audio, and more, Tinuiti delivers measurable results with brutal simplicity: Love Growth. Hate Waste.


We’d love to hear from you if:

Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other marginalized folks tend to only apply when they check every box. So if you think you qualify, but don't necessarily meet every single point on the job description, please still get in touch.


Overview:
As a Commerce Media Senior Strategist, you will lead the execution and optimization of sophisticated omnichannel marketing campaigns within the commerce media ecosystem. Leveraging your deep expertise, you will drive strategic insights and recommendations, ensuring exceptional client outcomes and advancing agency best practices.

Key Responsibilities

Client-Centric:

  • Build, drive, and optimize successful omnichannel marketing campaigns within your specialty and channel (e.g., DSP, Search on Amazon, Walmart, Criteo) to meet and exceed client goals, measured by campaign performance metrics such as conversion rates and ROI.
  • Foster strong working relationships with premier clients through effective communication across phone, email, and in-person interactions, aiming for a Client Satisfaction score of 9 or above and Client Retention of 95% or above.
  • Develop sophisticated omnichannel commerce media strategies tailored to each client’s unique goals and challenges, ensuring sustainable achievement of growth, retention, and profitability targets.
  • Tailor client-facing communication and presentations based on audience, client personality, and executive-level attendance, ensuring alignment with client’s holistic business objectives.

Product-Led:

  • Integrate Tinuiti’s product and technology suite into omnichannel strategies, focusing on scalability, growth, and efficiency, and measuring success through achievement of key client metrics and channel-specific success.
  • Demonstrate expert fluency in Tinuiti's product app suite by utilizing the tool suite in day-to-day work, answering complex questions using the app, providing strategic feedback and improvement recommendations, and leveraging the app as a primary method of client communications.

Data & Measurement Data-Driven:

  • Analyze complex cross-channel data and insights to interpret trends and make strategic recommendations, ensuring alignment with clients’ KPIs and the broader commerce media landscape.
  • Achieve Same Store Growth targets for clients you manage, using data analytics to drive decision-making and optimize campaign performance.

Channel Specific Expertise & The Tinuiti Way:

  • Maintain expert-level knowledge of a variety of commerce media platforms, proactively educating clients and account team members on program updates and benefits, and ensuring annual certifications are up to date.
  • Spearhead innovative thought leadership across the broader commerce media landscape, advancing agency best practices and contributing insights internally and externally.
  • Act as a holistic business account leader for your book of business, leading account team peers to drive accountability, cross-channel synergy, and streamlined execution in your areas of expertise.
  • Delegate effectively to more junior commerce team members to execute strategies.

Owner Mindset:

  • Proactively assess and diagnose omnichannel opportunities for improvement, implementing changes to achieve growth, retention, and profitability targets, tracked by performance metrics and client outcomes.
  • Contribute to a culture of continuous improvement by experimenting with new strategies and tools, measured by the implementation of innovative solutions and client feedback.
  • Effectively prioritize and manage time across clients, partner relationships, and internal initiatives, ensuring timely delivery of strategic objectives.
  • Take ownership of assigned accounts by proactively managing day-to-day operations, ensuring all deliverables are quality-checked, and consistently monitoring performance to confirm the account is running as intended.

Tinuiti Caliber

Beyond skills and experience, this is what we look for in every Tinuitian - the qualities that help people grow here, and help our clients and company grow with them.

  • Greatness Attracts Greatness: Craft is never finished here. Sharpen your read on what drives performance across DSP, Search, and retail media platforms, and put new tools and AI to work in how you plan and optimize.
  • Clients Grow, We Grow: Client needs are the truth we build from. Build strategies around what actually grows a brand's business on the platforms that matter to them, and turn campaign performance into a story that moves decisions forward.
  • Culture of Ownership: Ownership isn't a title, it's a daily choice. Own your accounts end to end, and stay invested in every dollar of client spend as if it were your own.
  • Future Fit: Our industry never stands still. Retail media platforms, formats, and measurement keep evolving, and AI is changing how we plan and optimize campaigns - staying ahead of that pace is what keeps our work sharp.

Professional & Technical Qualifications:

  • 7-10 years of experience in commerce media, paid commerce, or senior media planning roles with a proven track record of executing successful campaigns with monthly budgets of $500k+.
  • Experience with commerce media platforms such as Amazon, Walmart, Criteo, etc. preferred
  • Experience with Skai, Analytic Index, Pacvue, and Helium10 preferred.

The hiring salary range for this role is $120,000 - $140,000. We also offer an incentive pay program (RevShare) comprising a monthly variable revenue payment opportunity and a discretionary annual performance bonus. *This position is required 3 days hybrid in New York City.


Hiring salaries are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, parity with other team members, and alignment with market data. Please contact us to request accommodation.


Benefits:


Unlimited PTO: At Tinuiti, we believe you deserve time to rest, recharge, and enjoy life unplugged. When you prioritize time for yourself, you're able to bring your best self to work. That’s why we offer unlimited paid time off, a fully remote environment, and flexibility to take the time you need, when you need it. On top of that, we provide 20 paid holidays, including multiple long weekends, to ensure you have dedicated time to step away and disconnect. We're proud to offer above-industry standard work-life balance, consistently rated as one of the most loved benefits by Tinuitians year after year.

title: Sr Director, Card Risk: Credit & Data
description:
Sr Director, Card Risk: Credit & Data

As a Senior Director in Capital One’s Card Risk team, you will apply your leadership and analytical skills to our highest profile Risk Management efforts. You will act as a thought leader working across the business to develop and implement cutting edge Risk solutions to ensure Capital One’s continued success. Senior Directors in Capital One’s Card Risk organization partner with Executives, Line of Business, Compliance and Legal associates to develop and implement well-managed risk practices in an open, collaborative environment.

Senior Risk Directors at Capital One are highly motivated risk and process management professionals with excellent analytical, organizational, and communication skills. These skills allow the Senior Director to gain insights and act as a change agent to influence their business partners. As Capital One evolves to meet the ever-changing technology landscape, so do our risk managers. Being successful includes operating from a foundation of knowledge about the Line of Business with whom they are working, laws, regulations, processes and associated controls, and sound risk management practices. They are forward thinking, quick to adapt, and technologically adept.


This role leads the vertical risk management function for Card Data, Data Platforms and Credit Intent Governance, which includes overseeing credit policy controls, as well as risk advisory in the areas of data management, data products, and platform controls within the Card Data, Models, Decisioning, & Credit (DMDC) organization.


This role is designated as a hybrid position. You are expected to adhere to Capital One's hybrid policy regarding required on-site presence at your designated office location.


Responsibilities:

  • Utilize data management metrics and insights to influence senior business leaders in a compelling, action-oriented manner
  • Apply understanding of data governance processes and controls to proactively mitigate risks
  • Provide strategic program leadership and drive program alignment in a matrixed, highly complex regulated environment
  • Spearhead large scale Risk Management Program Management/Governance
  • Design, develop, and manage risk management-focused project plans in a complex dynamic environment, revising needs to meet changing requirements
  • Ensure projects are being delivered on time and on budget within a challenging environment while simultaneously managing risk
  • Communicate program requirements across the organization, to both internal and external stakeholders as needed
  • Partner cross-functionally with project customers to provide strategic and tactical thought partnership to effectively drive project delivery
  • Report out on program status, risks, issues and decisions to a wide variety of constituents across the company; flags critical risks and/or concerns to Risk Management and Business Leadership
  • Lead critical assessments on risk categories to mitigate risk to the company
  • Build relationships and collaborating with key stakeholders to ensure delivery of commitments
  • Consult strategically with Accountable Executives and partner teams
  • Problem-solve with cross-functional teams and partners on an array of issues and opportunities
  • Design and drive a transformation vision for your organization
  • Identify opportunities for continued improvement in the business
  • Partner proactively with partners’ teams, internal business teams, other risk office groups to help document and improve policies, processes, controls, and procedures

Senior Directors in this space are highly motivated professionals with excellent leadership, problem solving, communication and influence skills. They are experienced in operating in a highly dynamic environment and can balance the needs of multiple stakeholder groups. They have the ability to work with executives to create innovative solutions, and can think strategically, while executing on operational requirements.


Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or military experience
  • At least 8 years of experience in Risk Management, Project Management, Operations, Compliance, or Process Management
  • At least 8 years of people leadership experience
  • At least 7 years of experience supporting, partnering or interacting with internal business clients

title: Automotive Body Technician
description:
Service Center

Willow Glen

Every day, over 20,000 car accidents disrupt lives. When our customers face one, we step in to make things right — quickly, confidently, and with care.


At Caliber, fixing fenders has its benefits—like working with modern equipment, opportunities to create a career that works for you, and a center safety rating that helps make sure you get home to your family each night.


Are you the right fit?

If you find yourself nodding your head to the list below, Caliber might be right for you.

  • Experienced hands—At least two years of turning wrecks into road-ready rides. ​
  • Frame and structural know-how—If you can pull, straighten, and square it up, we want you. ​
  • No-shortcuts mentality—Blueprint it, fix it right the first time.​
  • Sharp eye for detail—You’re committed to tightened bolts, perfected welds, and no excuses. ​
  • Physically fit for the job—You can lift up to 50lbs.​
  • Team-first attitude—You collaborate with the painters, estimators, and front office staff in the business.​
  • Must be eligible to work in the U.S. with no restrictions

What’s in it for you?

We value your skills and reward you with solid benefits, performance-based earning potential, and opportunities to build a career that moves you forward.

  • Competitive pay—Unlimited work paired with a flag rate of up to $32–$35 paid weekly means your hard work is rewarded.​​
  • Career growth—Opportunities to create a career that works for you.​
  • Training that levels you up—I-CAR, ASE certifications—we invest in you. ​
  • Paid time off and holidays—Start accruing time off on day one and enjoy six company-wide holidays each year.​
  • Day-one benefits—Medical, dental, vision, 401k match—no waiting. ​
  • Best equipment and tech in the business—3M products, industry-leading gear.​

How will you spend your days?

No two crashes are identical, which means your days are filled with new challenges and interesting work.

  • Blueprint and execute—No guesswork, no shortcuts—just clean, precise repairs. ​
  • Full collision repair—From fender benders to frame rebuilds, you handle it all. ​
  • Panel and structural work—If it’s bent, twisted or torn, you bring it back to factory specs. ​
  • Quality reassembly—Fit and finish matter—your final touches make all the difference. ​
  • Work as a team—Trust and teamwork move cars through.​
  • Keep it clean—A pro always puts work location safety and tidiness first.

Accidents are our business. Being a great place to work? We do that on purpose. Apply today

title: Project Manager, EPC Power & Energy - ARB, Inc
description:
Job Overview:

ARB, Inc. is seeking an experienced Project Manager to lead the execution of large, complex EPC projects within the power generation and oil & gas sectors. The Project Manager is responsible for full lifecycle project execution and provides single-point accountability for safety, cost, schedule, quality, and contractual performance from project start-up through commissioning and project closeout.

The Project Manager would own the project, manage multi-disciplinary teams as well as coordinate engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning activities. The position interfaces directly with owners, subcontractors, vendors, and regulatory agencies, and ensures disciplined execution consistent with EPC best practices while aligning with corporate objectives, policies, and governance.

Key Responsibilities

  • Be the single point of accountability for overall project execution, outcomes, and client satisfaction.
  • Establish and maintain a strong safety culture where safety is the highest priority across all phases of execution.
  • Build, lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing, multi-disciplinary project team across engineering, construction, procurement, commissioning, and project controls.
  • Develop and manage strong, collaborative client relationships and act as the primary interface with customers and key stakeholders.
  • Lead upfront project planning, execution strategy development, and constructability reviews.
  • Ensure development, integration, and adherence to engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning schedules.
  • Own and manage all financial aspects of the project, including budgeting, cost forecasting, contingency management, cost control, and change control.
  • Administer and enforce the EPC contract and all related subcontracts and purchase orders.
  • Review engineering changes, field modifications, and design adjustments for cost, schedule, and contractual impacts.
  • Coordinate procurement of long-lead equipment, bulk materials, and specialty services to support execution and commissioning.
  • Proactively identify and resolve execution issues, evaluate alternatives, and drive timely, aligned decisions.
  • Ensure that commissioning, planning and readiness are integrated early and executed effectively through system turnover, testing, and final acceptance.
  • Communicate clearly and consistently with executive leadership regarding project status, risks, and opportunities.
  • Ensure compliance with corporate policies, procedures, regulatory requirements, and governance standards.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or a related technical discipline.
  • 10-15 years of progressive experience in engineering, construction, and project management within EPC delivery of power generation, energy infrastructure, or heavy industrial projects.
  • Extensive experience managing EPC projects through full lifecycle execution with direct responsibility for cost, schedule, safety, quality, and commercial performance.
  • Strong understanding of EPC contracting models, project controls, cost management, and schedule management.
  • Proficiency with Primavera P6, MS Project, and MS Office tools.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license preferred, but not required.
  • Master’s degree or MBA preferred, but not required.

Leadership Profile

  • Safety-driven, accountable, and decisive.
  • Commercially astute with a strong execution mindset.
  • Trusted to operate independently with limited oversight.
  • Effective in high-visibility, high-pressure environments.
  • Collaborative, pragmatic, and solutions-oriented.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary Range: $145,000 – $185,000 annually
  • Per Diem: Available if eligible
  • Competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), and paid time off

title: Sr Engineering Designer - Engine Team
location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
description:
Job Description

This role is categorized as hybrid. The selected candidate will be expected to work on-site at the Warren Tech Center at least three days per week, or as otherwise determined by the hiring leader.

  • This role is not eligible for relocation assistance.

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.


Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale."

About the Role:

General Motors is seeking an Engineering Designer to develop integrated, high-quality, manufacturable designs for the Engine space. In this role, you will help translate vehicle, propulsion, structural, manufacturing, and program requirements into robust virtual designs that support performance, safety, durability, serviceability, and production readiness.


The role is focused on complete Engine systems. You will own or support Siemens NX math models, design criteria, typical sections, clearance studies, subsystem integration, NX Analysis, material and mass data, design reviews, and on-time math releases.

You will work closely with the Design Manager, Design Lead Team, Design Release Engineer, fellow designers, engineering partners, manufacturing, joining, quality, suppliers, plant, program, and service teams to identify risks early, resolve integration issues, and deliver release-quality data through the Global Vehicle Development Process.


What you will do:

  • Develop and maintain robust, accurate, and production-oriented Siemens NX parametric models for assigned components and subsystems.
  • Create virtual vehicle integration solutions aligned with program requirements, design principles, packaging constraints, design criteria, and subsystem interfaces.
  • Develop and refine NX criteria and typical sections using approved modeling methods and program standards.
  • Establish and control hard points, packaging zones, clearances, service access, and critical interfaces.
  • Apply structural design fundamentals, including stiffness, strength, fatigue, buckling, section efficiency, joints, materials, reinforcements, and local load introduction.
  • Evaluate primary and secondary load paths for durability, crash, support, and propulsion-related conditions.
  • Identify load introduction points, reactions, joints, discontinuities, weak links, and opportunities for efficient structural improvement.
  • Perform or support clearance, usage, configuration, and virtual studies across components, subsystems, and the complete vehicle.
  • Complete NX Analysis for assigned components or subsystems and use results appropriately to guide design decisions with support from Design Lead Team or senior designers as needed.
  • Apply GD&T, tolerance awareness, variation-management, and stack-up principles to support fit, function, joining, load transfer, and assembly.
  • Design for manufacturability and assembly from the beginning of the design process, considering process capability, tooling, fixturing, access, sequence, joining, weldability, inspection, repairability, and production variation.
  • Maintain accurate and traceable material, mass, specification, and related data within the math file.
  • Translate program and component requirements into clear design criteria, integration checks, verification expectations, and release deliverables.
  • Plan and execute work against design sync points, review milestones, release timing, and other Global Vehicle Development Process deliverables.
  • Deliver accurate, complete, and on-time math releases with clean CAD, correct interfaces, complete details, and minimal rework.
  • Use structured problem solving to resolve non-routine and moderately complex virtual integration issues.
  • Communicate design intent, load paths, integration risks, timing, decisions, and technical concerns clearly and proactively.
  • Track actions and issues through integration, analysis, reviews, release, build, validation, and verified closure.
  • Seek input early, support fellow designers, collaborate across functions, and share lessons learned and effective design practices.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of modeling methods, design reviews, checks, templates, workflows, and data quality.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, engineering technology, or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent experience.
  • Two to five years of experience in automotive or mechanical CAD, engineering design, or a related product-development environment.
  • Demonstrated experience using Siemens NX for parametric modeling, model organization, design intent, references, constraints, and model-quality practices.
  • Understanding of automotive or mechanical structural design and the ability to reason about load paths, stiffness, strength, joints, reinforcements, materials, and interfaces.
  • Experience with virtual integration, packaging, clearance studies, configurations, usage validation, or comparable design-integration activities.
  • Working knowledge of GD&T, tolerance concepts, and variation management.
  • Working knowledge of design for manufacturability and design for assembly.
  • Ability to interpret requirements, identify ambiguity or conflict, and maintain traceability from requirements through design, review, analysis, release, and issue closure.
  • Ability to complete assigned work accurately and on schedule while managing multiple interfaces and program commitments.
  • Strong technical communication, problem-solving, collaboration, ownership, and follow-through skills.
  • Willingness and ability to work onsite at the Warren Tech Center at least three days per week—Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday—or at another frequency determined by the manager.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience designing structural sheet-metal components, including stamping, forming, draw direction, flanges, hemming or joining interfaces, local reinforcements, spring back, and process capability.
  • Knowledge of casting processes, including draft, wall thickness, ribs, fillets, porosity risk, machining, datum strategy, and process limitations.
  • Experience with Electrical Routings and/or fluid structures.
  • Advanced Siemens NX experience, including complex surfacing, expressions, templates, checks, reusable modeling practices, or workflow improvement.
  • Broader NX Analysis experience and the ability to connect analysis results to design changes, performance, and risk.
  • Experience with joining strategies and the relationship between joint design, load transfer, durability, process capability, and production performance.
  • Experience with DFMEA, tolerance analysis, durability thinking, design optimization, or failure-mode anticipation.
  • Experience leading configuration or design changes across load paths, interfaces, tooling, joining, validation, and released data.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence technical decisions without formal authority through facts, alternatives, and practical recommendations.
  • Experience coaching or developing less-experienced designers in NX modeling, virtual integration, load-path reasoning, DFM/DFA, or review discipline.
  • Master’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline.
