title: Consultant, Services de conseil et d’analyse / Consultant, Consulting & Analytics Services
description:
IQVIA est le leader mondial de la fourniture de données sanitaires et pharmaceutiques au secteur des soins de santé. Notre équipe de services de conseil et d’analyse est réputée pour offrir à ses clients une perspective commerciale approfondie.

IQVIA propose une gamme de services pour aider les entreprises des sciences de la vie à planifier et à ajuster leurs modèles commerciaux et leurs équipes afin de maximiser leur impact. L’équipe de services de conseil et d’analyse utilise les données d’IQVIA, des sources primaires de renseignements et les données de ses clients pour développer des modèles analytiques robustes qui sont à l’origine de toutes les recommandations et les découvertes d’IQVIA.


Chez IQVIA, vous connaîtrez tous les éléments qui suivent :

  • Accès à une richesse d’expériences mondiales, de ressources et de données de santé sur lesquelles s’appuyer pour créer des solutions innovantes.
  • Des collègues motivés et perspicaces issus d’horizons divers dans tous les aspects des industries pharmaceutiques et de la santé.
  • Propriété et responsabilité de la fourniture d’analyses de produits, d’entreprises et de marchés aux clients axés sur le Canada qui façonneront des recommandations à nos clients pharmaceutiques multinationaux et à d’autres intervenants des soins de santé.
  • Un environnement d’apprentissage, avec un accès structuré à des experts mondiaux et des leaders dans les méthodes analytiques conçues pour les sciences de la vie.
  • Un environnement entrepreneurial offrant d’importantes occasions d’avancement.
  • Un environnement favorable et convivial axé sur la réussite des clients, des entreprises et des individus.


Vue d’ensemble du poste

En étroite collaboration avec les consultants seniors, les directeurs associés et les directeurs, vous serez chargé de fournir des données analytiques de haute qualité et dans les délais aux projets des clients dans le domaine des sciences de la vie. Les missions vont de l’analyse quantitative tactique et de la résolution de problèmes à l’aide au développement de solutions stratégiques complexes. Les consultants peuvent servir de chefs de projet pour de petites équipes ou des flux de travail.


Responsabilités principales

  • Aider à l’examen et à l’analyse des exigences ou des problèmes des clients et aider à l’élaboration de propositions et de solutions pour les clients.
  • Aider à l’élaboration d’une documentation et de spécifications détaillées.
  • Effectuer des analyses quantitatives ou qualitatives substantielles pour aider à l’identification des problèmes des clients et au développement de solutions de conseil en analyse avancée.
  • Aider à la conception/structuration et à la réalisation de présentations adaptées aux caractéristiques ou aux besoins du public.
  • Développer et présenter, au besoin, des livrables client complets dans des cadres et méthodologies connus/identifiés.
  • Développer de manière proactive une connaissance de base des méthodologies de conseil et du marché des sciences de la vie grâce à la prestation de missions de conseil et à la participation à des occasions d’apprentissage formelles et informelles.
  • Les responsabilités basées sur l’engagement sont attribuées et gérées par des consultants seniors, des directeurs associés ou des directeurs.
  • Prendre en charge (ownership) des analyses ou des volets de livrables clairement définis, en assurant la rigueur analytique, l’exactitude et le respect des échéanciers.
  • Communiquer les résultats (oralement et par écrit) de façon claire et structurée; adapter la narration (« storyline ») à l’auditoire.
  • Participer à des interactions clients (p. ex., appels, ateliers) pour clarifier les besoins, tester des hypothèses et expliquer les méthodes, avec soutien de l’équipe senior.
  • Travailler efficacement avec des ensembles de données IQVIA et/ou clients : préparation, manipulation, validation, visualisation et interprétation (Excel, Power BI et/ou outils statistiques/de programmation).
  • Être à l’aise dans des contextes ambigus : poser de bonnes questions, proposer des options, documenter les hypothèses et gérer plusieurs priorités simultanément.
  • Contribuer à des initiatives internes (p. ex., amélioration d’outils/actifs, partage de connaissances, soutien à des activités d’équipe), en lien avec votre niveau.

Qualités requises

  • Baccalauréat requis.
  • 3 à 5 ans d’expérience connexe requis.
  • PowerBI, R, Python ou expérience avec d’autres outils d’analyse, un atout.
  • Expérience avec la suite Microsoft (Excel, PowerPoint) requise, maîtrise avancée souhaitée.
  • Volonté de travailler efficacement avec d’autres personnes au sein de l’organisation pour atteindre les objectifs de l’équipe.
  • Excellentes compétences en communication (synthèse, storytelling, vulgarisation) et aisance à présenter/échanger avec des clients.
  • Aisance à travailler avec des données imparfaites/incomplètes et à documenter des hypothèses; rigueur et souci du détail.
  • Connaissance et compréhension des processus fondamentaux de l’entreprise, de leur interaction et de l’impact des influences externes/internes sur la prise de décision, la croissance et le déclin.
  • Connaissance des méthodes, outils et techniques de conseil liés à son domaine fonctionnel.
  • Compétences efficaces en gestion du temps requises.
  • Capacité démontrée à gérer plusieurs priorités simultanément et à naviguer dans l’ambiguïté.
  • Connaissance du système de santé canadien (accès au marché, remboursement, etc.) : un atout.


Ce à quoi ressemble le succès au cours de la première année (exemples)

  • Livraison / Qualité : produire des analyses exactes, reproductibles et bien documentées; livrables soignés (Excel/PowerPoint/Power BI) nécessitant peu de retouches.
  • Rigueur analytique : démontrer une démarche structurée (hypothèses claires, validation des données, contrôles de qualité, interprétation prudente).
  • Autonomie progressive : prendre en charge des modules d’analyse ou des volets de livrables; gérer ses tâches et échéanciers de manière fiable; escalader les risques tôt.
  • Communication & collaboration : contribuer en réunion (interne et, progressivement, client), expliquer clairement les approches et résultats, intégrer efficacement les retours.
  • Gestion des priorités : performer sur 2+ mandats en parallèle en maintenant qualité et délais; être à l’aise avec des demandes évolutives.
  • Connaissance métier : développer une compréhension pratique des enjeux des sciences de la vie au Canada (commercialisation, accès, remboursement — selon les mandats).
  • Contribution interne : contribuer à au moins une initiative d’équipe (actif réutilisable, amélioration d’un modèle/outil, partage de connaissances, soutien à une proposition, etc.).

Vous devrez travailler directement avec des départements, des équipes, des fonctions de support et des parties prenantes d'IQVIA situés partout au Canada et à travers le monde, par conséquent, une connaissance fonctionnelle de l'anglais, tant à l'écrit qu'à l'oral, est nécessaire à l'exercice des fonctions de ce poste.

Comme nos équipes de recrutement sont mondiales, veuillez soumettre votre CV en anglais et en français.



IQVIA is the world leader in the provision of health and pharmaceutical data to the health care sector. Our Consulting and Analytics (C&A) team is renowned for providing deep business-focused insights for our customers.

IQVIA delivers a suite of services to help life sciences companies plan and adjust their commercial models and teams to maximize impact. The C&A team leverages IQVIA data, primary intelligence, and customer-owned data to develop robust analytical models that underpin our recommendations and findings.


At IQVIA C&A you will experience:

  • Access to a wealth of global experience, resources, and healthcare data from which to draw on to build innovative solutions.
  • Motivated, insightful colleagues with diverse backgrounds in all aspects of the pharmaceutical and healthcare industries.
  • Ownership and responsibility for delivering product, company and market analyses to Canadian-focused client stakeholders that will shape recommendations to our multinational pharmaceutical clients and other healthcare stakeholders.
  • A learning environment, with structured access to global experts and leaders in analytic methods designed for life sciences.
  • An entrepreneurial environment providing significant growth opportunities.
  • A supportive and friendly environment focused on client, business, and individual success.


Job Overview

Working closely with Senior Consultants, Associate Principals and Principals, you will be responsible for providing high quality, on-time analytical input to client projects in the life sciences field. Assignments range from tactical quantitative analysis and problem solving to assisting in the development complex strategic solutions. Consultants may serve as project managers for small teams or work streams.


Essential Functions

  • Assists with the review and analysis of client requirements or problems and assists in the development of proposals and client solutions.
  • Assists in the development of detailed documentation and specifications.
  • Performs substantial quantitative or qualitative analyses to assist in the identification of client issues and the development of advanced analytics advisory solutions.
  • Assists in the design/structure and completion of presentations that are appropriate to the characteristics or needs of the audience.
  • Develops, and may present, complete client deliverables within known/identified frameworks and methodologies.
  • Proactively develops a basic knowledge of consulting methodologies and the life sciences market through the delivery of consulting engagements and participation in formal and informal learning opportunities.
  • Engagement based responsibilities are assigned and managed by Senior Consultants, Associate Principals or Principals.
  • Own defined analyses and/or workstreams, ensuring analytical rigor, accuracy, and on-time delivery.
  • Communicate findings clearly in both written and verbal formats; tailor storyline and materials to the audience.
  • Interact directly with client stakeholders (e.g., calls, working sessions) to clarify requirements, test assumptions, and explain methods under senior guidance.
  • Work hands-on with IQVIA and/or client datasets: preparation, manipulation, validation, visualization, and interpretation (Excel, Power BI and/or statistical/programming tools).
  • Operate effectively in ambiguity by asking the right questions, proposing options, documenting assumptions, and managing multiple priorities.
  • Contribute to internal initiatives (e.g., knowledge assets, tools, best practices, team activities) as appropriate for level.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree required.
  • 3-5 years of related experience required.
  • PowerBI, R, Python or experience with other analytics tools preferred.
  • MS Suite experience (Excel, PowerPoint) required, advanced proficiency preferred.
  • Works willingly and effectively with others in and across the organization to accomplish team goals.
  • Strong communication skills (synthesis, storytelling, translating analyses for non-technical audiences) and comfort presenting/discussing with clients.
  • Comfort working with imperfect/incomplete data; strong attention to detail and documentation of assumptions.
  • Knowledge and understanding of the fundamental processes of business, their interaction, and the impact of external/internal influences on decision making, growth and decline.
  • Knowledge of consulting methods, tools, and techniques, related to one’s functional area.
  • Effective time management skills required.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and operate effectively in ambiguity.
  • Exposure to or interest in the Canadian healthcare system (market access, reimbursement, public/private dynamics) is an asset.

What success looks like in Year 1 (examples)

  • Delivery / Quality: produce accurate, reproducible, well-documented analyses; polished outputs (Excel/PowerPoint/Power BI) requiring minimal rework.
  • Analytical rigor: demonstrate structured problem-solving (clear assumptions, data validation, QA checks, careful interpretation).
  • Growing ownership: own defined analysis modules/workstreams; manage tasks and timelines reliably; flag risks early.
  • Communication & collaboration: contribute effectively in internal (and gradually client) discussions; explain approaches and findings clearly; incorporate feedback quickly.
  • Prioritization: succeed across 2+ concurrent engagements while maintaining quality and deadlines; remain effective as requirements evolve.
  • Business context: build practical understanding of Canadian life sciences topics relevant to projects (commercial strategy, market access, reimbursement, etc.).
  • Internal contribution: contribute to at least one internal initiative (reusable asset, model/tool improvement, knowledge share, proposal support, etc.).

You will be required to work directly with IQVIA departments, teams, support functions and stakeholders located across Canada and around the world therefore, a functional knowledge of English, both written and spoken, is necessary to perform the duties of this position.

title: Software Engineering Group Manager
description:
Job Description Summary:

Digital products play a central role in how we create value for customers, support the teams who serve them, and shape the consumer experience.

Our Product and Engineering organizations bring together small, empowered teams that move with clarity, speed, and purpose, enabling digital to be a meaningful source of advantage across Coca-Cola’s North America Operating Unit.

Our work spans customer journeys, service delivery, sales workflows, and the platforms that connect them. We are raising our standards for product craft and rebuilding the systems behind these experiences.

As a Software Engineering Group Manager, you will lead multiple engineers across full stack, front end, and back-end disciplines to deliver customer-facing and internal products in a product operating model. You will partner closely with Product, Design, Data, and Architecture to shape strategy, build durable platforms, and deliver measurable outcomes.

This role is for leaders who can grow strong teams, raise engineering standards, and guide technical direction - while staying close enough to the work to make sound architectural and delivery decisions.

What You Will Work On

At Coca-Cola, engineers have the opportunity to build products at meaningful scale—shaping the digital experiences, platforms, and intelligent systems that power how we serve customers, enable field teams and partners, support sales, and drive transaction growth across one of the world’s most recognized brands. Depending on the team, you could work on connected service tools that improve resolution speed and reliability, data and API platforms that unlock growth and decisioning, customer and operational experiences that reduce friction across workflows, or sales products that equip teams with better visibility, insights, and execution capabilities. This is a chance to join at a pivotal moment: helping define modern engineering practices, influence product direction, and build high-impact solutions in empowered, cross-functional teams where your work directly connects to business performance and customer outcomes

How We Work

You’ll be part of a dedicated, cross-functional team (Product, Design, Engineering) that is:

  • Empowered to solve problems, not just build features

  • Accountable for outcomes, not output

  • Collaborative by default, from discovery through delivery

  • Continuously learning, using data and customer insight to improve

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage and coach a group of full stack, front end, and back-end engineers through technical leadership and professional development

  • Play a key role in building out your Software Engineering Team;

  • Bring a strong technical perspective to help the team identify what is feasible, what is valuable, and what is worth building

  • Challenge assumptions and propose alternative solutions that are simpler, faster, or more impactful

  • Partner with Product Management and Design to frame problems, define outcomes, and translate strategy into an executable roadmap

  • Align cross-team dependencies and coordinate delivery across multiple services and applications

  • Communicate status, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to stakeholders; make decisions that optimize for customer and business impact

  • Make pragmatic tradeoffs between speed, scalability, maintainability, and cost

  • Ensure alignment with broader platform and enterprise architecture where appropriate

  • Guide architecture and technical direction across front end, back end, and platform capabilities; ensure solutions are scalable, secure, and maintainable

  • Partner with Data Engineering and Data Analytics to enable reliable data products, feature pipelines, and ML-powered experiences where they create measurable value

  • Establish engineering standards for APIs, UI architecture, data contracts, and eventing; ensure alignment with enterprise and platform architecture

  • Own technical risk management (security, privacy, resiliency, cost); surface tradeoffs and investment needs early

  • Ensure strong engineering practices, including testing, observability, and CI/CD

  • Maintain a high bar for code quality and system design through reviews and hands-on contribution

  • Drive continuous improvement of the product through iteration, feedback, and learning

  • Establish reliability targets (SLOs/SLAs where applicable) and drive continuous improvement in performance, availability, and cost efficiency

  • Balance short-term delivery with long-term product and technical health, including planned reduction of technical debt

  • Ensure the team is focused on delivering meaningful impact, not just completing work

  • Create clarity on ownership boundaries, decision rights, and interfaces between teams to enable autonomy with alignment

Contribute to a Strong Engineering Culture

  • People leadership: Proven experience managing and growing software engineers across levels and specialties in collaboration with Product, Design and Data leadership

  • Full stack fluency: Comfort guiding modern front end and back-end architectures, APIs, and integration patterns

  • Product operating model mindset: Outcome-oriented, customer-centered, and skilled at partnering with Product and Design

  • Data & ML experience: Experience delivering data engineering and machine-learning-enabled solutions in production

  • Technical judgment: Makes smart tradeoffs, avoids over-engineering, and manages risk proactively

  • Product mindset: Cares about users, outcomes, and why things are built

  • Technical judgment: Makes smart tradeoffs, avoids over-engineering

  • Ownership & leadership: Takes initiative and influences decisions

  • Collaboration: Works effectively with product managers and designers

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience, including building and shipping production-grade applications

  • 3+ years of people management experience leading software engineers (ideally across full stack, front end, and back end)

  • Experience setting technical direction across services, web/mobile UIs, and cloud platforms; comfortable reviewing architecture and design

  • Experience partnering with Product and Design in a product operating model (continuous discovery and delivery; outcome-based roadmaps)

  • Working knowledge of data engineering and ML delivery patterns (pipelines, feature stores/serving, model lifecycle, monitoring)

  • Experience building and shipping production-grade applications

  • Proficiency in modern programming languages and frameworks (frontend and backend)

  • Experience working with APIs, distributed systems, and cloud environments

  • Experience leading multiple teams or a larger engineering group with shared services and cross-team dependencies

  • Experience building internal platforms or reusable components that accelerate delivery across product teams

  • Experience with modern cloud and data stacks (e.g., container platforms, event streaming, data warehouses/lakehouses)

  • Experience operationalizing ML (MLOps, model monitoring, responsible AI practices, experimentation)

  • Strong stakeholder management skills across technology, product, and business partners

  • Experience contributing to product discovery or solution design, not just delivery

  • Track record of technical leadership within a team (formal or informal)

  • Experience building customer-facing products

  • Familiarity with modern engineering practices (CI/CD, testing, observability)

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field

  • Equivalent practical experience is equally valued

Who Thrives Here

Engineers who:

  • Are curious about customers and how products create value

  • Enjoy collaborating and debating ideas across disciplines

  • Take pride in both what they build and why it matters

Who This Role Is Not For

This role may not be the right fit if you:

  • Prefer working from detailed requirements with limited ambiguity

  • Want to focus primarily on coding without engaging in product decisions

  • Are most comfortable in highly structured, delivery-driven environments

The Coca-Cola Company will not offer sponsorship for employment status (including, but not limited to, H1-B visa status and other employment-based nonimmigrant visas) for this position. Accordingly, all applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and must not require The Coca-Cola Company's sponsorship to continue to work legally in the United States.

Skills:

title: Winter Environmental Educator
description:
SUMMARY

Bogus Basin’s Environmental Education program is seeking an energetic and knowledgeable field instructor to teach snow science and winter ecology to school field trip groups during the winter season. This position will report to the Environmental Education Supervisor. As a Winter Environmental Educator, you’ll lead students on snowshoes through the Boise National Forest while engaging them in hands-on environmental education activities such as digging snow pits and analyzing snow crystals. The goal of this program is to connect students to the natural world and winter environment that surrounds them. We hope to foster the next generation of ecologists, land managers, environmental stewards, and more, who will stand for access and preservation of our public lands and the world around them. The Environmental Educator will be trained to lead students through educational activities, mentored on how to provide positive learning experiences for children in a field trip setting, encouraged to create activities of their own interest that fit into our curriculum, and expected to positively redirect students’ behavior when necessary. Winter Environmental Educators will support our adult programming by creating and leading at least one guided nature program on a theme of their choice for the general public.


The team will be working towards these goals:


1. Connect People to Land Through Outdoor Experiences
We aim to foster a personal and lasting connection to the natural world by offering hands-on, place-based education programs that encourage curiosity, observation, and stewardship.

2. Provide Accessible, Affordable, and Inclusive Environmental Education
We are committed to reducing barriers to participation in environmental education by keeping programs affordable, accessible to diverse communities, and welcoming to people of all ages and backgrounds. Our volunteers help us extend our reach and reflect the diversity of our community, making programs more personal, welcoming, and supported.

3. Empower the Next Generation of Environmental Stewards
Our core programming serves youth ages 9–14 through camps, field trips, and school partnerships, helping them build knowledge, confidence, and a love for the outdoors.

4. Expand Meaningful Learning Opportunities for Teens and Adults
We will broaden our impact by creating more teen and adult programs, including thematic tours, workshops, and immersive experiences that support lifelong learning.

5. Educate for Climate Action and Environmental Awareness
We integrate climate education into our programming to deepen understanding of local impacts, inspire hope through solutions, and encourage responsible decision-making.


Transportation: Transportation is provided up and down the mountain from the Harrison Hollow parking lot 2600 N Harrison Hollow Ln, Boise, ID 83702.


Duration: This is a full-time seasonal position. 30 hours a week Monday-Friday.

Winter Orientation is on November 14th. Training is December 14th-16th.

The season will take place between January 4th and April 9th.

MLK Day (January 18th) and Presidents Day (February 15th) will be off.

Spring Break STEM Camp March 15th – 19th (40 hours).

Field trips typically run from 10am – 2pm with the Winter Environmental Educator work hours running from around 9:15am – 3:15pm. Daily commitment hours being 8:30am – 4pm with transportation up and down the mountain included.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE JOB

· Teach snow science, hydrology, and winter ecology to students (grades 3–12) and community members.

· Lead snowshoe-based explorations, guiding students through field activities and scientific investigations.

· Coordinate day-of logistics with instructors, interns, teachers, and volunteers.

· Connect participants from diverse backgrounds with Bogus Basin’s SnowSchool curriculum.

· Maintain snowshoe trails, signage, igloos, and program equipment.

· Assist the Sustainability Team with recycling, trail maintenance, and other tasks.

· Ensure a safe learning environment for all participants.

· Positively redirect misbehavior when necessary.

· Maintain a professional attitude toward all students, staff, supervisors, and other departments.


NON-ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE JOB

  • Collect program payments when needed.
  • Assist with volunteer coordination and communication.
  • Support participant data collection and reporting.
  • Clear and shovel snow a required.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

title: Manager, Wind Engineering
description:
The Manager, Project Engineering (Onshore Wind) will support Vena Energy's regional wind farm engineering and design activities from early-stage screening through pre-construction development. The role is accountable for delivering optimized project designs that maximize project value and minimize Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) across Vena's onshore wind portfolio.


The position will manage a multidisciplinary engineering team based in Bangalore and provide technical leadership across wind resource assessment, energy yield analysis, site suitability assessments, wind farm design optimization, concept engineering, project feasibility studies, and CAPEX/OPEX estimation.


The successful candidate will drive the internalization of key engineering capabilities, standardization of engineering methodologies, development of digital engineering tools, and implementation of best practices across Vena's wind development portfolio. The role will additionally be responsible for overseeing Vena Energy's regional wind measurement portfolio, ensuring effective monitoring of meteorological masts and LiDAR campaigns through the VeMeMos platform and providing high-quality wind resource data to support project development, site suitability assessments, and energy yield analyses.

In addition to supporting Vena Energy's internal development portfolio, the Manager will support in developing and growing an external engineering consulting and advisory business. The role will leverage Vena's expertise in wind resource assessment, energy analytics, LCOE optimization, site suitability, concept engineering, operational performance analysis, and VeMeMos-based wind measurement monitoring to provide value-added technical services to external clients across the renewable energy sector.

Are you ready to engineer a greener future?

title: Principal Medical Writer - FSP (M/W/D)
description:
Principal Medical Writer is responsible for the development of clinical documents for submissions to regulatory authorities globally. Provides strategic direction to cross-functional project teams with minimal oversight to ensure that clinical documents (eg, Investigators' Brochures [IBs], Clinical Study Reports [CSRs], and marketing authorization submission documents) accurately and consistently present key data-driven clinical messages in accordance with program goals and regulatory requirements. Writes or provides direction and leadership to other writers to ensure the timely delivery of high quality documents that are scientifically rigorous, logically organized, and have accurate data presentation and interpretation. Oversees the medical writing activities of multiple compounds and serves as lead writer for individual summary documents. Has a broad understanding of clinical research processes and global regulatory document standards.

Essential Functions


Develop regulatory documents for submission to regulatory agencies globally, in accordance with ICH and other global guidelines, standards and processes, and client's authoring standards, as applicable, in adherence with study/project timelines and corporate objectives.

 Manage medical writing projects, including developing timelines (working with the study/project teams, as necessary) and communication with cross-functional team members to maintain awareness of review cycles and expectations.

 Participate in cross-functional meetings to provide input regarding medical writing deliverables, timelines, and any process(es) needed for the completion of regulatory documents.

 Review other documents associated with the assigned project(s) (eg, Protocols and Statistical Analysis Plans), as appropriate.

 Participate in cross-functional process improvement initiatives.

 Participate in defining and writing standard operating procedures and best practices for an efficient preparation of quality documents.

 Manage internal and contract medical writing resources as required to ensure timely completion of assigned projects.

Qualifications


Bachelor's degree required. Advanced degree in a relevant scientific/clinical/regulatory field preferred.

 At least 5 years of medical writing experience in the biopharmaceutical/CRO industry required or comparable experience within clinical or preclinical development.

 Proficiency in organizing and communicating clinical information required with minimal oversight.

 Strong organizational, time management, and project management skills are required.

 Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills needed to work effectively in a team environment.

 Proficient understanding and knowledge of global regulatory requirements needed and knowledge of therapeutic areas in all phases of clinical development desired.

IQVIA is a leading global provider of clinical research services, commercial insights and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences and healthcare industries. We create intelligent connections to accelerate the development and commercialization of innovative medical treatments to help improve patient outcomes and population health worldwide. Learn more at

All information and credentials submitted in your application must be truthful and complete. We appreciate your honesty and professionalism.

title: Helper
description:

Working alongside a driver, you will be responsible for collecting solid waste and recyclable materials from residential and commercial routes, operating truck compaction equipment, and ensuring strict adherence to safety standards.


What We Offer

  • Competitive hourly wage

Key Responsibilities


Field Operations & Route Maintenance


  • Collection & Loading: Collect solid waste, organic, and recyclable materials from customer premises or curbside; load materials into the rear/side compartments of the vehicle.
  • Equipment Operation: Safely operate hydraulic compaction equipment and mechanism controls on the truck.
  • Route Efficiency: Work with the driver and route supervisor to follow predetermined route standards and suggest efficiency improvements.
  • Sorting & Material Handling: Sort materials into designated compartments as required; assist with sorting, cleaning carts, managing pallets/containers, and operating warehouse compactors as needed.

Vehicle & Driver Support


  • Driver Assistance: Direct the driver during backing maneuvers and tight-space navigation to ensure safe vehicle operation.
  • Pre-Route Audits: Verify the truck is equipped with necessary tools (e.g., broom, shovel, spill kits) prior to departing the branch.
  • Vehicle Maintenance: Assist the driver in keeping the interior cab and exterior of the vehicle clean and well-maintained.

Safety, Compliance & Quality


  • Safety Protocols: Strictly follow all personal, vehicle, and equipment safety checks. Comply with federal, state/provincial, local, and company safety rules.
  • PPE Adherence: Wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) at all times (e.g., high-visibility safety vest, work boots, safety glasses, gloves).
  • Prohibited Items: Identify and tag prohibited waste items, notify the driver/supervisor, and remove non-compliant items from carts or cans.
  • Meetings & Continuous Improvement: Actively participate in mandatory branch and safety meetings.


Customer & Professional Service


  • Professional Representation: Maintain a professional demeanor and positive attitude when interacting with customers and the public.
  • Issue Reporting: Immediately report customer concerns, damaged equipment, or route obstacles to the driver or supervisor.
  • General Support: Perform other operational duties as assigned by management.

Qualifications & Requirements


  • Education: High School Diploma or GED preferred, but not required.
  • Experience: 1–3 months of related experience (labor, route assistance, or waste management) preferred, but not required.
  • Driver’s License: Valid driver’s license is a plus, but not required.
  • Safety Compliance: Must meet all company criteria for performing safety-sensitive functions, including passing applicable background/drug screenings.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities


  • Strong verbal and written communication skills to interact effectively with team members and the public.
  • Ability to understand and execute instructions with limited supervision.
  • Capability to learn and safely operate truck mechanisms and route tools.

Physical Demands & Working Conditions


  • Physical Activity: Frequent standing, walking, bending, reaching, kneeling, crouching, and balancing throughout the shift.
  • Manual Lifting: Ability to manually lift and carry up to 65 lbs regularly.
  • Team Lifting: Ability to push, pull, or move up to 100 lbs with assistance.
  • Vision Capabilities: Must have good depth perception, peripheral vision, close/distance vision, and color recognition.

Work Environment


  • Outdoor Exposure: Work in an outdoor field environment up to 100% of the shift, exposed to varying weather conditions (rain, extreme heat, cold, high humidity).
  • Safety Hazards: Continuous work in motor vehicle traffic conditions, around moving

title: Director of Family Wealth
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Columbia Trust Company is building a dedicated Multi-Family Office (MFO) practice to serve ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) clients and families, leveraging Columbia's trust charter and expanded fiduciary and custodial capabilities. The Director of Family Wealth is a senior executive responsible for leading the organization's comprehensive wealth planning and family office strategy — spanning financial planning, estate and trust planning, tax-aware wealth strategies, business-owner advisory, family governance, philanthropy, risk management, and multigenerational wealth transfer. This role establishes the vision, capabilities, and service model necessary to deliver a differentiated, integrated family wealth experience, leading a team of specialized wealth professionals while client facing and partnering closely with relationship managers, private bankers, investment professionals, trust and fiduciary advisors, and other internal and external specialists.

About the Role:


Family Wealth Strategy & Family Office Leadership


  • Develop and execute the strategic vision for the MFO's Family Wealth and Family Office capabilities, establishing a consistent, scalable service model for UHNW families.
  • Build a comprehensive family office offering — consolidated wealth strategies and reporting, coordination of investment, trust, banking, and lending relationships, family governance, next-generation education, and philanthropic strategy.
  • Define service tiers and engagement models based on client complexity, assets, revenue potential, and family needs.
  • Serve as senior subject-matter expert and thought leader on complex family wealth matters, identifying emerging trends and evolving the platform's advisory capabilities accordingly.

Wealth & Estate Planning


  • Provide leadership and oversight for the organization's wealth and estate planning professionals, establishing standards for comprehensive, practical, and actionable planning.
  • Develop advanced planning capabilities for business owners, executives, entrepreneurs, and families experiencing significant liquidity or wealth-transfer events.
  • Partner with fiduciary and trust professionals on sophisticated trust, estate, and wealth-transfer opportunities, ensuring planning drives relationship development and retention.

Business Development & Revenue Growth


  • Partner with market leaders, relationship managers, private bankers, investment advisors, and trust professionals to identify and develop high-value opportunities.
  • Participate directly in significant prospective and existing client engagements where advanced planning or family office expertise can differentiate the platform.
  • Drive growth in AUM, fiduciary and trust appointments, lending relationships, planning penetration, share of wallet, and multigenerational client retention.
  • Build relationships with attorneys, accountants, investment bankers, private equity professionals, and other centers of influence serving wealthy families.

Business Owner & Liquidity Event Strategy


  • Develop specialized capabilities for entrepreneurs and closely held business owners across the business lifecycle, including succession, pre-transaction planning, and liquidity events.
  • Partner with commercial, investment banking, and private banking teams to identify business owners well before a potential transaction, positioning the team as central advisor before, during, and after the event.

Family Governance & Next-Generation Strategy

  • Develop programs that help families transition wealth, values, knowledge, and decision-making responsibilities across generations, including governance structures, family meetings, and education.
  • Create next-generation programs that build financial knowledge, strengthen relationships with heirs, and reduce generational asset attrition.

Team Leadership & Enterprise Partnership


  • Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing team of family office professionals and subject-matter experts, with clear performance expectations tied to engagement, planning activity, and revenue contribution.
  • Partner across Private Banking, Investment Management, Trust and Fiduciary Services, Commercial Banking, Investment Banking, Legal, Risk, and Compliance to create a seamless, coordinated client experience.
  • Ensure Family Wealth and Family Office activities operate within applicable legal, regulatory, fiduciary, and compliance frameworks.

Other Duties

  • Demonstrates compliance with all bank regulations for assigned job function and applies to designated job responsibilities – knowledge may be gained through coursework and on-the-job training. Keeps up to date on regulation changes.
  • Follows all Bank policies and procedures, compliance regulations, and completes all required annual or job-specific training.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of Bank's written policies and procedures regarding Bank Secrecy Act, Regulation CC, Regulation E, Bank Security and other regulations as applicable to this job description.
  • May be asked to coach, mentor, or train others and teach coursework as subject matter expert.
  • Actively learns, demonstrates, and fosters the Columbia corporate culture in all actions and words.
  • Takes personal initiative and is a positive example for others to emulate.
  • Embraces our vision to become “Business Bank of Choice”
  • May perform other duties as assigned.

About You:


Education/ Licenses/ Certifications


  • B.A. Required
  • JD, LLM, CPA Pref
  • CFP®, CFA®, CPWA®, CEPA®, CTFA, or other advanced trust/estate planning designation preferred.


Experience


  • 15+ Years experience in private wealth management, financial planning, estate planning, trust and fiduciary services, family office, private banking, or a related discipline. Required

Skills


  • Significant experience advising high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individuals, families, executives, and business owners.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead sophisticated wealth planning and family office engagements involving multiple professional disciplines.
  • Strong understanding of estate planning, trusts, taxation, investment management, business succession, philanthropy, and multigenerational wealth planning.
  • Demonstrated success leading and developing high-performing professional teams.
  • Strong business-development orientation with the ability to translate advisory expertise into measurable client and organizational growth.
  • Exceptional executive communication and presentation skills; ability to work effectively with senior executives, business owners, wealthy families, attorneys, CPAs, and other sophisticated advisors.


TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

  • Frequent

The base pay range for this role is $155,000.00 to $245,000.00.

At Nordstrom, our customers build our brand, but it is driven by our people. You will contribute to our long-standing culture and reputation by giving the best service, being a great teammate, and meeting sales goals. .

title: Assistant Member - Med Onc - Clinical Investigator
description:
Working at Moffitt is both a career and a mission: to contribute to the prevention and cure of cancer.

As the only National Cancer Institute-designated Comprehensive Cancer Center based in Florida, Moffitt employs some of the best and brightest minds from around the world. Join a dedicated team of nearly 11,000 who are shaping the future we envision. Moffitt has been recognized as a Best and Brightest Company to Work For in the Nation and is continually named one of the Tampa Bay Times’ Top Workplaces.

Summary

Certified by the American Board of Internal Medicine (or equivalent, as determined by the Medical Executive Committee, from time to time) with certificates of special qualification in hematology and/or medical oncology. For hematology, an internist with additional approved training, who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of malignant diseases of the blood, spleen and lymph glands. This specialist uses chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and targeted biologic therapies to treat conditions that include leukemia, lymphoma, and plasma cell neoplasms. For medical oncology, an internist with additional approved training, who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of multiple types of cancer of the solid organs. This specialist uses chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and targeted biologic therapies to treat conditions that include cancers of multiple organ systems. Practices medicine within the scope of authority and privileges granted by Moffitt Cancer Center. As a Member of the Moffitt Medical Group, provides patient care and serves as a member of the academic medical enterprise. Spanning the clinical and research enterprise in support of patient care, research, and education, advances the Institutional mission of contributing to the prevention and cure of cancer,

Moffitt Cancer Center is searching for a medical oncologist to join a high-volume GU practice with close collaboration with multidisciplinary colleagues in surgical oncology, radiation oncology, interventional radiology, pathology, radiology, and supportive care medicine. The candidate would provide patient care under the auspices of the Moffitt Medical Group and serve as a member of the academic medical enterprise, advancing the institutional mission of contributing to the prevention and cure of cancer. The position spans the clinical and research enterprise, and supports patient care, research, and education. The candidate would be joining a team of 6 medical oncologist throughout multiple sites and would have a special focus on bladder cancer clinical research. The candidate would work closely with a GU disease site team, which is a rapidly growing department at Moffitt with a robust clinical trial portfolio in GU cancer immunotherapy, cell therapy and adaptive therapy. More than 140 pts were enrolled in clinical trials over the past years and over 80% of the trials are early phase trials. Some of the investigator initiated studies like adaptive therapy and CAR T trial are developed through close collaborations with Moffitt’s research institute. Qualifications: Education/Licensure: • MD or Equivalent • Board certified (or eligible) in Hematology/Oncology • Requires successful completion of an approved Fellowship in Hematology/Oncology • Florida Medical License • DEA License • ACLS as required by privileges granted through Medical Staff

Deliver technically complex software solutions supporting business-critical mainframe applications. Perform application development, system integration, implementation, maintenance, and production support activities across the software development lifecycle. Partner with business product owners, technology teams, and other stakeholders to understand business objectives, evaluate technical requirements, and provide effective solution recommendations during design and implementation.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Following is a summary of the essential functions for this job. Other duties may be performed, both major and minor, which are not mentioned below. Specific activities may change from time to time.


· Design, develop, analyze, test, implement, and maintain complex application solutions using technologies and tools appropriate for the assigned application and technology environment.

· Lead and participate in the development, testing, implementation, maintenance, and support of highly complex solutions in adherence with company standards, including robust unit testing and support for subsequent release testing.

· Analyze business and technical requirements and translate them into reliable, scalable, maintainable, and supportable technology solutions.

· Perform system integration activities and collaborate with upstream and downstream application teams to support end-to-end business and technology processes.

· Troubleshoot and resolve complex application, batch, online transaction, data, and production issues using effective problem determination and root-cause analysis.

· Build and maintain application monitoring, operational controls, security controls, and other non-functional capabilities in accordance with company standards.

· Provide escalated technical and production support for highly complex and business-critical applications.

· Lead moderately complex technical initiatives and participate in larger, cross-functional technology initiatives.

· Apply software engineering standards and development best practices throughout requirements analysis, design, development, testing, implementation, and production support.

· Participate in code reviews and provide technical guidance to promote application quality, maintainability, performance, and adherence to established development standards.

· Serve as a technical resource for teammates with less experience and provide guidance to support technical development and knowledge sharing.

· May oversee or coordinate the technical work of a small team.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
1. Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering, or related field with 5 years of relevant experience or equivalent education and training.
2. In-depth knowledge of information systems and ability to identify, apply, and implement IT best practices.

Preferred Qualifications
1. Strong hands-on experience developing, maintaining, and supporting applications in an IBM z/OS mainframe environment.

2. Advanced proficiency with COBOL, including analysis, design, coding, debugging, maintenance, and performance considerations for complex batch and online applications.

3. Strong knowledge of JCL, including development and troubleshooting of production batch streams, utilities, return codes, abends, dataset allocation, and job dependencies.

4. Strong experience with CICS, including development and support of online transactional applications, CICS/COBOL programs, transaction flows, and production problem determination.

5. Strong DB2 for z/OS and SQL experience, including application programming, data analysis, SQL troubleshooting, and performance-conscious database access.

6. Experience designing, developing, maintaining, and supporting applications utilizing VSAM files.

7. Experience with enterprise workload automation and job scheduling tools such as ESP, TWS, or CA7, including job dependencies, production schedules, restart and recovery procedures, and troubleshooting failed production job streams.

8. Experience with mainframe source code management and deployment tools such as ChangeMan or Endevor. Familiarity with Git is beneficial.

9. Strong analytical, debugging, problem-solving, and production-support skills for complex enterprise applications.

10. Experience developing and supporting high-volume, business-critical applications in an enterprise environment.

11. Experience working with application integrations and interfaces across mainframe and distributed technology environments.

12. Experience working within Agile software development practices and collaborating across business and technology teams.

13. Banking or financial services industry experience.

Master's degree or equivalent advanced education and experience

title: Staff Platform Engineer, Cloud Platform
location: Seattle, Washington, United States of America
description:
Job Description

About the role

We want the experience of building and running software on GM's cloud to be as good as or better than what our engineers get from the best developer platforms on their own projects. Pushing code should be quick, getting a namespace or a database should take minutes, and production should stay up without heroics. We are not there yet, and that gap is the job.


This is a Staff-level, hands-on engineering role that spans the whole cloud platform. You will work across GM's internal cloud platform, the foundations underneath it, the control plane that developers interact with, and the runtime that keeps workloads healthy. You will write code, set technical direction, and raise the bar for the engineers around you.


We are hiring a small number of very strong engineers for this. If you have built a scaled platform that people chose to use because it was the easiest path, we want to talk to you.


What you'll work on

You will go where the hardest problems are, and today those include:

  • A platform people choose. Build the default way to ship software at GM so that it is easier than going around it. Move existing workloads onto it without downtime, and keep improving it based on what slows teams down.
  • Self-service infrastructure. Replace hand-built and ticket-driven provisioning with declarative, API-driven infrastructure, covering networking, identity and accounts.
  • Interfaces for people and agents. Design the APIs, CLI and MCP tools that engineers and AI agents use to get work done. Keep them simple and consistent, so no one needs another person in the loop to ship.
  • Reliability at scale. Design for availability and scale, including cell-based and multi-region architecture. Partner with SRE to define SLOs that mean something and remove the failures that page people at night.
  • Fast, safe delivery. Make the path from merge to production quick and boring, with promotion, rollback and policy built in.

What you'll do

  • Design and build core platform capabilities end to end, from API design through production operations.
  • Set technical direction for one or more platform areas and write the design documents that the rest of the team builds from.
  • Find the biggest sources of developer toil and platform instability, and eliminate them with code and automation rather than process or headcount.
  • Build golden paths so that the right way to ship at GM is also the easiest way.
  • Use AI tooling (Cursor, Claude Code and agents) as a normal part of how you build, and help make the platform itself usable by agents through APIs and MCP.
  • Partner with SRE on reliability, on-call and incident reviews, and hold the platform to measurable SLOs.
  • Mentor senior engineers, review designs and code across teams, and model the engineering standards we want.
  • Work directly with application teams to understand where the platform gets in their way, then fix it.

What we're looking for

  • 8 or more years building and operating production infrastructure or platforms, including several years in a senior or staff role with technical leadership across teams.
  • Deep, hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production at scale, including cluster operations, multi-tenancy, autoscaling and upgrades.
  • Strong software engineering skills in Go or a comparable language. You write production code, not only configuration.
  • Experience designing and running an internal developer platform, PaaS or cloud control plane that other engineers depend on.
  • Expertise with infrastructure as code and declarative provisioning (Terraform, Crossplane, or Kubernetes operators and controllers).
  • Solid grounding in cloud networking, identity and security, preferably on Azure.
  • A track record of improving reliability with SLOs, observability and blameless incident practice.
  • Strong product sense for developer experience. You care about the CLI output, the error message and the docs as much as the architecture.
  • The judgment to simplify. You would rather delete a system than add another one.
  • Clear written communication and the ability to bring a skeptical room along with a good design.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Istio or another service mesh, Gateway API, ArgoCD, Kargo, KEDA, Karpenter or Kyverno.
  • Built or migrated a large platform with zero downtime for tenants.
  • Experience with event streaming platforms such as Azure Event Hubs or Kafka.
  • Experience with cell-based or multi-region architectures.
  • Built MCP servers or other interfaces designed for AI agents.
  • Experience with cloud cost optimization and FinOps data pipelines.
  • Contributions to open source projects in the cloud native ecosystem.

title: Will train PCT
description:
PURPOSE AND SCOPE:

Functions as part of the dialysis health care team in providing safe and effective dialysis therapy for patients under the direct supervision of a licensed nurse in accordance with organization policies, procedures, and training and in compliance with regulations set forth by the corporation, state, and federal agencies. Responsible for the setup and operation of hemodialysis machines. Assist in the maintenance of a safe and clean working environment. Supports the organization commitment to the Quality Enhancement Program (QEP) and CQI Activities, including those related to patient satisfaction and actively participates in process improvement activities that enhance the likelihood that patients will achieve the organization Quality Enhancement Goals (QEP).

PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Patient Related

Education:

  • Assist other health care members in providing patient specific detailed education regarding adequacy measures where appropriate - Online Clearance Monitoring (OLC), Adequacy Monitoring Program (AMP), Urea Kinetic Modeling (UKM), and regarding disease process/access.

Treatment:

  • Welcome assigned patients and inquire as to their wellbeing since their last treatment.

  • Evaluate vascular access for patency, perform vascular access cannulation, and perform administration of heparin as delegated or as allowed by state law.

  • Obtain necessary pre and post treatment vital signs and weight and perform vascular access evaluation pre- treatment

  • Initiate dialysis treatment according to prescribed orders including blood flow (QB) and dialysate flow (QD).

  • Evaluate intradialytic problems and provide intervention as prescribed by physician order or as directed.

  • Monitor patients’ response to dialysis therapy.

  • Obtain vital signs prior to reinfusion; perform all relevant functions necessary for the discontinuation of treatment - document.

  • Discontinue dialysis treatment according to established procedures and evaluate patient prior to termination of venous access - standing & sitting blood pressure

  • Obtain Hemostasis and apply appropriate dressings.

  • Evaluate the patient prior to discharge.

  • Perform and record Pre and Post dialysis evaluation, weight, and vital signs with initial identification

  • Responsible for calculating and entry of individual patients’ dialysis machine programming for Ultrafiltration (UF) goal; treatment time; and UF modeling as prescribed.

  • Responsible for ensuring appropriate safety alarms are enabled, including Narrow Venous Limits, (NVL) 160.

  • Record accurate and timely information regarding vital signs and treatment parameters onto the Hemodialysis Treatment Sheet with initial identification

  • Responsible for accurate documentation of information related to patient treatment including completion of Hemodialysis Treatment Sheet and, if applicable, progress notes.

  • Report any significant information and/or change in patient condition directly to the registered nurse or supervisor.

  • Observe patient and conduct machine safety checks according to facility policy. Report any change or unusual findings to the registered nurse or supervisor.

  • Perform and document any intervention for unusual patient status and document patients' response to intervention.

  • Evaluate patients’ vascular access during treatment including arterial and venous monitoring pressures, provide appropriate intervention as needed, document and report any unusual findings to the registered nurse or supervisor.

  • Obtain all prescribed laboratory testing and prepare specimens for collection.

  • Ensure that all blood spills are immediately cleaned with appropriate disinfectant according to facility policy.

  • Prepare, organize, and efficiently utilize supplies and equipment to prevent wastage.

  • Monitors patients performing self-care under the supervision of RN.

Staff Related

  • Assists in training of applicable direct patient care staff on appropriate programs under the supervision of a nurse.

Education/Communication:

  • Follows all organization business policies, procedures and systems incorporated into training, including compliance with ethical business practices

  • Maintain environmental integrity and aesthetics - ensure all areas are safe and clean.

  • Clean and disinfect dialysis machine surface, chair, equipment, and surrounding area between treatments according to facility policy.

  • Conduct all tasks necessary for preparation for dialysis treatment and document where appropriate and perform all required pretreatment dialysis machine alarm testing including Pressure Holding (PHT).

  • Initiate Solution Delivery System (SDS) system.

RECORD KEEPING:

  • Complete and document ongoing participation in Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) activities.

  • Enters all treatment data into the designated clinical application in an accurate and timely manner.

  • Review treatment sheets for completeness, ensure nursing signatures are documented, and ensure

omitted entries are completed or corrected by appropriate staff.

  • Prepare initial patient chart for admission and compile paperwork for appropriate placement in chart.

  • Prepare/print lab requisitions for prescribed or stat Lab specimens according to laboratory destination.

  • Collect, label, appropriately prepare and store lab samples according required laboratory specifications.

  • Ensure collection of lab specimens by appropriate lab courier.

INFECTION CONTROL:

  • Assists in collecting information for infection control audits.

  • Supports staff and patient Adherence to infection control practices.

  • Follows infection control Policies and Procedures

  • Participates in and reinforces infection control education of patients and families under the direction of the CM or designee as allowed by state law.

TRANSITIONAL CARE UNIT:

  • Follows all newly admitted patients through their first 4 weeks of dialysis and coordinating their transitional dialysis care

  • Reinforces all education and care related matters as it relates to the new patient as allowed by state law

  • Liaisons with appropriate FKC staff members to provide the best patient experience including making sure all disciplines are scheduled to see patient according to plan.

  • Assists in assuring patient understanding or home dialysis products, benefits of home and how home dialysis can work for them.

  • Sets and preforms a treatment on all machines used in the transitional care unit.

  • Assist in assuring patient understanding of treatment options including demonstration of the peritoneal dialysis set-up.

  • Assists with coordination of transition to patient’s modality choice.

  • Assists with supply ordering and inventory for TCU

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS:

  • The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee

encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable

individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Employees are required to take the Ishihara's Color Blindness test as a condition of employment. Note that: Failing the

Ishihara Test for Color Blindness does not preclude employment. The Company will consider whether reasonable

accommodations can be made.

  • Day to day work includes desk and personal computer work and interaction with patients, facility staff, and physicians. The position requires travel between assigned facilities and various locations within the community. Travel to regional, Business Unit and Corporate meetings may be required.

  • The work environment is characteristic of a health care facility with air temperature control and moderate noise levels. May be exposed to infectious and contagious diseases/materials

  • The position provides direct patient care that regularly involves heavy lifting and moving of patients and assisting with ambulation. Equipment aids and/or coworkers may provide assistance. This position requires frequent, prolonged periods of standing and the employee must be able to bend over. The employee may occasionally be required to push and/or pull equipment, exerting up to 15 pounds of force. The employee may be required to lift and to lower solutions on a frequent basis of up to 30 lbs., and on an occasional lift basis up to 40 lbs., as high as 5 feet. There is a two-person assist program and "material assist” devices for the heavier items.

EDUCATION AND LICENSES:

  • High School diploma or G.E.D. required.

  • Must meet Center for Medicaid/Medicare Services (CMS)-approved state and/or national certification requirements within the required state or CMS timeline.

  • All appropriate state licensure, education, and training (if any) required.

  • Demonstrated commitment to organization culture, values, and customer service standards

EXPERIENCE AND REQUIRED SKILLS:

  • Previous patient care experience in a hospital setting or a related facility preferred.

  • Continued employment is dependent on successful completion of the organization dialysis training program and successful completion of CPR certification.

Senior Director, Enterprise Risk Management

At Capital One, we dare to dream, disrupt, and deliver a better way. We bring ingenuity, simplicity, and humanity to an industry ripe for change. As a senior leader in Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), you will join a critical second-line-of-defense function responsible for defining the bank’s risk management architecture. This role is at the heart of our Risk Management Framework, positioned to take a critical role as we modernize our processes to be more nimble and effective while maintaining a robust risk posture.


We are seeking a strategic, forward-leaning Senior Director to spearhead our Risk Appetite, Board Reporting, and Effective Challenge programs. You will lead the charge crafting impactful and insightful enterprise-wide risk reporting to our Senior Management and Board of Directors, You will be a critical leader in the transformation in our Risk Appetite and Effective Challenge programs, with a focus on real time, intelligent solutions. This is a high-impact leadership position where you will regularly analyze complex topics and engage with senior executives across the lines of defense.


Responsibilities:

  • Deliver high-impact reporting to Senior Management and the Board of Directors, providing a comprehensive and strategic view of the enterprise risk profile.
  • Design and operationalize a next-generation Risk Appetite program that leverages intelligent risk insights and real-time data aggregation, taking into account our diverse financial services company.
  • Lead cross-functional efforts to enhance Effective Challenge discipline across the second line of defense, ensuring rigorous oversight and impactful risk management.
  • Partner with technology and data teams to implement an enterprise system of record for key risk metrics, enabling predictive analytics, and automation.
  • Lead and develop a team of 8-12 risk professionals, organizing the team’s work to drive results, providing feedback and coaching to support professional development, and maintaining a strong pipeline of talented risk leaders.

This role is designated as a hybrid position. You are expected to adhere to Capital One's hybrid policy regarding required on-site presence at your designated office location.

  • Bachelor's Degree or military experience
  • At least 10 years of experience in Risk Management, Project Management, or Process Management
  • At least 5 years of experience leading initiatives in a highly-regulated financial services environment
  • At least 5 years of experience influencing C-suite stakeholders and Board-level committees
  • At least 5 years of experience leading and developing teams

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to interact and influence at all levels in the organization, including with senior and C-level executives
  • Experience driving risk framework evolution through technology, AI, and automation.

  • Expertise in navigating and influencing across all three lines of defense.

title: Business Planner Intern
description:
Job Description

Job Description


Are you passionate about the automotive industry and ready to start a career at General Motors? Join our Business Planning team and work side by side with the Managing Director of GM de México (and the Mexico Executive Committee) in a role that gives you a front-row seat to how a global automaker is run.


As a Business Planner Intern, you will provide administrative, coordination and analytical support to the Managing Director, ensuring the seamless planning and execution of meetings, events, trips and special projects. You will interact daily with leaders across functions, plants, dealers and regional/global counterparts, and you will have the chance to learn the business end to end while leveraging Artificial Intelligence and digital tools to make our team more efficient.


What You Will Do

  • Manage and coordinate the General Director's agenda, meetings, guests and visits, anticipating conflicts and keeping stakeholders aligned.
  • Plan and coordinate domestic and international travel: flight and hotel options, itineraries, logistics and ground transportation.
  • Support the planning and execution of executive events and leadership forums (Mexico Executive Committee sessions, plant visits, town halls, leadership meetings), including agendas, participants, catering and vendor coordination.
  • Prepare and track expense reports, purchase requisitions and purchase orders in GM systems (e.g., Concur, Ariba), working with Finance and suppliers to close them on time.
  • Draft and send professional communications in Spanish and English to executives, internal teams, and regional and global counterparts.
  • Keep key information up to date and organized (executive/planner directories, organization charts, shared folders, trackers and templates).
  • Support cross-functional projects and initiatives, preparing presentations, summaries and follow-ups for the Managing Director's office.
  • Build and improve team tools, dashboards and automations using data and AI to reduce manual work and improve decision-making.
  • Handle confidential information with the highest level of discretion and professionalism.

What We Are Looking For

Requirements

  • Currently enrolled in the final stages of a bachelor's degree (semester or quarter), with expected graduation in December 2027 or July 2028.
  • Education: Engineering, Business Administration, Industrial Relations, Economics, Marketing, or related disciplines.
  • English: Advanced (written and spoken) – you will communicate with global teams and executives.
  • Proficient in MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, Teams).
  • Practical knowledge of Artificial Intelligence and experience applying it to projects (e.g., generative AI assistants, process automation, content or data analysis).
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build relationships and communicate effectively with people at all levels of the organization.
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proactive, curious and resilient; comfortable adapting to changing priorities and working with autonomy.
  • Ability to handle confidential information with discretion and integrity.
  • Genuine interest in the automotive industry and in building a long-term career at GM.

Desirable (not mandatory)

  • Knowledge of Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet)
  • Experience or exposure to Databricks, Microsoft Azure or Google Apps Script.
  • Data analytics: basic understanding of data analysis and visualization (Excel, Power BI or similar), or a strong interest in developing these skills.
  • Prior internship or project experience in planning, project coordination, operations or executive support.

What You Will Gain

  • Direct exposure to GM México's senior leadership and to how strategic decisions are made.
  • End-to-end visibility of the business: sales, marketing, product planning, manufacturing, finance and more.
  • Hands-on experience with AI, data and automation in a real corporate environment.
  • Mentorship, networking and a clear path to explore opportunities and grow your career within GM.






About GM

Our vision is a world with Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions and Zero Congestion and we embrace the responsibility to lead the change that will make our world better, safer and more equitable for all.

Why Join Us

We believe we all must make a choice every day – individually and collectively – to drive meaningful change through our words, our deeds and our culture. Every day, we want every employee to feel they belong to one General Motors team.

Non-Discrimination and Equal Employment Opportunities

From concrete and asphalt repairs to restoring surfaces affected by underground utility construction, our restoration crews play an important role in completing projects safely and professionally.

  • Iowa – Statewide
  • Sioux Falls, South Dakota
  • Omaha, Nebraska

Primoris Gas Operations, which includes companies such as Q3 Contracting, ARB, Primoris Distribution Services, Snelson, and Pipejacking Trenchless, brings over 60 years of experience to the natural gas distribution industry.

Throughout the years, we've maintained longstanding customer relationships, many spanning more than two decades, through our commitment to safety, quality workmanship, and exceptional value.

We recognize that the quality of our work begins with the people performing it, and we're proud of the dedicated professionals who help us serve our communities every day.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Perform hands-on restoration work following underground utility construction.
  • Assist with concrete patching, repairs, and finishing.
  • Lay and finish asphalt patches.

  • Assist with preparing, maintaining, and cleaning up job sites.
  • Follow established safety procedures and work collaboratively with crew members.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned to support daily restoration operations.

We're seeking dependable individuals who take safety seriously, work well with others, and are ready to contribute to a hardworking restoration crew.


General Requirements:

  • Valid driver's license with a clean driving history.
  • Class A CDL highly preferred, but not required for all positions.
  • Willingness to travel occasionally when project needs require it.
  • Ability to perform physically demanding outdoor work.
  • Ability to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to stand and walk on uneven surfaces, bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, and perform other physical tasks throughout the workday.
  • Willingness to work in varying weather conditions, including extreme heat and cold.
  • Ability to follow instructions, work safely, and contribute to team goals.
  • Commitment to quality workmanship, teamwork, and dependable attendance.

Specific qualifications and requirements may vary depending on the position.


Compensation & Benefits

Competitive Union Wages – Paid Weekly!

  • Competitive union wages based on applicable classification and agreements.
  • Annual negotiated wage increases.
  • Union-sponsored benefits, subject to applicable agreements and eligibility.
  • Outstanding paid, on-the-job training.
  • Award-winning safety programs.
  • Overtime opportunities based on project needs.
  • Opportunities for career growth and advancement.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

Restoration work takes place primarily outdoors in active construction environments.

Employees may be exposed to:

  • Varying weather conditions, including heat, cold, rain, and humidity.
  • Uneven ground surfaces and changing terrain.
  • Elevated noise levels from construction equipment and surrounding activity.
  • Slow- and fast-moving traffic near active work zones.
  • Physically demanding tasks requiring frequent standing, walking, bending, lifting, and kneeling.

Ready to Join the Crew?

Every great project deserves a great finish. Be part of the team that makes it happen.

Whether you're an experienced restoration professional or a hardworking individual ready to build a career in the utility construction industry, we encourage you to apply.

Bring your work ethic. Take pride in your work. Let's get to it!

Drug-Free Workplace

Q3 Contracting maintains a drug-free work environment. All candidates are subject to applicable drug testing requirements.


Equal Employment Opportunity

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
