title: IRT Systems Project Manager
description:
IRT Systems Project Manager

We are seeking an experienced IRT Systems Project Manager to lead the design, implementation, and delivery of Interactive Response Technology (IRT) solutions supporting global clinical trials.

In this highly consultative role, you will partner with pharmaceutical and biotechnology clients to translate complex clinical study protocols into effective IRT system designs that ensure patients receive the correct study treatment throughout the trial. You will act as a trusted advisor to clients, providing expert guidance on system strategy, study configuration, and best practices while managing projects through the full lifecycle from design to go-live.

This role combines technical IRT expertise, client consultation, and project leadership, offering the opportunity to work across a diverse portfolio of clinical research studies.

Key Responsibilities

IRT System Design & Client Consultation

  • Review and analyse clinical study protocols to understand study objectives and system requirements.
  • Partner with clients to design IRT solutions that align with protocol requirements and operational goals.
  • Provide strategic guidance and recommendations on optimal system design and study setup.
  • Author and maintain detailed user requirements and design documentation.
  • Collaborate with clients and internal stakeholders to review, refine, and approve system requirements.

Project Management & Delivery

  • Lead the end-to-end delivery of assigned IRT studies, ensuring project milestones and timelines are achieved.
  • Manage study implementation activities to support successful study launch ahead of First Patient In (FPI).
  • Monitor project scope, identify potential risks, and manage change requests and budget impacts where required.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure successful execution of project deliverables.
  • Conduct system quality reviews and support client demonstrations throughout the project lifecycle.

User Acceptance Testing (UAT)

  • Coordinate and support internal and client-facing User Acceptance Testing activities.
  • Work closely with technical and validation teams to ensure systems meet study requirements.
  • Guide clients through the UAT process and provide expert support in resolving questions and issues.
  • Ensure testing outcomes are accurately documented and implemented before production release.

Leadership & Continuous Improvement

  • Serve as a subject matter expert (SME) for IRT system design and implementation.
  • Contribute to process improvement initiatives, standards development, and lessons learned activities.
  • Support protocol amendment activities and system enhancements throughout the study lifecycle.
  • Deliver comprehensive study handovers and training to operational teams.
  • Mentor junior team members and contribute to technical training programmes.
  • Support client meetings, bid defence presentations, quarterly business reviews, and audit activities as required.

Qualifications & Experience

Required

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
  • Several years of experience in clinical research, clinical technology, project management, or a related field.
  • Hands-on experience delivering and managing Interactive Response Technology (IRT) solutions.
  • Strong understanding of clinical trial operations, patient randomisation, and clinical supply management processes.
  • Experience working directly with sponsors, CROs, or other external stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to interpret clinical protocols and translate requirements into effective system solutions.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong client-facing consulting and relationship management skills.
  • Excellent project planning, organisation, and prioritisation abilities.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to delivering quality outcomes.
  • Collaborative team player with the ability to work independently.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and other business applications.

As an IRT Systems Project Manager, you will play a critical role in the successful execution of clinical trials that help bring innovative therapies to patients around the world. As a Senior Site Reliability Engineer on JLL’s Technical Engineering team for corporate functions, you will serve as a trusted technical authority for the PeopleSoft FSCM 9.2 environment that underpins finance operations across our global business. You will bring deep expertise in PeopleSoft development, functionality, and backend administration, along with strong automation skills, including server-level scripting and Python, to design, implement, and maintain reliable, scalable, and performant platforms. title: 2027 Summer Intern - Research & Development - Energy and Propulsion Controls
location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
description:
Job Description

The Role:

As a 2027 Summer Intern on the Energy and Propulsion Controls team, you will support researchers and engineers working on advanced vehicle energy-management, propulsion-control, and thermal-management technologies.


A primary focus of this role will be the EVE Research Program, where thermal management is a core technical deliverable. You will help translate ongoing research into vehicle-level control concepts, models, simulations, and implementation activities that support efficient, safe, and high-performing electrified propulsion systems.


You will gain experience connecting control strategies with batteries, power electronics, electric machines, propulsion systems, thermal loops, sensors, actuators, and vehicle-level energy requirements. GM’s thermal-control work includes coordinating battery, power-electronics, drive-unit, charging, HVAC-related, and front-end airflow requirements while balancing efficiency, performance, comfort, and component

protection.


The Team:


The Research and Development organization explores technologies that can improve vehicle efficiency, propulsion performance, charging, thermal behavior, durability, and customer experience. The EVE Research Program includes work across advanced controls, thermal management, propulsion-energy conversion, fast charging, and vehicle health management.


You will work in a multidisciplinary environment with controls researchers, thermal engineers, propulsion specialists, modeling and simulation experts, and vehicle-development teams. The team applies systems engineering, controls theory, experimentation, simulation, and data analysis to evaluate new concepts and transition promising research into vehicle applications.


What You’ll Do:

  • Support ongoing research assignments related to energy management, propulsion controls, thermal management, and vehicle-level control coordination.
  • Help develop, evaluate, and document control strategies for battery, power electronics, electric machines, drive units, charging systems, and related thermal systems.
  • Support the vehicle implementation of thermal-management research, including control logic for coolant pumps, valves, compressors, heaters, fans, shutters, and other thermal actuators.
  • Develop or modify models used to study battery, propulsion, and thermal-system behavior under representative vehicle operating conditions.
  • Run simulations and analyze system behavior across drive cycles, ambient conditions, charging conditions, operating modes, and component limits.
  • Evaluate tradeoffs among energy consumption, range, component temperature, charging performance, propulsion capability, drive quality, efficiency, and occupant comfort.
  • Support the development of interfaces between propulsion controls, energy-management functions, battery systems, thermal systems, HVAC-related systems, and vehicle-level controllers.
  • Analyze sensor and actuator data to identify trends, control issues, performance limitations, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Compare simulation results with laboratory, bench, hardware-in-the-loop, or vehicle-test data when available.
  • Assist with control-strategy verification and validation through test-case development, test execution, data review, and issue investigation.
  • Support the documentation of requirements, control logic, system assumptions, interfaces, calibration parameters, test procedures, and technical results.
  • Create plots, dashboards, presentations, technical summaries, and other materials that communicate findings to engineering and research stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with researchers and engineers to define technical questions, establish analysis plans, review results, and recommend next steps.
  • Present progress and technical findings in team reviews and incorporate feedback into follow-on work.

Required Qualifications:

  • Pursuit of an advanced degree (MS or PhD) in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, controls engineering, computer engineering, chemical engineering, systems engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months.
  • Must be willing to work in a laboratory, engineering test, or vehicle-development environment, as applicable to the assignment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Coursework, research, or project experience in control systems, thermal systems, energy management, vehicle dynamics, battery systems, power electronics, electric propulsion, or mechatronics.
  • Experience with MATLAB/Simulink, Python, Modelica, GT-SUITE, or comparable modeling and simulation tools.
  • Familiarity with feedback control, system identification, optimization, state estimation, calibration, or control-oriented modeling.
  • Experience analyzing time-series data from simulations, laboratory testing, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or vehicle testing.
  • Experience with sensors, actuators, data acquisition, embedded controls, or software development.
  • Understanding of battery state of charge, battery power limits, thermal limits, energy consumption, regenerative braking, or propulsion-system operating modes.
  • Familiarity with CAN, LIN, signal databases, vehicle data logging, or other automotive communication and measurement technologies.
  • Ability to organize technical work, document assumptions, investigate unexpected results, and communicate conclusions clearly.
  • Strong analytical, written, and verbal communication skills, along with curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Primary Skills & Experience

  • 10+ years of experience in Modern End User Computing infrastructure, with 5+ years of hands-on experience in Microsoft Intune and SCCM.

  • Strong Intune administration & Engineering experience including user management, application packaging and deployment, service administration, PR & Platform scripting, compliance policies, and device profile management.
  • Expertise in Intune Conditional Access, Device Compliance, Software Update Management, Endpoint Security, and Device Configuration Policies.

  • Manage global software distribution, Microsoft security updates, and standard desktop software deployments.

  • Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards, operational reports, and executive-level reporting for endpoint compliance, software lifecycle management, device health, inventory, and security posture.
  • Strong automation capabilities using PowerShell and VB Scripting for endpoint administration, software deployment, remediation, and operational process automation.
  • Work with corporate security teams to identify, assess, and remediate endpoint security risks.
  • Meet with internal stakeholders to assess business needs, identify challenges, and define project scope and deliverables.
  • Deep understanding & hand on experience with Digital Employee Experience platforms such as Nexthink or SysTrack.
  • Strong understanding of endpoint security technologies, security baselines, and modern workplace security patterns.

  • Ability to influence outcomes, drive adoption, and gain buy-in for new initiatives and ways of working.
  • Product-oriented mindset with the ability to identify opportunities for innovation, automation, and continuous improvement.
  • Demonstrable thought leadership and passion for Modern Workplace, Digital Employee Experience, and Endpoint Management services.
  • Strong awareness of IT Service Management principles and ITIL practices.
  • Develop and drive the Endpoint Management and Modern Workplace roadmap, aligning technology investments with business objectives, security requirements, and employee experience goals.
  • Partner with Architecture, Security, Infrastructure, and Digital Workplace teams to define and implement strategic initiatives that improve endpoint security, automation, operational efficiency, and user productivity.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies, industry trends, and Microsoft roadmap capabilities, providing recommendations to leadership on future-state workplace services and platform modernization.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives, leveraging automation, analytics, and data-driven insights to optimize service performance, compliance, and operational effectiveness.

  • Experience with Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) solutions such as BeyondTrust EP & CyberArk, Intune.

title: Senior CRA
description:
Why Join Clinical Functional Service Partnerships (CFSP)?

At IQVIA, our Clinical Functional Service Partnership (CFSP) model gives you the best of both worlds: the variety and sponsor-level exposure of working as an embedded member of a leading pharmaceutical or biotechnology team, backed by the stability, global infrastructure, and career support of IQVIA. You'll develop deep, specialist expertise on a dedicated program, with the flexibility to expand across sponsors and therapeutic areas as your career progresses - and the security of a long-term IQVIA career even as individual programs evolve.

Through our long-standing partnerships with the world's leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, you'll contribute to clinical research programs that bring innovative treatments to patients worldwide, working across all phases of development and a broad range of therapeutic areas, within a culture that supports flexibility, continuous learning, and wellbeing.

Key responsibilities

  • Conduct site qualification, initiation, monitoring, and close-out visits in accordance with study protocols, GCP, ICH guidelines, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure investigational sites maintain high standards of patient safety, data integrity, protocol compliance, and study quality.
  • Build and maintain effective relationships with investigators and site personnel, providing ongoing guidance, training, and support throughout the study lifecycle.
  • Monitor study progress, including regulatory documentation, patient recruitment and enrollment, data query resolution, and site performance metrics.
  • Collaborate with sites to implement and optimize patient recruitment and retention strategies to support study timelines.
  • Maintain accurate, complete, and inspection-ready study documentation, including Investigator Site Files (ISF), Trial Master Files (TMF), monitoring reports, and follow-up communications.
  • Identify, assess, and appropriately escalate study risks, site issues, and quality concerns while driving timely resolution.
  • Partner closely with cross-functional study teams to support successful study execution and delivery of project objectives.
  • Mentor and support junior clinical team members through coaching, training, and co-monitoring activities, as applicable.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and support study start-up, maintenance, close-out, and site financial activities as required.

What you’ll bring

  • University degree in Life Sciences, Health Sciences, Nursing, Pharmacy, or a related discipline, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 4 years minimum on-site monitoring experience of clinical trials within a CRO, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or healthcare environment.
  • Strong knowledge of GCP, ICH guidelines, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Preferrable experience in a sponsor-dedicated or cFSP environment.
  • Knowledge of patient recruitment and study start-up activities is preferred.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and collaborate effectively within cross-functional teams.
  • Willingness to travel within the assigned region (up to 40-60% of working time).

Please note this position cannot offer visa sponsorship, candidates must hold right to work in UK & Ireland.

Build Your Future with IQVIA

As a Senior CRA at IQVIA, you'll apply your clinical research expertise to drive meaningful outcomes for patients and sponsors around the world. You'll work on innovative studies across a variety of therapeutic areas, collaborate with industry-leading professionals, and take on increasingly strategic responsibilities throughout the clinical trial lifecycle. With continuous professional development, global career opportunities, and a culture that values expertise and innovation, IQVIA provides the platform to elevate your career and make a lasting impact on healthcare.

IQVIA is a leading global provider of clinical research services, commercial insights and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences and healthcare industries. title: Facilities Technical Project Manager (TPM)
description:
Who We Are


Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.


What We Offer


Salary:

$116,000.00 - $159,500.00

Location:

Gloucester,MA

You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.

About the Role

  • We are seeking a Level 4 Facilities & Real Estate Technical Project Manager to lead delivery of mission-critical infrastructure projects that enable semiconductor R&D and advanced manufacturing operations.
  • This role is accountable for cleanroom retrofit/build projects and tool-ready infrastructure/process utilities (highest priorities), managing work from feasibility through commissioning and turnover in a live, operational environment.
  • This is a senior individual contributor role (no direct reports) that operates in a matrix environment with strong support from controls, electrical, IT, gas/life safety, EHS, and administrative resources.
  • The TPM will own scope, schedule, and CAPEX forecasting, and will lead cross-functional alignment with lab owners, R&D/Engineering, Operations, and Logistics.
  • Note: This role does not coordinate tool installs directly; it is responsible for delivering infrastructure readiness to support tool installation and ongoing operations.

What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities)

Project Leadership (End-to-End Delivery)

  • Lead facilities and real estate capital projects from concept/feasibility through design, construction, commissioning, and closeout.
  • Develop and manage project execution plans including phasing strategies, shutdown/tie-in plans, and business continuity measures for live operations.
  • Drive disciplined scope definition and establish clear design and construction deliverables, acceptance criteria, and turnover requirements.

Top Priority #1: Tool-Ready Infrastructure / Process Utilities

  • Deliver infrastructure upgrades and expansions supporting semiconductor tools and R&D operations, including coordination of HVAC and environmental control systems; process and general exhaust systems; make-up air and airflow balance strategies; clean dry air (CDA), vacuum, and other process utilities (as applicable); electrical distribution; controls/BMS integration; and monitoring systems.
  • Coordinate specialty gas infrastructure interfaces in partnership with gas/life safety SMEs.
  • Ensure infrastructure designs and field execution align with operational needs, reliability targets, and safety requirements.

Top Priority #2: Cleanroom Retrofit / Build

  • Lead cleanroom retrofit/build efforts while protecting contamination control, safety, and uptime.
  • Coordinate cleanroom design and execution considerations including ISO classification considerations, pressure regimes, airflow patterns, filtration strategies, and contamination control practices during construction.
  • Plan commissioning readiness and operational turnover.

Construction & Contractor Management

  • Lead RFP development, bid evaluation, contractor selection recommendations, and ongoing contract administration in partnership with Procurement.
  • Manage construction execution including RFIs, submittals, field coordination, quality inspections, safety compliance, change management, schedule recovery plans, and punch list closure.
  • Coordinate commissioning activities, turnover documentation, and closeout packages.

Financial & Schedule Ownership (L4 Expectations)

  • Own project financial management with emphasis on CAPEX forecasting, monthly projections, accrual coordination, and variance analysis (PO approval monitoring).
  • Evaluate change orders and manage forecast impacts (cost and schedule).
  • Build and maintain integrated schedules in Microsoft Project (required) including logic ties, milestones, critical path management, and progress updates.
  • Partner with controls support for reporting and schedule performance insights; Primavera P6 exposure is a plus for future scaling.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Leadership (Matrix Execution)

  • Serve as the primary project integrator across Facilities, EHS, Security, IT, Engineering, R&D, Operations, and Logistics.
  • Lead effective meetings (weekly project reviews, design reviews, construction coordination, commissioning readiness).
  • Communicate clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders; escalate risks early with recommended mitigation paths.
  • Influence without authority while maintaining accountability across internal partners and contractors.

What Success Looks Like (Performance Outcomes)

  • Infrastructure readiness delivered on time to support tool enablement and lab operations (tool install managed by others).
  • Cleanroom retrofit/build projects executed with strong contamination control, safety performance, and minimal operational disruption.
  • Forecast accuracy improves over the project lifecycle with transparent variance explanations and proactive corrective actions.
  • Contractors managed effectively: quality execution, controlled change, safe work, and predictable turnover.
  • Stakeholders describe execution as disciplined, transparent, and operationally sensitive.

Required Qualifications

  • 5–10 years of progressive project management experience in facilities capital projects; 10–15 years preferred for complex, independent ownership.
  • Demonstrated delivery of MEP-intensive projects in operational environments (manufacturing, life sciences, data centers, advanced R&D, or similar).
  • Proven ability to lead construction administration including RFIs, submittals, contractor performance management, and change control.
  • Strong competency in CAPEX forecasting, cost tracking, and variance reporting (PO approval not required).
  • Microsoft Project proficiency (required): ability to build schedules from scratch and manage critical path and updates.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder leadership in a matrixed environment.

Highly Desirable Qualifications

  • Experience delivering tool-ready infrastructure for semiconductor or advanced manufacturing environments.
  • Experience with cleanrooms (retrofit/build, contamination control practices, operational turnover).
  • Primavera P6 exposure (nice-to-have) for potential future adoption.
  • PMP (or equivalent) is a plus.
  • Familiarity with commissioning approaches for MEP/process utility systems and structured turnover documentation.

Core Competencies (Level 4)

  • Technical breadth: understands how building systems interact; can challenge assumptions and spot coordination gaps.
  • Owner-rep rigor: clear scope control, disciplined change management, contract/commercial awareness.
  • Operational sensitivity: plans work to protect uptime, safety, and contamination control.
  • Predictive management: anticipates risk and communicates mitigation early; drives decision-making.
  • Stakeholder leadership: influences without authority, aligns competing priorities, and maintains accountability.

Working Conditions

  • Onsite presence required; work includes frequent field walks and active construction areas.
  • Occasional off-hours coordination may be required for shutdowns/tie-ins and critical work windows.
  • Limited relocation assistance may be considered for the right candidate (role-dependent).

Additional Information

Time Type:

Full time

Employee Type:

Assignee / Regular

Travel:

Yes, 10% of the Time

Relocation Eligible:

No

title: Cost Performance & Value Lead
description:
Rio de Janeiro, Brazil


Job Family Group:

Production Engineering Upstream


Worker Type:

Regular


Posting Start Date:

October 30, 2026


Business Unit:

Upstream


Experience Level:

Experienced Professionals


Job Description:


Job Description

1. About the Role

The Cost Performance & Value Lead will step-change how Production Excellence manages, challenges and influences OPEX performance across the INOVA and Mero non-operated portfolio (~900 MM SS). The role integrates cost performance management, industry benchmarking using available metrics such as McKinsey and A&M, forward spend forecasting based on historical performance and planned technical activities, contract & ballot strategy evaluation against cost impact and structured JV influence to improve cost transparency, mature value opportunities, close structural cost gaps and move assets toward top-quartile competitiveness. The incumbent will turn operational, contractual and financial data into clear value cases, use them to shape Operator decisions, strengthen Shell positions and deliver practical, sustainable OPEX improvements.


Key accountabilities


  • Own the integrated OPEX performance view for INOVA and Mero, covering Operator Billing, Actuals, Work Program & Budget, Latest Estimate, Ballots and Operational Plan.
  • Analyze cost performance at (i) asset, (ii) FPSO, (iii) discipline and (iii) contract level, explaining variances, trends, and changes in scope, rate, volume, FX or timing. Work close to the technical discipline and SC focal points is paramount. Given the nature of NOV business, it is required to adopt some practices to infer figures and their range of uncertainty and ensure consistency across asset/FPSO for such assumptions.
  • Build robust quarterly forecasts (support group quarter LE and monthly routine) and annual plan assumptions by integrating production outlook, contract conditions and emerging risks and opportunities.
  • Assess deepwater OPEX drivers and use internal and external benchmarks to identify structural cost gaps, outliers and repeatable good practices across the portfolio.
  • Translate cost gaps into risk-based opportunity statements with clear baselines, value potential, dependencies, owners, milestones and decision requirements. Be a key member of the Roomba framework: develop and maintain a health funnel of opportunities for Prod Excellence.
  • Lead JV approach: Prepare fact-based technical and commercial positions to influence the Operator through JV governance forums and working-level engagements. Challenge Operator (budgets, forecasts, ballots, contract strategies and cost proposals) distinguishing unavoidable spending from controllable, deferrable or avoidable demand.
  • Partner with Contracting & Procurement, Finance, Economics, Legal, Operations and technical disciplines to develop negotiation strategies and aligned Shell positions.
  • Define business requirements for digital and analytical solutions that automate data ingestion, reconciliation, classification, benchmarking and scenario analysis.
  • Coach and quality-assure cost-analysis activities across the team, setting standards for analytical rigor, commercial framing and executive communication.

2. Skills and Requirements


Experience and knowledge

  • Engineering degree with 10+ yr experience in cost performance within upstream and its dependencies with contract and commercial dependencies as well as technical disciplines.
  • Robust knowledge of costs related to operations activities since this is mainly Opex driven. Candidates should be highly capable of deriving inferences of cost movements within a NOV environment.
  • Good understanding of O&G Joint Operating Agreements, JV governance and cost-recovery mechanisms.
  • Demonstrated ability to build business cases, engage Operator, influence outcomes and convert analysis into opportunity funnel.
  • Advanced analytical capability using large and imperfect datasets, with strong Excel and data-visualization skills.
  • Experience shaping digital or automated cost-management solutions is highly advantageous.
  • Fluent professional English and Portuguese, written and spoken.

Critical skills and behaviors

  • Influence without authority: building credibility through fact-based opportunities identification, building credible solution space, navigates conflicting interests and secures commitment across organizational boundaries.
  • Analytical problem solving: separates signal from noise, tests assumptions and converts complex data into clear decisions.
  • Constructive challenge: asks difficult questions, uses evidence and remains solution-oriented.
  • Delivery focus: maintains a disciplined opportunity pipeline and follows through to measurable outcomes.

description:

Job Description:

What’s the role

Shell is seeking an Asset Engineer to join its team in Monaca, Pennsylvania.

The Asset Engineer provides front-line technical and equipment support for the Production Unit (PU), helping ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operation of the asset. The role is embedded within the PU technical team, which translates operational priorities into structured technical work and manages troubleshooting, threat resolution, and operational improvement activities focused on the unit’s most critical reliability, safety, and optimization needs.

This role will bring a strong field presence and broad equipment perspective, working closely with Operations and other technical resources to identify emerging equipment issues, understand their operational impact, support near-term resolution, and escalate issues requiring deeper technical expertise.

This role will serve as an embedded technical resource in the production team, with a primary focus on the physical condition, reliability, and near-term technical needs of the equipment within the area.

The future operating model positions the Hard Side Asset Engineer as the PU resource responsible for managing physical equipment engineering solutions. More broadly, the frontline technical team monitors equipment performance, analyzes technical issues, and supports troubleshooting and reliability improvement.

You will work closely with Operations to maintain awareness of equipment condition and emerging threats, provide timely technical input, and help translate equipment concerns into clear actions. You will resolve issues within the capability and time horizon of the PU while engaging Site Technical when problems require advanced troubleshooting, engineered solutions, specialized discipline support, or longer-term intervention. The operating model specifically differentiates these responsibilities, with Production focused on near-term operations and Site Technical addressing deeper technical issues and systemic reliability problems.

The role requires an engineer who is comfortable operating in the field, working across engineering disciplines, making sound risk-based technical judgments, and connecting equipment condition to safe and reliable operation.


What you’ll be doing

  • Provide day-to-day equipment engineering support to the Production Unit, maintaining close engagement with Operations and the frontline technical team
  • Monitor equipment condition and performance, identify developing reliability or integrity concerns, and support troubleshooting of near-term equipment issues
  • Maintain a regular field presence to understand equipment condition, changing operating conditions, and potential safety or environmental concerns
  • Support development of practical mitigation plans for on-stream equipment issues, engaging the appropriate discipline engineers when specialized engineering is required
  • Monitor upcoming inspection and equipment integrity requirements and identify obstacles that could affect near-term compliance or execution
  • Provide operating and equipment context to Site Technical when issues exceed PU capability and require advanced troubleshooting, root cause analysis, or an engineered solution. The operating model establishes Site Technical as the partner for recurring equipment issues and systemic failure resolution
  • Support Management of Change activities by providing the unit requirements, operating context, and equipment knowledge needed to define safe and effective changes. In the future-state model, Production defines the need and operating constraints while Site Technical or Projects determines the engineering solution and governance

What you bring

  • Must have legal authorization to work in the US on a full-time basis for anyone other than current employer
  • Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline relevant to industrial asset or equipment support
  • At least 5 years of relevant experience
  • Strong understanding of equipment reliability, mechanical integrity, troubleshooting, and safe operation in a manufacturing or process environment
  • Ability to recognize developing equipment problems, assess technical risk, and translate observations and data into practical recommendations
  • Strong field orientation and willingness to spend time where the equipment and work are located
  • Ability to work effectively across engineering disciplines rather than approaching every issue through a single-discipline lens. This aligns with the future-state expectation that Production develops broader cross-discipline troubleshooting capability and escalates when deeper specialization is required
  • Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make sound technical judgments using incomplete or evolving information
  • Working knowledge of equipment integrity, reliability, Management of Change, technical assurance, and risk-management principles
  • Ability to communicate technical issues clearly to Operations, Maintenance, engineering specialists, and leadership
  • Strong collaboration and influencing skills, with the ability to bring multiple disciplines together around safe, practical solutions
  • Ability to balance immediate operational needs with equipment integrity and reliability considerations
  • A proactive mindset, curiosity about how equipment performs and fails, and a commitment to identifying issues before they become operational events

What we offer

The base salary range for this position is $124,000 - $186,000 per year. Individual pay will be based on various factors, such as relevant work experience, education, certifications, skill level, seniority, and internal equity.

For regular full-time or regular part-time employees of the Company (participating companies as listed in the Summary Plan Description), insurance coverage options include medical, dental, vision coverage, life Insurance, Business Travel Accident Insurance, and Occupational Accidental Death Benefit programs. Employees also participate in a company pension plan and a 401(k) plan. Paid leave includes up to 6 weeks of paid vacation time, up to 11 paid holidays, and parental leave offering 16 weeks of paid leave for birthing parents, and 8 weeks of paid leave for non-birthing parents.

Additionally, employees are eligible for short-term disability leave for up to 26 weeks at 100% or 50% of base pay as well as Long-Term Disability insurance. Shell also offers other compensation such financial reimbursement for adoption, wellness, education, and personal learning expenses, and some roles are eligible for discretionary long-term incentives. For interns, eligible benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, Business Travel Accident Insurance, and Occupational Accidental Death Benefit programs; participation in a 401(k) plan; and paid leave for up to 11 paid holidays. Additional information on Shell’s US benefit programs can be found at https://www.shell.us/careers/about-careers-at-shell/rewards-and-benefits.html.

You bring your skills and experience to Shell and in return you work with talented, committed people on one of the most important challenges facing our planet. You’ll have the opportunity to develop the skills you need to grow in an environment where we value honesty, integrity, and respect for one another. You’ll be able to balance your priorities as you become the best version of yourself.

  • Progress as a person as we work on the energy transition together
  • Continuously grow the transferable skills you need to get ahead
  • Work at the forefront of technology, trends, and practices
  • Collaborate with experienced colleagues with unique expertise
  • Achieve your balance in a values-led culture that encourages you to be the best version of yourself
  • Benefit from flexible working hours, and the possibility of remote/mobile working
  • Perform at your best with a competitive starting salary and annual performance related salary increase – our pay and benefits packages are considered to be among the best in the world.
  • Take advantage of paid parental leave, including for non-birthing parents
  • Join an organization working to become one of the most diverse and inclusive in the world. We strongly encourage applicants of all genders, ages, ethnicities, cultures, abilities, sexual orientation, and life experiences to apply
  • Grow as you progress through diverse career opportunities in national and international teams
  • Gain access to a wide range of training and development programs

We'd like you to know that Shell has a bold goal: to become one of the world’s most diverse and inclusive companies. You can get to know more about how we're working towards that goal, click here.

Shell in The United States

With more than 11,000 employees, Shell has been in the US for more than 100 years and is delivering secure energy supplies across America.

From producing a reliable supply of oil and gas in the US Gulf of America to biofuels, our retail sites and EV charging network, to marketing and trading electricity generated by gas plants, solar and wind power, we are one of the few countries where every Shell business is represented.

We are working with our customers to deliver the energy the world needs today and building the energy systems of tomorrow, all while creating value for society and shareholders.

We are Omnissa!

The world is evolving fast, and organizations everywhere—from corporations to schools—are under immense pressure to provide flexible, work-from-anywhere solutions. They need IT infrastructure that empowers employees and customers to access applications from any device, on any cloud, all while maintaining top-tier security. That’s where Omnissa comes in.

The Omnissa Platform is the first AI-driven digital work platform that enables smart, seamless and secure work experiences from anywhere. It uniquely integrates multiple industry-leading solutions including Unified Endpoint Management, Virtual Apps and Desktops, Digital Employee Experience, and Security & Compliance through common data, identity, administration, and automation services. Built on the vision of autonomous workspaces - self configuring, self-healing, and self-securing - Omnissa continuously adapts to the way people work; delivering personalized and engaging employee experiences, while optimizing security, IT operations and costs. we're experiencing rapid growth—and this is just the beginning of our journey!

At Omnissa, we’re driven by a shared mission to maximize value for our customers. Our five Core Values guide us: Act in Alignment, Build Trust, Foster Inclusiveness, Drive Efficiency, and Maximize Customer Value—all with the aim of achieving shared success for our clients and our team.

What is the opportunity?

Workspace ONE is a digital workspace platform that simply and securely delivers and manages any app on any device by integrating access control, application management and multi-platform endpoint management. It is available as a cloud service or for on-premises deployment.


Our goal is to enable Workspace One-Unified End point Management platform to scale and manage billions of devices across various operating system platforms and device types by providing choice for customers who require sovereignty.

  • Program management for OSS in India & selected APJ markets.
  • Stakeholder management - Responsible for reporting to ELT, BU & senior APJ stakeholders for OSS partners
  • Champion the need for OSS partner model & eco-system across region in APJ
  • Responsible for OSS road map & business plan in APJ

What will you bring to Omnissa?


  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science or related field
  • Strong experience in partner management within End User Compute 6 to 12 years experience.
  • Hands-on experience with EUC customer business development.
  • Solid working knowledge of India Market for End User Compute.
  • Familiarity with Sovereignty & related issues .
  • Experience of program & customer management.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across matrix and cross functional teams.
  • An understanding of what it takes to deliver customer experience in regulated markets.
  • Experience of driving GTM programs across different market and country segments.

Nice to Have


  • Working technical knowledge of Omnissa Workspace One, Omnissa Portfolio or other MDM/UEM digital workplace solutions.
  • Exposure to working with regulated & highly secure customers.
  • Proposition Management expérience

title: Senior Engineer
description:
Welcome to Haleon. We’re a purpose-driven, world-class consumer company putting everyday health in the hands of millions. In just three years since our launch, we’ve grown, evolved and are now entering an exciting new chapter – one filled with bold ambitions and enormous opportunity.

Our trusted portfolio of brands – including Sensodyne®, Panadol®, Advil®, Voltaren®, Theraflu®, Otrivin®, and Centrum® – lead in resilient and growing categories. What sets us apart is our unique blend of deep human understanding and trusted science.

Now it’s time to fully realise the full potential of our business and our people. We do this through our Win as One strategy. It puts our purpose – to deliver better everyday health with humanity – at the heart of everything we do. It unites us, inspires us, and challenges us to be better every day, driven by our agile, performance-focused culture.

About the role

We are seeking a highly skilled Platform Engineer to design, engineer and maintain enterprise operating system platforms across Haleon’s Cloud and Edge environments. This role is primarily focused on Linux platforms, with responsibility for supporting Windows Server platforms and related technologies where required.

Working within an Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and DevOps delivery model, the successful candidate will leverage technologies such as Ansible and Terraform to develop scalable, secure, and consistent platform solutions. The role requires strong Linux engineering expertise, automation skills, and a passion for continuous improvement.


This is a platform engineering and consultancy role rather than a traditional operations position. The focus is on engineering, automation, and continuous improvement of server platforms, while providing technical guidance to application, cloud, and infrastructure teams.


Key Responsibilities

  • Engineer, automate, and continuously improve enterprise Linux and Windows server platform capabilities.
  • Define and maintain operating system standards, engineering patterns, and best practices.
  • Develop and support Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and platform automation solutions using approved tooling.
  • Provide technical consultancy and guidance to application, cloud, and infrastructure teams.
  • Ensure server platforms align with security, compliance, and operational requirements.
  • Support the delivery of secure, reliable, and scalable platform services across cloud and edge environments.
  • Drive platform standardisation and continuous improvement initiatives.

Qualifications and Skills


Education

  • Bachelor’s Degree: Preferably in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field (of equivalent experience).

Professional Experience

  • 8+ years' experience administering and engineering enterprise server platforms, with a primary focus on Linux operating systems and exposure to Windows Server environments.
  • Experience supporting Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), Oracle Linux, Ubuntu, and Windows Server operating systems in enterprise environments.
  • Experience building, maintaining, and supporting Linux and Windows Server gold images and standard server templates.
  • Experience implementing CIS Benchmarks and operating system security hardening controls.
  • Experience developing and supporting automation solutions using Ansible, Terraform, Packer, Python, Shell scripting, and/or PowerShell.
  • Experience working with CI/CD pipelines and Infrastructure-as-Code methodologies.
  • Experience engineering and supporting Linux and Windows Server workloads within Microsoft Azure environments.
  • Experience with operating system lifecycle management, including patching, upgrades, software repositories, and image maintenance.
  • Experience with Red Hat Satellite or equivalent enterprise operating system management solutions is desirable.

Essential Skills

  • Strong administration and engineering knowledge of Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), Oracle Linux, and Ubuntu.
  • Good working knowledge of Windows Server administration, operating system management, and associated technologies.
  • Knowledge of enterprise server imaging, operating system deployment, and image lifecycle management.
  • Strong automation skills using Ansible and IaC tools such as Terraform, Packer.
  • Proficiency in Python, Shell scripting, and/or PowerShell.
  • Knowledge of Microsoft Azure infrastructure, cloud services, and hybrid environments.
  • Understanding of Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and CI/CD principles.
  • Knowledge of CIS Benchmarks and operating system security hardening standards.
  • Knowledge of Red Hat Satellite, package lifecycle management, patch management, and software repository administration.
  • Understanding of Active Directory, DNS, identity and access management, and enterprise authentication services.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across infrastructure, cloud, security, and application teams.

title: 2027 Summer Intern - Research and Development - Aftertreatment Catalysis
location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
description:
Job Description

The Role

General Motors is seeking a motivated student to join the Energy and Propulsion Systems Research team as a Summer Intern in aftertreatment catalysis. The intern will contribute to research supporting next-generation automotive emissions-control technologies, including catalyst performance, durability, materials development, reaction kinetics, system modeling, and data-driven materials discovery.


This opportunity is intentionally broad and may be well suited for students with experimental, computational, modeling, data science, or artificial intelligence and machine learning backgrounds. The specific project will be aligned with the candidate’s skills and the team’s research priorities.


The Team

The team is re-establishing and advancing GM’s aftertreatment catalysis research capabilities. Current research areas include three-way catalysts, platinum-group-metal reduction, catalyst aging and durability, alternative catalyst and substrate materials, hydrocarbon and nitrogen-oxide traps, reaction kinetics, predictive modeling, and AI/ML-enabled materials discovery.


What You’ll Do

Depending on your background, you may:

  • Design, conduct, and analyze laboratory experiments for catalyst, washcoat, powder, or aftertreatment core evaluation.
  • Prepare samples and support testing using laboratory reactor systems and analytical tools.
  • Investigate catalyst activity, selectivity, conversion efficiency, thermal durability, aging, sintering, and degradation mechanisms.
  • Apply characterization methods such as Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, diffuse-reflectance infrared Fourier-transform spectroscopy, surface-area analysis, chemisorption, microscopy, spectroscopy, or related techniques.
  • Develop reaction-kinetic, catalyst-performance, degradation, or system-level models.

Laboratory experimentation and analytical characterization. Mathematical modeling, simulation, scientific computing, or numerical methods. Data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, or optimization.

title: 2027 Summer Intern - Research and Development - Energy and Propulsion Systems Architecture
location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
description:
Job Description

The Role:

As a 2027 Summer Intern on the Energy and Propulsion Systems Architecture team, you will work with researchers and engineers to evaluate how energy storage and propulsion systems work together at the vehicle level. You will contribute to architecture studies, simulation and analysis activities, and laboratory testing that help inform the design and development of future electrified propulsion systems.

This role offers hands-on exposure to the connection between battery cells, modules and packs, electric propulsion components, power electronics, controls, thermal systems, and vehicle performance. You will apply engineering fundamentals, data analysis, and systems thinking to turn test and simulation results into clear technical insights.


The Team:

The Research and Development organization explores and evaluates technologies that can improve vehicle energy efficiency, propulsion performance, durability, range, and customer experience. The Energy and Propulsion Systems Architecture team connects research, modeling, simulation, and laboratory experimentation to understand system-level behavior and guide architecture decisions.


You will work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment with researchers and engineers across battery, propulsion, controls, thermal management, modeling, and vehicle development. The team values sound engineering judgment, careful experimentation, clear documentation, and the ability to communicate technical findings to both specialists and broader project teams.


What You’ll Do:

  • Support energy and propulsion systems architecture studies, including the evaluation of battery, electric machine, drive unit, power electronics, controls, and thermal-system interactions.
  • Develop, run, and interpret vehicle-level propulsion and energy simulations across representative operating conditions and drive cycles.
  • Analyze energy consumption, performance, power capability, operating limits, state-of-charge behavior, and other system-level measures to identify trends and architecture tradeoffs.
  • Assist with cell, module, and battery-pack testing by helping prepare test activities, configure equipment or data acquisition, collect data, and maintain organized test records.
  • Support laboratory work related to battery characterization, pack performance, durability, modeling, and analysis while following applicable laboratory safety and handling practices.
  • Compare experimental results with model predictions, investigate differences, and help improve model assumptions, inputs, or analysis methods.
  • Clean, process, visualize, and interpret test and simulation data; summarize results using clear plots, tables, and written technical explanations.
  • Create or update system block diagrams, interface descriptions, requirements documentation, analysis scripts, test summaries, and technical presentations.
  • Collaborate with researchers and engineers to define questions, document assumptions, review results, and recommend next steps.
  • Present technical findings in team discussions and incorporate feedback into follow-on analyses.

Required Qualifications:

  • Pursuit of an advanced degree (MS or Phd) in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, chemical engineering, materials science and engineering, automotive engineering, aerospace engineering, systems engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months.
  • Must be willing to work in a laboratory and engineering test environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Coursework, research, or project experience in battery systems, electrochemistry, energy storage, electric propulsion, power electronics, controls, thermal systems, vehicle dynamics, or systems engineering.
  • Experience with engineering modeling, simulation, or data analysis using MATLAB/Simulink, Python, Excel, or comparable tools.
  • Experience processing time-series data and communicating technical results through plots, reports, or presentations.
  • Laboratory, test, or instrumentation experience, including an understanding of experimental design, measurement quality, and safe work practices.
  • Ability to organize technical work, manage multiple priorities, and work effectively with cross-functional teams.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, curiosity, and a willingness to learn from both successful and unsuccessful experiments.

SUMMARY

The Charlotte Department of Transportation (CDOT) is seeking a Transportation Planner to lead and advance the city’s Shared Micromobility Program within the department's Mobility Planning Division. This position leads city oversight and administration of Charlotte’s permitted, privately operated dockless e-scooter and e-bike program, including operator compliance, program evaluation, policy development, and coordination of parking infrastructure. Working closely with staff across the city and external partners, the selected candidate will lead policy and program development for shared micromobility, conduct GIS and data analysis, assist with communications and stakeholder engagement, and lead planning and implementation of micromobility parking corrals.

Shared micromobility is an important component of Charlotte’s vision of safe and equitable mobility as outlined in the city’s adopted Strategic Mobility Plan (SMP) and Charlotte’s commitment to Vision Zero. Shared Mobility Program Administration

  • Serve as the primary City point of contact for permitted shared mobility operators, maintaining regular communication and working relationships with private partners.
  • Monitor operator compliance through data review, field observations, and complaint tracking; document deficiencies, coordinate corrective actions, and recommend further action under permit requirements when needed.
  • Coordinate with operators on special events and operational needs.
  • Manage updates to permit requirements and program rules.
  • Manage and track invoicing, program revenue, and required operator reporting.
  • Coordinate operators’ permit applications and renewals; review required documentation and maintain program records in collaboration with appropriate city staff.

Policy & Program Development

  • Develop and implement new policies and programs to improve the effectiveness and utilization of shared micromobility in Charlotte.
  • Manage and analyze operator data, GIS information, field observations, and public feedback to evaluate ridership, device availability, parking compliance, equitable access, and progress toward program goals.
  • Coordinate with operators, software vendors, and city technology staff to address data quality, reporting, and appropriate handling of program data.
  • Prepare periodic performance summaries, maps, presentations, and recommendations to inform program improvements and communicate results to city leadership and stakeholders.
  • Identify opportunities to:
    • Improve vehicle distribution, availability, and accessibility throughout the community.
    • Improve parking and vehicle management.
    • Expand access to shared micromobility.
    • Reduce costs to city administration and to end users to improve program efficiency.

Communications & Stakeholder Coordination

  • Prepare information and coordinate responses to inquiries from City Council, constituents, internal city partners, event teams, and other stakeholders; create and deliver. presentations communicating shared micromobility operations, concerns, and program benefits.
  • Monitor operator implementation of Community Access Program commitments, evaluate participation and barriers to use, and coordinate improvements with operators and community partners.
  • Coordinate public education with operators and city communications staff on responsible riding, proper parking, program access, and reporting concerns.
  • Coordinate with internal partners to address operational issues and incorporate shared mobility into broader City initiatives and events.
  • Respond to complaints and operational concerns and follow through with operators on corrective actions and best practices, including vehicle staging and parking.
  • Lead and participate in engagement initiatives to promote shared mobility and increase access and awareness, including occasional night and weekend events.

Shared Micromobility Infrastructure Planning & Development

  • Lead planning and implementation of micromobility parking corrals.
  • Perform routine field evaluations to monitor parking and deployment conditions.
  • Use shared micromobility management software and other available input and data to identify locations with high parking demand and prioritize future corral locations.
  • Working closely with partners on city staff, program the implementation and construction of parking corrals that support accessibility of devices and best practices for management of deployment and parking.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, & ABILITIES:


  • Demonstrated working knowledge of the principles and practices of urban and transportation planning.
  • Ability to develop, interpret, and administer transportation policies and ordinance requirements and revisions.
  • Project management skills and thorough understanding of active transportation facility planning, design, and implementation techniques.
  • Ability to diplomatically and effectively address concerns from residents, elected officials, various departmental managers, and outside agencies.
  • Ability to use common desktop computer applications for word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, publishing, electronic mail, internet research, billing, financial compliance, communications, etc.
  • Proficiency in ArcGIS for geospatial data analysis and production.
  • Familiarity with shared micromobility management platforms and data-sharing standards, such as Mobility Data Specification (MDS), and the ability to use these tools for program monitoring, analysis, and compliance.
  • Ability to understand and effectively use data for mobility-related analyses and mapping.
  • Ability to address controversial and emerging issues in the community on a regular basis.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective public relations and working relationships.
  • Experience as a regular user of active transportation, micromobility, and transit.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's Degree with five years of relevant work experience

OR

  • Master's Degree with three years of relevant work experience

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS :

  • Master's degree in Urban Planning, Transportation Engineering, or a related field
  • Certified Planner (AICP) and/or Professional Engineer (PE)
  • Direct experience with shared micromobility, permit administration, operator/vendor oversight, or transportation program management
  • Experience with Vision Zero, Safe System, or active transportation planning

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

The position involves a combination of office-based work and periodic field activities related to shared micromobility program administration and parking infrastructure planning.


Office and computer work: Ability to use a computer and standard office equipment, review documents and maps, analyze data, and prepare reports, presentations, and other written materials. Work may involve extended periods of computer use.


Communication: Ability to exchange information effectively with coworkers, operators, members of the public, and other stakeholders through in-person meetings, telephone, and electronic communication.


Fieldwork and site inspections: Ability to travel to and evaluate micromobility parking locations, observe operating conditions, and assess parking compliance and pedestrian accessibility. Fieldwork may involve walking and standing for varying periods and navigating sidewalks, curb ramps, paved paths, and other public-right-of-way environments.


Lifting up to 70 lbs., pulling, and moving equipment: Ability to occasionally lift, pull, push, or reposition shared micromobility devices, including electric scooters and bicycles, as needed to support program operations, parking assessments, or related activities.


·Outdoor work: Ability to conduct occasional field observations outdoors in varying weather conditions and in environments with pedestrian, bicycle, and vehicular traffic, while following applicable safety procedures.


Meetings and presentations: Ability to participate in meetings, deliver presentations, and engage with stakeholders in an office or other designated meeting environment.


Mobility within the workplace: Ability to move between office locations, meeting spaces, and field sites as required by assigned duties, using available transportation arrangements and reasonable accommodations where applicable

title: Field Sales Engineer - Barcelona Area
description:
Nordson Packaging, a global leader in precision dispensing, fluid management, and related technologies, is seeking a highly motivated and talented Field Sales Engineer to join our team in Spain. To be centrally located and close to our clients, you ideally reside in the Barcelona area. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we are looking for candidates who share that same commitment.


Summary of the Role


As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, where your ideas and contributions will be valued and respected.


As Field Sales Engineer, you will cover Strategic Users of Eastern Spain, in a remote, customer-facing role.


The role combines technical curiosity with commercial responsibility and offers autonomy within Nordson’s international EMEA organization. You will work with a broad portfolio of products and applications and varied technical challenges.


Role and Responsibilities


  • Identify new business opportunities within the territory, targeting and securing new key accounts in alignment with company objectives.
  • Develop and grow relationships with existing customers, expanding business by promoting additional products and applications.
  • Understand customers’ technical and commercial needs and propose suitable Nordson solutions through a consultative, value-based sales approach.
  • Conduct regular, meaningful customer visits and proactively plan your territory and weekly activities.
  • Develop and execute customer-specific account strategies informed by customers’ future investment plans, sharing relevant information with internal stakeholders.
  • Negotiate pricing, contracts and long-term commercial agreements to ensure profitability and growth.
  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date records of installed Nordson equipment, key contacts, customer visits, opportunities and pipeline information in C4C/CRM.
  • Support sales forecasting and reporting, and monitor market development, competitors, opportunities and potential business risks. Provide market intelligence to internal teams to guide product development and innovation.
  • Coordinate with Customer Service to ensure timely delivery and support.
  • Collaborate with colleagues across Sales, Service, Aftermarket, Engineering, technical teams and the wider EMEA organization.


Skills and Qualifications


  • A degree with a focus on Business, Engineering or a related field, an advanced business qualification is a plus.
  • At least 5 years of experience in a B2B sales role in industrial or technical markets.
  • Strong value-based selling skills, with the ability to clearly communicate the business value of proposed solutions.
  • Experience in negotiating complex contracts and long-term supply agreements
  • A consultative and customer-oriented sales mindset.
  • Strong relationship management skills and the ability to communicate with individuals at all levels.
  • Strong commercial awareness and analytical capability.
  • Good organization and territory-planning skills, with the ability to work independently in a field-based environment.
  • Professional spoken and written working proficiency in Spanish and English are mandatory.
  • A valid driving license and willingness to travel regularly throughout the territory.
  • Experience using C4C/CRM systems and Microsoft Office/Microsoft 365.
  • Familiarity with structured sales methodologies (Value Selling, Solution Selling) are beneficial.
  • Previous experience within pneumatics, sensors, vision systems, PLCs, injection-related systems or comparable products are an advantage.

Travel


Customer interaction is at the heart of the position. You can expect:


  • Approximately 70% field travel incl. regular overnight stays (weekly 1-2)

Benefits


We offer a flexible work schedule, a comprehensive benefits package, a company car for private use and opportunities for growth and development.


About Nordson Packaging

Nordson Packaging is the leader in precision dispensing, fluid management, and related technologies. We serve the Packaging end market to improve production efficiency and product quality for a variety of packaging manufacturing processes. By joining our team today, you will help us bring innovative ideas to life. Nordson Packaging is a global team that works to create technology that helps efficiently apply adhesives to meet both form and function for a wide variety of packaging applications like tankless technology, self-diagnostic and intuitive touch-screen controls, auto-fill technology, clean-cutoff and self-cleaning applicators, and pattern generation controls. We offer a supportive culture in a growing and dynamic work environment. Whether you're just beginning your career or you're a seasoned professional, there's a place for you to belong at Nordson Packaging. We offer hourly and salary positions in production, maintenance, customer service, quality, engineering, and more. We actively invest in our teams to help you build your skillsets and advance your career.

Our recruitment process is designed to identify the best qualified candidates for the role, and we are committed to ensuring a fair and equitable interview process. We are looking for candidates who have a passion for inclusion, diversity and equity, and the ability to contribute to a culture where all employees feel valued, respected, and included.


Interested?


If you are interested in being a part of a team that is dedicated to providing advanced inspection and testing solutions and creating an inclusive and diverse workplace, please apply online with your CV.

title: VP, Program Team Lead
description:
Program Team Leader, Vice President

About BridgeBio Oncology Therapeutics

BBOT is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing a next-generation pipeline of novel small molecule therapeutics targeting RAS and PI3K malignancies. BBOT has the goal of improving outcomes for patients with cancers driven by the two most prevalent oncogenes in human tumors. For more information visit BBOTx.com.

Who You Are

We are seeking a Program Team Leader (PTL), Vice President to serve as the strategic and operational leader for BBOT’s clinical development programs. Reporting to the Chief Medical & Development Officer, the PTL will have high-level accountability for the delivery of business objectives and portfolio value across the full product lifecycle. This is a visionary leadership role for an entrepreneurial scientist-executive who excels at leading cross-functional teams as the program leader, driving ambitious but deliverable product strategies, and building credibility with internal and external stakeholders at the highest levels. The PTL will be instrumental in advancing BBOT’s mission to deliver transformative oncology therapies to patients.

Responsibilities

Strategic Program Leadership

  • Lead the cross-functional program team (core team and sub-teams) to define, refine, and execute the integrated global product strategy across the full development lifecycle—from early-phase through initial approval, launch, and lifecycle indications
  • Serve as the primary accountable leader for program delivery, ensuring milestones, timelines, and budget targets are met; proactively identify risks and lead the team in developing and executing mitigation strategies
  • Drive ambitious and deliverable product strategy by identifying and maximizing opportunities for the program; coalesce diverse internal and external stakeholder perspectives to inform key decisions and align the organization
  • Ensure appropriate governance and compliance across all program activities; protect BBOT’s rights, data, and intellectual property throughout the development and commercialization lifecycle
  • Represent the program in interactions with BBOT senior leadership, the Board, and external stakeholders; provide clear, compelling updates on program status, strategy, and value creation

Cross-Functional Team Leadership

  • Build, lead, and inspire high-performing cross-functional program teams spanning Clinical Development, Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Translational Medicine, Clinical Pharmacology, CMC, and other relevant functions
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, scientific rigor, and entrepreneurial problem-solving within the program team; ensure team members are aligned, motivated, and empowered to deliver
  • Lead integrated program planning across all functions, ensuring clear ownership, dependencies, and resource alignment for all program-critical activities
  • Serve as the primary point of escalation and decision-making authority for cross-functional program issues; facilitate rapid, well-reasoned decisions to maintain program momentum

Scientific and Clinical Strategy

  • Provide strategic scientific and clinical leadership for assigned programs, including input into clinical development plans, protocol design, patient selection strategies, biomarker integration, and data interpretation
  • Translate emerging clinical and scientific data into strategic insights that shape program direction; lead data review meetings and ensure findings are rapidly and accurately communicated to internal and external stakeholders
  • Champion the integration of precision medicine and biomarker strategies into program development plans, partnering closely with Translational Medicine and Clinical Pharmacology
  • Build and maintain productive relationships with key external oncology opinion leaders, academic collaborators, investigators, cooperative groups, and patient advocacy organizations to strengthen BBOT’s scientific position and program execution

Regulatory and Commercial Alignment

  • Serve as the program-level strategic interface with Regulatory Affairs to shape global regulatory strategy and ensure consistent, proactive engagement with FDA, EMA, and other global health authorities
  • Ensure program strategies are informed by deep understanding of the competitive landscape, payer environment, and commercial opportunity; integrate commercial insights and market research into development planning
  • Support and contribute to regulatory submissions, health authority meetings, and interactions with investigators and advisory committees as the senior scientific and strategic program representative

title: Winter Weekend Snowshoe Tour Guide
description:
Join the Team: Winter Weekend Snowshoe Tour Guide

Bogus Basin Mountain Recreation Area — Boise National Forest, ID | Seasonal | Part-Time (Weekends)

The Winter Snowshoe Tour Guide will lead nature-based, guided snowshoe outings and programs at Bogus Basin on Saturdays and Sundays. Working with the Environmental Education Coordinator, this position will share knowledge of winter ecology, recreation and Bogus Basin as they tour the snowshoe trails around the Frontier Point Lodge. The Weekend Snowshoe Tour Guide will also work with local experts on select outings throughout the winter giving opportunity for themed programs. Through these tours and programs we hope to foster curiosity in participants of the natural world.


Why Bogus Basin?

Where Mountain Life Meets City Living: Located just 16 miles from Boise, Bogus Basin offers the unique chance to work in a mountain environment while living in one of the fastest-growing and most livable cities in the U.S.

Mission-Driven, Community-Focused: As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Bogus Basin’s mission is to provide affordable, accessible, and fun recreation and education opportunities for the community. Every guided snowshoe tour helps deepen participants’ connection with nature and the winter landscape while supporting environmental education.

Unbeatable Access to the Outdoors: Snowshoe through the Boise National Forest and help inspire curiosity in participants while enjoying perks such as mountain access and employee discounts.


How You’ll Make a Difference

As a Winter Snowshoe Tour Guide, you’ll create meaningful guest experiences by leading educational tours, connecting participants to the natural world, increasing accessibility in winter recreation, and supporting Bogus Basin’s nonprofit mission. You’ll also collaborate with supervisors and local experts to offer themed programs and ensure tours are engaging, safe, and memorable.


A Day in the Life

On a typical weekend day, you’ll prepare equipment, welcome guests and share about your offerings, meet and greet participants, and lead groups of 1–15 individuals on guided snowshoe tours. Along the trails, you’ll share your knowledge of winter ecology, Bogus Basin, and winter recreation while adjusting routes to meet group needs. Some days, you’ll coordinate with local naturalists to deliver themed outings. After tours, you’ll support Nordic lodge operations, maintain professional communication with staff and patrons, and contribute to the overall success of the program.


Essential Functions of the Job

  • Work independently and with supervisor to thoughtfully plan and organize tours with relevant talking points and group-appropriate routes.
  • Lead and engage groups of adults and youth in a winter environment (1–15 individuals) while on snowshoes.
  • Talk on the trail and spend the day outdoors in a variety of weather conditions.
  • Create a safe and fun learning environment.
  • Communicate with industry experts before “guest speaker” tours.
  • Maintain a professional attitude toward all patrons, staff, supervisors, and other departments.
  • Perform other duties as required
