This senior individual contributor role, with no direct reports, will connect Engineering business priorities with the data foundations, standards, and organizational capabilities necessary to make information trusted, accessible, and reusable.

Working across Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, Product Management, Service, and IT, the selected candidate will establish strategic priorities, guide data governance and stewardship, and partner with technical specialists to enable scalable solutions. The role will support engineering data domains including laboratory data, product lifecycle information, parts and materials, engineering documents, product configuration, and supplier data.

The position will also help advance engineering taxonomies, ontologies, knowledge graphs, and semantic capabilities that enable Engineering IQ, digital-thread initiatives, and AI-driven engineering workflows.

  • Facilitate cross-functional alignment and lead organizational change to promote adoption of common standards, processes, and data-driven ways of working.
  • Partner with technical teams to identify and address data quality issues, integration challenges, and barriers to information accessibility.
  • Establish measures of business value, adoption, data quality, and operational efficiency to evaluate progress and guide continuous improvement.
  • Build partnerships across Engineering, business functions, and enterprise technology teams to promote reusable capabilities, shared accountability, and sustainable solutions.

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, data science, information systems, business, analytics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience translating business objectives into data, analytics, and technology priorities that deliver measurable value.
  • Ability to lead through influence, build cross-functional partnerships, and align stakeholders in a complex, matrixed organization.
  • Experience driving organizational change, stakeholder engagement, and adoption of new technologies or ways of working.

  • How can an airline build and enhance its payment value proposition for consumers and/or small businesses?
  • How can a credit card issuer use emerging technologies like open banking to acquire new customers?
  • How can an acquirer or merchant better understand customer loyalty?

VCA engages clients throughout Europe and is organised in teams within, UK & Ireland, South Europe, FBL, Nordics & Baltics, Central Eastern Europe, and Central Europe


Day to day responsibilities of an Intern Consultant:

Job Profile Summary:
Provides expert guidance to international students and scholars, spearheads initiatives that promote global education and cross-cultural understanding, and ensures compliance with immigration regulation. Provides expert guidance to students participating on international and domestic programs.

Job Description:

Arizona State University’s Global Education Office (ASU GEO) is hiring a Faculty Directed Program Coordinator. The successful candidate will be part of a team of eight (8) working to support ASU’s robust custom program portfolio and join a broader office with 25 team members. If you are interested in joining a growing and collegial office that values creativity, innovation and access, then this is the job for you. Come be a part of the future of global education at America’s most innovative university!

ASU GEO is a leader in global education, enrolling over 3,000 students annually in traditional mobility programs, including study abroad, internship, service-learning, and research opportunities, and has developed a growing portfolio of online global learning programs that enroll an additional 1,700+ students each academic year. The office has a strong commitment to professional development. You will have opportunities both internally and externally to grow your skill set and knowledge base.

The Coordinator will be assigned to a portfolio of international and domestic programs and will be responsible for managing their full life cycle, from the proposal stage through to the collection of program evaluations. This position works primarily with faculty, university administration and service providers and will report to the Assistant Director. Student contact is indirect and limited.


Position Salary Range:

$52,000/year


Essential Duties:

  • Works closely and collaboratively with faculty member(s), to facilitate, develop and finalize individualized custom program proposals including, but not limited to: budgets, logistics, housing, transportation, health & safety requirements, excursions and curriculum.
  • Facilitates and prepares, with faculty member(s), the development and maintenance of a program budget and associated course fee(s), prepares disbursements, proposals, recommendations and approvals where appropriate and ensures adherence to and control of budget items.
  • Requests bids from providers, facilitates contract negotiations with identified vendor(s); prepares all applicable contracts for each program to ensure achievement of stated outcomes and requirements.
  • Acts as primary contact between third party vendors and faculty; reviews providers’ bid responses to provide guidance/recommendations to faculty identifying differences that may enhance the program from both a content and expense perspective.
  • Plans, prepares, launches and administers associated web brochure(s) to promote program including descriptive information, cost, program length/timing and application process. Reviews submitted applications for eligibility criteria, accepts/denies students, and aids in the achievement of required minimum participants.
  • Prepares Memoranda of Understanding (MOU) and Scope of Work for vendors; in conjunction with Risk Management, OGC and Associate Director International Health, Safety and Security evaluates new providers for compliance with ASU standards/requirements.
  • Working in conjunction with faculty, facilitates promotion of programs, holds informational sessions, creates flyers for programs; assists in the planning of Global Education Office events throughout the year to increase awareness and promote program opportunities to students, faculty, and colleges.
  • Working with faculty, coordinates, organizes and delivers pre-departure orientations for students, both in person and virtually; monitors virtual pre-departure orientation required for all students.
  • Advises students on program specifics, funding options, and application process; performs follow up as needed to ensure students have the opportunity to complete process; withdraws students as requested.
  • Performs other duties and special projects as assigned by supervisor.

  • Experience working with college/university faculty members or VIP customers/clients

ASU GEO is a leader in global education, enrolling over 3,000 students annually in traditional mobility programs, including study abroad, internship, service-learning, and research opportunities, and has developed a growing portfolio of online global learning programs that enroll an additional 1,700+ students each academic year.

  • Vendor Management.
  • Ordering and Invoicing.
  • Inventory Management, stocking, ordering, and establish par levels to minimize waste.
  • Management of service desk portal for all service lines (across positions).
  • Management of the Coupa system for invoice payments.

Offboarding

  • Clear any items left behind.
  • Clean workstations/offices.

  • Track and manage regular maintenance contract for all equipment and inspections with appropriate vendors.
  • Self-perform maintenance on equipment (daily coffee machine rinses, Molekule air filter replacements, etc.).

Incident Management (Break/Fix)

  • Investigate and troubleshoot miscellaneous facility and office items (height adjustment desks not working, loose doorhandle, etc.).

  • Upon request provide desktop sit/stand units, reorient workstations, add whiteboards, hang artwork.
  • Coordinate with outside vendors for support, when required.

Experience: Minimum of 1 year of work experience required; hospitality, food & beverage, hotel, or client service experience preferred. Experience in professional office hospitality or conference services is a plus.

title: Inpatient Coding Specialist II (Remote)
description:
If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.

Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)

This is a Stanford Health Care job.

A Brief Overview
Requires review of medical record documentation to accurately assign International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10-CM/PCS), as well as assignment of the Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) / All Patient Refined - Diagnosis Related Group (APR-DRG) and abstracts specific data elements for each account in compliance with federal and state regulations. This position codes the majority of patient types of inpatient records, including more complex cases such as Intensive Care. Follows the Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting, the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) Standards of Ethical Coding, as well as all American Hospital Association (AHA) Coding Clinic guidance. Follows Stanford Health Care policies and procedures and maintains required quality and productivity standards. Reviews, abstracts and assigns accurate and ethical ICD-10-CM/PCS codes to inpatient services. Ensures compliance with third party, State and Federal regulations. Reviews, analyzes and abstracts physician/other documentation for diagnoses, procedures, and other services provided. Obtains missing information and/or clarifies existing information. Completes volume of work from work queues per departmental productivity standards. Groups codes and completed product into payment group. Analyzes information for optimal and approprite reimbursement. Ensures compliance with all appropriate coding, billing and data collection regulations and procedures. Uses appropriate software to validate information. Utilizes Epic, 3M Coding and Reimbursement System (Encoder), 3M CDIS, 3M Audit Expert, MS Office, and other software as appropriate to compile and validate medical information.

Locations
Stanford Health Care

What you will do

  • Reviews medical record documentation and accurately assigns appropriate ICD-10 diagnosis and procedure codes, leading to the assignment of the correct Medicare Severity-Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) or All Patient Refined Diagnosis Related Group (APR-DRG). The Inpatient Coding Specialist II is responsible for verification of the patient's discharge disposition, assignment of the correct sources of admission for state regulation reporting purposes, and ensuring the appropriate present on admission (POA) indicators are assigned to each code. The assigned codes must support the reason for the visit that is documented by the provider in order to support the care provided.
  • Correctly abstracts required data per facility specifications.
  • Responsible for monitoring Discharged Not Billed accounts, and as a team, ensuring timely, compliant processing of inpatient accounts through the revenue cycle.
  • Collaborates with Clinical Documentation Specialists (CDSs) and members of the medical staff to ensure completeness of documentation in the medical records so that appropriate codes, and, ultimately, the correct Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) may be assigned.
  • Responsible for ensuring accuracy and maintaining established quality and productivity standards.
  • Demonstrates a high degree of independence in performance of responsibilities, working effectively without direct supervision. Exhibits strong time management, problem solving and communication skills.
  • Possesses critical thinking, good judgment and decision making skills.
  • Demonstrates excellent written and oral communication skills.
  • Remains abreast of current Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) requirements as well as Correct Coding Initiative (CCI) edits, Hospital Acquired Conditions (HACs), Patient Safety Indicators (PSIs), and when applicable, National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs,) including the addition of appropriate modifiers to ensure a clean claim the first time through.
  • Maintains competency and accuracy while utilizing tools of the trade such as the 3M encoder, 3M Audit Expert process (3M AES), 3M Clinical Documentation Improvement System (3M CDIS) and abstracting systems, as well as all reference materials.
  • Follows all established Stanford Health Care policies and procedures.
  • Attends required system, hospital and departmental meetings and educational sessions as established by leadership, as well as completion of required annual learning programs, to ensure continued education and growth.


Education Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or GED equivalent


Experience Qualifications

  • Five (5) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience


Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Successful completion of the Coder Proficiency Exam (pre-hire)
  • Ability to adapt to and deal with change and ambiguity
  • Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, work independently and meet deadlines
  • Ability to comply with the American Health Information Management Association’s Code of Ethics and Standards and apply Uniform Hospital Discharge Data Set (UHDDS) standards
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships
  • Ability to manage, organize, prioritize, multi-task and adapt to changing priorities
  • Ability to solve technical and non-technical problems
  • Ability to utilize the ICD-10-CM/PCS and CPT-4 coding conventions to code medical record entries; abstract information from medical records; read medical record documentation; assign accurate codes for grouping of MS-DRGs and APR-DRGs
  • Ability to work effectively through and with others
  • Knowledge of diagnosis/procedure DRG grouping schemes such as MS-DRGs and APR-DRGs
  • Knowledge of health information systems for computer application to medical records
  • Ability to foster effective working relationships and build consensus
  • Ability to work effectively with individuals at all levels of the organization
  • Knowledge of CCI (Correct Coding Initiatives) and CMS compliance issues
  • Knowledge of computer systems and software used in functional area
  • Knowledge of standards and regulations pertaining to the maintenance of patient medical records; medical records coding systems; medical terminology; anatomy and physiology and study of diseases


Licenses and Certifications

  • RHIA - Registered Health Information Administrator or
  • RHIT - Registered Health Information Technician or
  • CCS - Certified Coding Specialist


These principles apply to ALL employees:

SHC Commitment to Providing an Exceptional Patient & Family Experience

Stanford Health Care sets a high standard for delivering value and an exceptional experience for our patients and families. Candidates for employment and existing employees must adopt and execute C-I-CARE standards for all of patients, families and towards each other. C-I-CARE is the foundation of Stanford’s patient-experience and represents a framework for patient-centered interactions. Simply put, we do what it takes to enable and empower patients and families to focus on health, healing and recovery. You will do this by executing against our three experience pillars, from the patient and family’s perspective:


  • Know Me: Anticipate my needs and status to deliver effective care

  • Coordinate for Me: Own the complexity of my care through coordination

title: DUI/DWI Investigations Analyst
description:
Concept Solutions, LLC is seeking a detail-oriented and analytical DUI/DWI Investigations Analyst to support the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) under its C3 Program.


This position supports the FAA's Office of Security and Hazardous Materials Safety (ASH), specifically the Regulatory Investigations Division, in conducting preliminary investigations involving alcohol- and drug-related motor vehicle actions reported by certificated airmen.


The successful candidate will play an important role in supporting regulatory compliance and aviation safety by reviewing investigative records, researching information from multiple sources, evaluating potential regulatory violations, and ensuring accurate documentation throughout the investigative process.


This opportunity is well suited for a professional with experience in investigations, regulatory compliance, law enforcement support, or administrative case management who enjoys detailed research, applying regulations, and managing cases from initial intake through resolution.


Investigative Case Management and Research


  • Receive, review, document, and process notification letters submitted by airmen concerning alcohol- or drug-related motor vehicle actions.
  • Establish and maintain accurate investigative case records in applicable FAA databases and case-management systems.
  • Research, request, and obtain driving histories, motor vehicle records, and other supporting documentation relevant to preliminary investigations.
  • Access and review FAA databases to obtain airman certification information and other records necessary to evaluate potential regulatory violations.
  • Monitor investigative progress, track outstanding documentation, prioritize cases, and initiate follow-up requests or reorder records as necessary.


Regulatory Compliance and Preliminary Investigations

  • Ensure investigative records and correspondence are handled accurately and with appropriate discretion.

title: Sr. Principal Engineer, Employee Experience (Hybrid - Seattle, WA)
description:
Job Description

At Nordstrom, we're committed to delivering outstanding customer experiences by harnessing the power of data. We are seeking a Sr. Principal Engineer - Employee Experience to join our Technology team. In this role you will define and drive the technical strategy, architecture, and engineering standards for the systems that power Nordstrom's financial operations, people process, and workplace collaboration. This work spans enterprise finance and ERP systems, HR and talent platforms, and the productivity and collaboration tools tens of thousands of Nordstrom employees rely on every day.


This is a strategic, influence-driven role that will shape how engineering teams design, secure, and scale the technology behind Finance, HR, and the Nordstrom workplace experience for years to come. You will collaborate with executives and leaders across Finance, HR, Nordstrom Technology, and business functions to translate enterprise priorities into technical roadmaps, establishing the architectural foundations that enable operational excellence, employee experience, and AI-enabled productivity. If you're passionate about enterprise engineering and ready to make a lasting impact on how Nordstrom works, we want to hear from you.

A day in the life…

  • Define Enterprise Technology Strategy: Develop and communicate a multi-year technical vision and roadmap for Finance, HR, Productivity and Collaboration systems, aligned with enterprise architecture, cloud strategy, and AI ambitions.
  • Architect Core Business Systems: Own architecture and design patterns across financial systems (ERP, procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, financial planning), HR systems (Human Capital Management, commissions, recruiting, work force management), and productivity/collaboration platforms (M365, messaging, workflow, and service management tools). Establish SaaS integration patterns, API standards, event schema and data contracts connecting these systems to the rest of the enterprise.
  • Lead Complex, Cross-Functional Initiatives: Lead design and delivery of large-scale initiatives, including platform modernizations, vendor migrations, technical debt deprecations and system consolidations, that span multiple engineering teams and business functions.
  • Ensure Security, Compliance, and Resilience: Define architecture patterns for identity, access control, and data protection appropriate to sensitive financial and HR data. Partner with security, privacy, and compliance teams to meet PCI, SOC, data privacy, and audit requirements.
  • Enable AI and Automation: Identify opportunities to apply AI, AI Native automation, SaaS AI features and self-service capabilities to finance, HR, and workplace processes. Guide teams evaluating AI-enabled tools, including conversational assistants, intelligent document processing, and workflow automation, for productivity and collaboration use cases.
  • Build Engineering Culture and Talent: Set technical standards and best practices across the Finance, HR, and Productivity & Collaboration engineering portfolio. Mentor senior and principal engineers, participate in architecture reviews, and advise on technical career growth and promotions.

You own this if you have…

  • Extensive Experience: 15+ years in software engineering, systems architecture, or platform engineering, with demonstrated progression to strategic, enterprise-scope technical leadership.
  • Domain Breadth: Hands-on experience architecting or engineering solutions across enterprise finance systems (ERP, GL, procure-to-pay), HR/HCM platforms (e.g., Workday or similar), and productivity/collaboration tools (e.g., Microsoft 365, ServiceNow, Slack).
  • Integration and Data Expertise: Deep expertise in enterprise integration patterns, APIs, event-driven architecture, and the data flows connecting core business systems.
  • Strategic Influence: Demonstrated ability to lead through influence rather than authority, building consensus with engineering, product, and business stakeholders.
  • Security and Compliance Fluency: Working knowledge of the security, privacy, and regulatory considerations (Segregation of Duties, SOC, data privacy, access governance) relevant to financial and employee data systems.
  • Platform Proficiency: Expertise with multiple cloud platforms (AWS & GCP preferred), modern application architectures, and enterprise SaaS ecosystems sufficient to evaluate build-vs-buy tradeoffs.
  • Business Acumen: Ability to connect technical architecture to business outcomes and communicate value to executive stakeholders across Finance, HR, and Technology.
  • Collaborative Leadership: Track record of developing engineering talent and building cross-functional partnerships across teams you don't directly manage.

The Role

Do you find your purpose in empowering others? As a Café Ambassador, you are the face of Capital One’s mission to change banking for good. We’ve broken the mold of traditional banking—you won’t be found behind a teller line or a glass window. Instead, you’ll move throughout the Café, bridging the gap between digital innovation and human connection.

In this role, you’ll act as a high-end service specialist and a guide to digital banking. You aren't just serving a community; you’re building one by bringing Capital One’s mission to life within a vibrant, modern community hub.

What You’ll Actually Do

  • Be a Natural Connector: Proactively engage with guests in a high-energy environment that serves as both a community space and a local coffee shop. (Note: You are a banking guide, not a barista—you won’t be serving coffee!)
  • Serve as a Brand Advocate: You’ll share the value of Capital One’s products and services through genuine conversation rather than transactions. Because we focus on the guest experience, this role is free from traditional sales goals or high-pressure tactics. Your success is measured by the quality of the connection, not a quota.
  • Simplify the Complex: Guide customers through our digital ecosystem, helping them master mobile tools and troubleshooting tech challenges with ease.
  • Facilitate Purposeful Impact: Host and support local events that promote financial health. You’ll act as a brand steward, working within the framework of Capital One’s established programs and strategic community partnerships to ensure our impact is professional, focused, and effective.
  • Advocate & Problem-Solve: You’ll advocate for our customers, problem solve, and own issue resolution in alignment with compliance and regulatory requirements. Handling complaints and/or escalated situations is very important, and de-escalation may be a complex part of your role supporting our customers—we’ll ensure you’re supported with the tools, resources, and experience to ensure you’re up for the challenge!

This isn't just a job—it’s work with a mission. title: Remote WebLogic Middleware Administrator
location: Norwich, CT, United States of America
description:
What success looks like in this role:

Role Summary
The Senior WebLogic Middleware Administrator is responsible for the administration, configuration, maintenance, security remediation, compliance management, automation, troubleshooting, and operational support of enterprise Oracle WebLogic platforms and supporting infrastructure. The role focuses on maintaining highly available, secure, and compliant environments while using automation to improve operational efficiency, reduce manual effort, and ensure consistency across middleware services.


Key Responsibilities

  • Administer and support Oracle WebLogic Server environments, including domain, Admin Server, Managed Server, cluster, and Node Manager configuration.
  • Support Oracle HTTP Server and Apache, plus Tomcat and IIS as needed.
  • Perform security remediation, vulnerability management, Oracle Critical Patch Update (CPU) patching, upgrades, and compliance validation.
  • Manage SSL/TLS certificates, keystores, truststores, LDAP, Kerberos, Active Directory integration, SSO, and WebLogic security realms and authentication providers.
  • Administer Linux, Solaris, and Windows servers supporting middleware environments.
  • Design, develop, and maintain automation for WebLogic administration, patching, compliance validation, and operational support using Shell, Python, and WLST (Jython) scripting.
  • Automate deployments, domain and configuration updates, certificate management, reporting, and system health checks.
  • Support CI/CD deployment processes and enterprise automation tools where applicable.
  • Perform performance monitoring, JVM tuning, data source and connection pool tuning, thread and heap dump analysis, troubleshooting, and root cause analysis.
  • Execute change management, incident management, and service restoration activities.
  • Maintain documentation, procedures, audit evidence, and compliance records.

You will be successful in this role if you have:

Required Qualifications

  • BA/BS degree and 6-8 years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 6+ years of middleware administration experience, with a primary focus on enterprise WebLogic environments.
  • Experience in security remediation, vulnerability management, and audit compliance.
  • Demonstrated experience developing automation solutions that improve operational efficiency and reduce manual effort.
  • US Citizenship required and ability to obtain a government security clearance.

Required Technical Skills

  • Oracle WebLogic Server, Oracle HTTP Server, Apache, Tomcat, IIS
  • WLST (Jython), Shell, Python, XML, HTML, Awk, Sed, Curl
  • Linux (RHEL, SUSE), Solaris, AIX, and Windows Server administration
  • SSL/TLS, LDAP, Active Directory, Kerberos, SSO, security hardening
  • REST API integration (including WebLogic REST management), task scheduling, and operational scripting
  • Oracle database (JDBC, data sources, GridLink/multi data source configuration)
  • JVM tuning, monitoring, and performance analysis

Preferred Qualifications

  • Oracle Fusion Middleware, Coherence, or SOA Suite exposure
  • Kafka, Zookeeper, Artifactory, WordPress, ServiceNow, or Remedy administration
  • Ansible, Jenkins, Git, GitLab CI/CD, or similar tools
  • Experience supporting security audits and compliance frameworks
  • Working exposure to IBM WebSphere (a plus, not required)

title: Assistant Manager General Ledger
description:
JLL empowers you to shape a brighter way.

Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology for our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people and empowering them to thrive, grow meaningful careers and to find a place where they belong. Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades or technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, join our team as we help shape a brighter way forward.

Context & Purpose:

JLL Business Services (JBS) operates in a matrixed global environment supporting multiple clusters across AMER, APAC & EMEA regions. Employees are expected to combine operational excellence during close cycles with strong analytical capabilities, stakeholder partnership, process governance, automation adoption and continuous improvement. The organization values ownership, transparency, collaboration, controllership mindset, problem solving and leadership at all levels.


Duties and Responsibilities:

The focus of the role will be upon -

Completes assigned close tasks to the close calendar and checklist; confirms task completion in the tracker; flags risks to deadlines to the reviewer before the due date; supports cut-off and accrual data collection.

Fully accountable to the GL month end close (MEC) including Balance Sheet reconciliation preparation

Act as a strategic bridge between Business and executive leadership. Align departmental priorities with company-wide growth targets, analyze performance data, and advise leaders on operational improvements.

What the job involves:

P2 is the core ownership level of the R2R role framework, sitting between the P1 &P3 roles, with independent ownership of close activities and balance sheet accounts. This document defines the P2 Assistant Manager General Ledger role within the R2R function, which delivers Month-End Close (MEC), Reconciliations, Financial Reporting, Governance and Continuous Improvement for global accounting operations. The role goes beyond execution: it investigates root causes, resolves issues without close supervision, performs meaningful variance and trend analysis, and partners regularly with entity controllers and business partners. P2s review the work of P1 analysts, support their onboarding, and begin to contribute to process improvement and automation. Success is measured by on-time, accurate delivery of owned deliverables, reconciliation health and the quality of insight provided to stakeholders

Detailed job responsibilities are mentioned in below table:

Key Responsibilities:

Area

Responsibilities at this level

Month-End Close (MEC)

Independently plans and executes owned close activities (accruals, provisions, intercompany, cut-off and allocations) to the calendar; tracks dependencies; escalates risks early with proposed solutions; contributes to post-close lessons learned.

Journal Entry Management

Prepares standard and moderately complex journals (accruals, reclassifications, provisions, FX revaluation) with full support; reviews journals prepared by P1s; ensures compliance with policy and approval thresholds.

Balance Sheet Reconciliations

Owns reconciliations for assigned accounts, including medium and high-risk accounts; ensures timely preparation, certification and evidence in Account Reconciliation Cloud Services (ARCS); investigates and resolves reconciling items; reviews P1 reconciliations.

Open Item Management

Manages aging and clearance of open items across owned accounts; drives action with owners in the business and finance; escalates items beyond threshold with root cause and a clearance plan; reports the aging trend.

Financial Reporting

Prepares and reviews management and statutory reporting inputs, schedules and disclosures; ensures reporting accuracy and consistency with the ledger; supports consolidation and group reporting submissions.

Variance Analysis

Performs month-on-month, actual-versus-budget and forecast variance analysis; identifies drivers and root causes; writes concise commentary for controllers and business partners; recommends corrective actions.

Governance & Controls

Operates and evidence key controls for owned processes; performs self-assessments; identifies control gaps and proposes remediation; ensures adherence to policy, SOX or equivalent requirements and segregation of duties.

Audit Support

Prepares audit documentation for owned accounts; responds to internal and external auditors directly on routine queries; supports remediation of findings.

Stakeholder Management

Acts as the day-to-day contact for entity controllers and business partners on owned areas; sets expectations on timelines and data needs; manages escalations on a first-line basis.

Continuous Improvement

Identifies recurring errors, bottlenecks and manual effort in owned processes; implements local improvements; updates procedures and desk instructions; participates in Lean or Six Sigma activities.

Digital & Automation Adoption

Maximises Account Reconciliation Cloud Services (ARCS) auto-matching and workflow features; builds and uses Excel and Power BI tools to improve analysis; documents requirements for automation candidates and supports testing and user acceptance.

Required Technical Skills:

Skill

Expected capability

General Accounting

Strong command of the accounting cycle including accruals, provisions, fixed assets, intercompany, FX and cut-off; applies sound judgement on standard transactions.

IFRS / US GAAP

Working knowledge of the standards that affect owned accounts (revenue, leases, provisions, financial instruments, FX); applies policy correctly and recognises when to seek technical guidance.

MEC Management

Plans and manages own close deliverables, dependencies and cut-off; anticipates delays and recovers the schedule.

Balance Sheet Reconciliations

Applies reconciliation policy, risk ratings and aging thresholds; resolves complex reconciling items; reviews reconciliations prepared by others.

Financial Reporting

Prepares management and statutory reporting schedules; understands the link between the ledger, consolidation and published reporting.

Variance Analysis

Decomposes variances into price, volume, timing and one-off drivers; challenges explanations; writes clear commentary.

Journal Review

Reviews journals for accuracy, support, period, account coding and policy compliance; identifies unusual patterns.

Internal Controls

Understands control design and operating effectiveness; executes and evidences key controls; identifies and reports gaps.

Account Reconciliation Cloud Services (ARCS)

Proficient in reconciliations, transaction matching, journal and task management modules; configures simple rules and formats with guidance.

SAP / Oracle / ERP Systems

Proficient in transactions, reporting and master data for owned processes; extracts and reconciles data independently.

Excel (Advanced)

Builds structured analyses using XLOOKUP or INDEX-MATCH, pivot tables, Power Query and conditional logic; creates reusable, auditable workbooks.

Power BI

Builds simple reports and uses existing dashboards to monitor KPIs and aging; foundational understanding of data models.

Behavioural Competency:

Competency

Observable expectation

Learning Agility

Quickly masters new entities, systems and policy changes; seeks feedback and stretches into P3-level topics.

Adaptability

Flexes across priorities, close pressures and changing requirements without a drop in quality.

Collaboration

Works effectively across R2R, AP, AR, Treasury, Tax and the business; shares knowledge proactively.

Customer Orientation

Anticipates stakeholder needs, communicates proactively on status and meets service commitments.

Accountability

Owns outcomes for assigned accounts and deadlines; takes responsibility for quality and corrects issues without prompting.

Decision Making

Makes sound decisions within policy and delegated authority; weighs risk and escalates matters beyond own remit.

Continuous Improvement Mindset

Actively looks for waste and rework, tests ideas and shares improvements with the team.

Communication Skills:

Competency

Observable expectation

Executive communication

Provides concise written updates to controllers and team leadership; highlights the issue, the impact and the ask.

Presentation skills

Presents analysis and status in team and stakeholder meetings in a structured manner.

Storytelling with financial data

Explains what the numbers say, why they moved and what to do next in plain language.

Ability to challenge constructively

Questions unusual transactions, missing support or unreasonable deadlines respectfully and with evidence.

Global stakeholder engagement

Works effectively with controllers and partners in multiple regions (SEA, ANZ, WA, MENA); adapts style to cultural and time zone differences.

To apply you need:

Item

Requirement

Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance or Commerce; Master's degree or MBA is an advantage.

Certifications

Part-qualified or newly qualified CA, CPA, ACCA or CMA preferred; Account Reconciliation Cloud Services (ARCS) certification, Power BI (PL-300) or Lean Six Sigma Green Belt are an advantage.

Years of experience

7 years of progressive accounting experience, including at least 2 years in R2R, GL or financial reporting within a shared services or multinational environment.

Systems exposure

Hands-on experience with SAP or Oracle, Account Reconciliation Cloud Services (ARCS) and advanced Excel; Power BI exposure preferred.

Process exposure

Has completed multiple full close cycles and owned reconciliations through audit.

40

title: 2027 Summer Intern – Research and Development – Vehicle Aerodynamics and Machine Learning
location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
description:
Job Description

The Role:

As a 2027 Summer Intern on the Vehicle Aerodynamics and Machine Learning team, you will work at the intersection of physics-based vehicle simulation, computational fluid dynamics, scientific machine learning, and aerodynamic design optimization.


You will support research that uses CFD and AI/ML to improve vehicle aerodynamic performance, accelerate design exploration, and enable more efficient development of next-generation vehicles. The work may include analyzing vehicle flow fields, developing data-driven aerodynamic models, evaluating design concepts, and translating research results into practical engineering tools.


This role is intended for an inquisitive, technically motivated student who enjoys applying engineering fundamentals and modern computational methods to complex problems. You will work with experienced researchers and cross-functional engineering partners while developing your skills in vehicle aerodynamics, simulation, machine learning, data analysis, and technical communication.


GM’s related research includes high-fidelity CFD, aerodynamic drag and efficiency improvement, physics-based AI models, surrogate modeling, transfer learning, and rapid aerodynamic feedback from vehicle geometry or design data.


The Team:

The Energy and Propulsion Systems Research team conducts applied research intended to improve vehicle efficiency, performance, range, cost, and sustainability. The team collaborates with researchers, vehicle-development organizations, engineering groups, universities, technology partners, and industry leaders to identify and develop technologies with potential value to GM.


You will work in a multidisciplinary environment that may include vehicle aerodynamicists, CFD specialists, data scientists, machine-learning researchers, vehicle designers, optimization experts, and engineers from propulsion, thermal, body, chassis, and vehicle-performance organizations.


The internship experience may also include innovation challenges, interactions with industry leaders, cross-functional networking events, technical presentations, and community-service activities.


What You’ll Do:

  • Support vehicle aerodynamics research involving external flow, aerodynamic drag, lift, downforce, cooling airflow, and vehicle efficiency.
  • Set up, run, monitor, and post-process CFD simulations for vehicle and component-level aerodynamic studies.
  • Prepare simulation geometry, meshes, boundary conditions, design variables, and analysis workflows.
  • Analyze aerodynamic coefficients, pressure distributions, velocity fields, wake structures, flow features, and other performance metrics.
  • Build and curate datasets from CFD simulations, experimental results, vehicle geometry, and design variables.
  • Develop, train, test, and evaluate machine-learning or surrogate models for aerodynamic quantities and flow-field predictions.
  • Investigate physics-informed, data-driven, reduced-order, graph-based, or other scientific machine-learning approaches relevant to vehicle aerodynamics.
  • Apply data preprocessing, feature engineering, dimensionality reduction, model selection, hyperparameter tuning, and validation techniques.
  • Evaluate model accuracy, robustness, generalization, uncertainty, and limitations across vehicle geometries and operating conditions.
  • Compare ML predictions with CFD, wind-tunnel, experimental, or other trusted engineering results.
  • Support design-of-experiments, surrogate-based optimization, sensitivity studies, and aerodynamic shape exploration.
  • Develop Python-based scripts, tools, and workflows to automate simulation setup, data processing, model training, visualization, and reporting.
  • Help identify opportunities to reduce analysis time and enable earlier aerodynamic feedback during vehicle design.
  • Document assumptions, methods, data sources, model configurations, results, limitations, and recommendations.
  • Create clear plots, visualizations, technical reports, presentations, and demonstrations for engineering and research audiences.
  • Collaborate with researchers and cross-functional partners to define technical questions, review results, and recommend next steps.
  • Present technical findings and participate in innovation, networking, and professional-development activities.

Required Qualifications:

  • Pursuit of an advanced degree (MS or PhD) in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, computational engineering, computer science, applied mathematics, physics, data science, or a related technical discipline.
  • Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Coursework, research, or project experience in fluid mechanics, vehicle aerodynamics, computational fluid dynamics, turbulence modeling, numerical methods, optimization, or heat transfer.
  • Experience with Python, MATLAB, C++, or comparable programming languages.
  • Experience with NumPy, pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar scientific-computing and machine-learning libraries.
  • Familiarity with CFD, CAE, CAD, meshing, visualization, Linux, high-performance computing, or engineering software workflows.
  • Experience developing or applying machine-learning models to scientific, engineering, physical-simulation, or time-series data.
  • Familiarity with surrogate modeling, physics-informed machine learning, graph neural networks, neural operators, transfer learning, uncertainty quantification, or model explainability.
  • Experience with design-of-experiments, parameter studies, optimization, or automated engineering workflows.
  • Ability to evaluate data quality, identify modeling limitations, and distinguish physically meaningful results from numerical or data artifacts.
  • Experience communicating technical results through reports, presentations, plots, code documentation, or demonstrations.
  • Strong analytical, written, and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with researchers and cross-functional engineering teams.

title: Manager, GPO Delivery and Optimization
description:
Manager, GPO Delivery and Optimization


What you will be doing:

The Manager Delivery and Optimization owns GPO contract delivery for an assigned portfolio of member accounts — from activation through renewal. This is an execution role: build the plan, run it, and drive it to a result. The Manager Delivery and Optimization leverages data and Premier's technology to tell a clear story about value, manages contract performance to ensure members actually realize it, and operates as a self-starter who figures out how to solve problems without being told how.

Delivery Execution and Value Creation – 50%

  • Owns the GPO portfolio lifecycle: tier activation and timing, renewals/expirations, distributor contract audits, roster accuracy, and admin fee revenue accuracy
  • Coordinates cross-functionally with GPO contracting, portfolio SMEs, and analytics teams to remove blockers and keep delivery on track
  • Owns the account's project plan, timeline, and RACI; escalates and resolves issues before they become problems
  • Executes contract activations, amendments, and renewals directly with distributors and suppliers; drives category adoption conversations to a decision
  • Manages contract performance across the account's category portfolio, ensuring optimal utilization and value realization
  • Leverages data analysis — through Premier's technology, AI, and Power BI tools and partnerships with Premier's analytics teams — to synthesize findings into recommendations that drive measurable value

  • Develops the account's annual growth forecast and contributes to the business review process, in partnership with their manager or COE Coach
  • Executes toward KPIs and targets set by SCO/GPO Ops leadership — contract growth, penetration, and member savings/value
  • Aligns with internal partners — Rx, Food, and Portfolio Advisors — on execution of the account's category strategy
  • Assures a regular cadence of complete member data submissions (PO, invoice, AP, capital plans, and other required data types) to support accurate analytics and GPO growth/penetration tracking
  • Leverages contract analytics from the MVE and other Premier analytics resources to help members model contracting scenarios — costs, behaviors, market share, and lower-cost alternatives

Supply Chain Relationship Management – 35%

  • Provides day-to-day guidance to member stakeholders as a trusted advisor
  • Builds a working understanding of each member's goals (savings targets, budget gaps, new service line launches), current capabilities, and pressure points — and shapes engagement around what that specific member needs, not a generic playbook
  • Acts as the account's GPO quarterback when no other dedicated GPO team resources are assigned to the account, coordinating all GPO-related activity on the member's behalf

title: Director National Accounts-GPO/Market Access
description:
The Director, National Accounts, will be a critical commercial leader responsible for developing and executing the company's national account strategy in preparation for and following the launch of the organization's first commercial product. This individual will lead relationships and negotiations with key healthcare stakeholders including Payer (GPOs), Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs), and National Health Plans across the Commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid books of business


As a member of the Market Access leadership team, the Director, National Accounts will play a highly visible role in shaping pricing, contracting, reimbursement, and access strategies that support successful product adoption and patient access. This role requires both strategic vision and hands-on execution, thriving in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial biotech environment.

Primary Relationships

  • Within Henlius: Collaborates closely with Sales, Marketing, Finance, Medical and Legal.
  • Outside Henlius: Builds and maintains relationships with top Payer GPOs, PBMs, and National Health Plans.

The activities of the Director, National Accounts will include, but are not limited to:

National Account Strategy & Execution

  • Develop and implement a comprehensive national accounts strategy to support launch readiness and long-term commercial success.
  • Establish and manage executive-level relationships with key stakeholders across PBMs, GPOs, national and regional payers, specialty pharmacies.
  • Identify, prioritize, and secure formulary access opportunities that align with corporate objectives.
  • Serve as the primary commercial lead for assigned national accounts, creating account-specific business plans and performance objectives.

Payer & GPO/PBM Contracting

  • Lead negotiations and management of rebate, formulary, and value-based agreements with PBMs and health plans.
  • Collaborate with Pricing, Market Access, Finance, Legal, and Compliance teams to develop contract strategies and evaluate financial implications.
  • Monitor payer coverage policies, competitive dynamics, and market trends to proactively adjust account strategies.
  • Support pull-through initiatives to maximize access and utilization within contracted organizations.

Launch Readiness & Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Serve as a key contributor to launch planning and commercialization efforts.
  • Provide account insights to support forecasting, pricing strategy, patient access programs, and brand planning.
  • Collaborate closely with Commercial, Medical Affairs, Trade, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal, Compliance, and Executive Leadership teams.
  • Develop processes, tools, and analytics to support national account management in a growing organization.

Leadership

  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer focus, and excellence.
  • Contribute to broader commercial strategy and organizational development initiatives.
  • Demonstrate the value of our products, services and the Henlius organization. Manage the interactions of executive-to-executive meetings
  • Facilitates communication with field personnel and leadership on customer strategies and market trends.
  • Responsible for the development of the account plan and the overall account strategy to include all stakeholders while working collaboratively to match customers’ needs and expectations.
  • Participate in Business reviews as a subject matter expert on assigned accounts.
  • Represent Henlius at Key National Conferences and Congress

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, specialty pharmaceutical, or healthcare organizations.
  • Minimum 5+ years of direct national account management experience with responsibility for Payer GPOs, PBMs, National Health Plans (to include government payers VA, DoD, and Medicaid).

Preferred Qualifications

Please review the following job description:

The Problem Management Automation and Reliability Engineering - Senior Technology Operations Consultant works inside Problem Management with a primary focus on reducing toil. The role does double duty. You work live Problem Management alongside the Problem Managers, investigating recurring problems, contributing to root cause analysis and post-incident reviews, and helping drive corrective actions to closure. You also find the repetitive, rules-based steps in that work and replace them with automation. Because you do the work yourself, you know which steps cost the most time and which are worth fixing first.

The engineering side is hands-on. The consultant applies SRE practices to remove manual effort from Problem Management by writing scripts, engineering applications, and design possible ServiceNow workflows. The consultant also builds ServiceNow dashboards that show recurring failure patterns, corrective action status, and control effectiveness to technology leaders. Success is measured in hours of manual effort removed, shorter cycle time from incident to root cause, and better data quality in Problem records.

The role works with Problem Management, Incident Management, Major Incident Management, Event Management, and the technology towers that own production services. The best fit is someone with a network, cloud, server, or infrastructure troubleshooting background who has already turned that experience into scripts, automation, and dashboards. Solutions must be secure, auditable, and supportable in a regulated financial institution.

For this opportunity: Truist will not sponsor an applicant for work visa status or employment authorization, nor will we offer any immigration-related support for this position (including, but not limited to H-1B, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, F-1 CPT, J-1, TN-1 or TN-2, E-3, O-1, or future sponsorship for U.S. lawful permanent residence status.)

*** Role is NOT remote ***
*** In office expectations are 5 days per week. ***

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Following is a summary of the essential functions for this job. Other duties may be performed, both major and minor, which are not mentioned below. Specific activities may change from time to time.

  • Delivers on technology operations for an assigned area, working independently with limited supervision to achieve operational targets for performance, availability, and security of critical systems and infrastructure in line with established strategies.
  • Contributes to the development and maintenance of technology standards, runbooks, and governance patterns, applying them consistently and providing guidance to reduce risk, support compliance, and improve how the job area operates.
  • Leads large or complex initiatives within the job area by planning, designing, and implementing technology solutions and operational improvements, delegating work to lowerlevel technical professionals and reviewing their deliverables.
  • Demonstrates innovative influence by evaluating and piloting emerging technologies, automation, and optimization techniques, and implementing changes that deliver measurable improvements in efficiency, reliability, or supportability.
  • Provides day-to-day technical guidance, coaching, and training to other engineers and technical professionals, including design reviews, troubleshooting support, and sharing best practices and patterns.
  • Translates job area and senior leadership objectives into practical technical plans and roadmaps for the assigned scope, offering informed recommendations that help shape goals and contribute to new or enhanced products and services.
  • Monitors and analyzes operational metrics, logs, and observability data for owned services, using insights to identify issues and drive continuous improvement initiatives with major impact on jobarea results.
  • Serves as a key technical contact for vendors, partners, and adjacent teams on assigned solutions or services, providing input on design and product choices and ensuring they fit operational and architectural requirements.
  • May lead high‑priority incident response by identifying issues, triaging, coordinating restoration efforts, and minimizing business impact while driving effective post‑incident reviews.
  • Diagnose and resolve recurring problems, collaborating across teams to implement permanent fixes and strengthen overall system reliability.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Bachelor’s degree Information Technology, Computer Science, a related technical discipline, or equivalent education, training, and work-related experience.
  • Minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in technology operations.
  • Deep expertise in IT infrastructure, cloud technologies, security, compliance, and risk management.
  • Proven track record in technology governance, strategic planning, and operational excellence.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on Problem Management experience, including root cause analysis, 5 Whys, post-incident reviews, corrective action tracking, and trend analysis of recurring incidents.
  • Technical troubleshooting background in network, cloud, server, or infrastructure administration, with a record of diagnosing complex production failures.
  • Python scripting (or PowerShell or Bash) to automate data collection, validation, routing, and reporting, including work with REST APIs.
  • ServiceNow experience building dashboards, reports, and workflows, including Performance Analytics or Flow Designer, and working knowledge of the Incident, Problem, and Change data model.
  • Site reliability engineering practices, including toil reduction, SLOs and SLIs, error budgets, operational readiness, and resilience patterns.
  • Experience building dashboards and decision-support tools in ServiceNow, Power BI, Tableau, Splunk, or similar platforms.
  • Experience with observability and event management platforms such as Splunk, Datadog, Dynatrace, or PagerDuty, including event correlation, deduplication, and noise reduction.
  • Experience automating operational procedures and runbooks.
  • Working knowledge of Git, code review, CI/CD, and release controls.
  • Experience using AI-assisted tools, including large language models, for classification, summarization, or analysis within appropriate governance and security controls.
  • Experience working in Rally, Jira, or similar backlog tools in an Agile delivery model.
  • Experience in a regulated environment where auditability, access controls, and technology-risk requirements shape how solutions are built.
  • Ability to make progress when requirements are incomplete, while stating assumptions, decision points, and acceptance criteria.
  • Ability to explain root cause, risk, and business impact clearly to executives and engineers.
  • ITIL certification or equivalent. Cloud or networking certifications such as AWS, Azure, or CCNA/CCNP are a plus.

description:

We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people and empowering them to thrive, grow meaningful careers and to find a place where they belong. Position Summary

The FDD Program Manager provides strategic leadership, governance oversight, and cross-functional execution for the lifecycle and steady-state operations of the organization's Fault Detection and Diagnostics infrastructure across its corporate real estate portfolio. This role acts as a primary advisor to global smart building and technology teams, helping to shape the overarching governance framework and long-term scaling strategy for predictive building technologies. The Program Manager owns portfolio tracking mechanisms, risk management frameworks, and stakeholders' alignment to successfully transition facilities into data-driven, Condition-based Maintenance (CbM) regimes.

Core Responsibilities

  • Program Governance & Portfolio Alignment: Establish and oversee standardized program tracking dashboards, formal risk frameworks (Risks, Issues, Changes, and Decisions), and progress update cadences to maintain absolute execution rigor.

  • Scalable Strategy Execution: Direct the end-to-end implementation process of digital building and diagnostics initiatives globally across corporate offices and leased properties.

  • Operational Strategy Evolution: Provide strategic guidance to enterprise smart building leadership to elevate global system requirements, refine site suitability assessment metrics, and build repeatable operational frameworks.

  • Stakeholder & Vendor Coordination: Serve as the chief coordination point for program updates. Lead regular alignment sessions, technical performance reviews, and progress tracking meetings with regional workplace service groups, internal operational teams, and third-party platform vendors.

  • Financial & Scope Management: Monitor execution variance against master budgets and contractual Scopes of Work. Evaluate technical variations and facilitate corporate approval paths for high-priority scope changes.

  • Continuous Improvement (Lessons Learned): Organize post-deployment reviews and workshops to integrate field findings back into standard execution playbooks, ensuring efficiency gains in subsequent development tranches.

title: Engineering Design group - Engine Team
location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
description:
Job Description

This role is categorized as hybrid. The selected candidate will be expected to work on-site at the Warren Tech Center at least three days per week, or as otherwise determined by the hiring leader.

  • This role is not eligible for relocation assistance.

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.


Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale."

About the Role:

General Motors is seeking an Engineering Designer to develop integrated, high-quality, manufacturable designs for the Engine space. In this role, you will help translate vehicle, propulsion, structural, manufacturing, and program requirements into robust virtual designs that support performance, safety, durability, serviceability, and production readiness.

The role is focused on complete Engine systems. You will own or support Siemens NX math models, design criteria, typical sections, clearance studies, subsystem integration, NX Analysis, material and mass data, design reviews, and on-time math releases.

You will work closely with the Design Manager, Design Lead Team, Design Release Engineer, fellow designers, engineering partners, manufacturing, joining, quality, suppliers, plant, program, and service teams to identify risks early, resolve integration issues, and deliver release-quality data through the Global Vehicle Development Process.

What you will do

  • Develop and maintain robust, accurate, and production-oriented Siemens NX parametric models for assigned components and subsystems.
  • Create virtual vehicle integration solutions aligned with program requirements, design principles, packaging constraints, design criteria, and subsystem interfaces.
  • Develop and refine NX criteria and typical sections using approved modeling methods and program standards.
  • Establish and control hard points, packaging zones, clearances, service access, and critical interfaces.
  • Apply structural design fundamentals, including stiffness, strength, fatigue, buckling, section efficiency, joints, materials, reinforcements, and local load introduction.
  • Evaluate primary and secondary load paths for durability, crash, support, and propulsion-related conditions.
  • Identify load introduction points, reactions, joints, discontinuities, weak links, and opportunities for efficient structural improvement.
  • Perform or support clearance, usage, configuration, and virtual studies across components, subsystems, and the complete vehicle.
  • Complete NX Analysis for assigned components or subsystems and use results appropriately to guide design decisions with support from Design Lead Team or senior designers as needed.
  • Apply GD&T, tolerance awareness, variation-management, and stack-up principles to support fit, function, joining, load transfer, and assembly.
  • Design for manufacturability and assembly from the beginning of the design process, considering process capability, tooling, fixturing, access, sequence, joining, weldability, inspection, repairability, and production variation.
  • Maintain accurate and traceable material, mass, specification, and related data within the math file.
  • Translate program and component requirements into clear design criteria, integration checks, verification expectations, and release deliverables.
  • Plan and execute work against design sync points, review milestones, release timing, and other Global Vehicle Development Process deliverables.
  • Deliver accurate, complete, and on-time math releases with clean CAD, correct interfaces, complete details, and minimal rework.
  • Use structured problem solving to resolve non-routine and moderately complex virtual integration issues.
  • Communicate design intent, load paths, integration risks, timing, decisions, and technical concerns clearly and proactively.
  • Track actions and issues through integration, analysis, reviews, release, build, validation, and verified closure.
  • Seek input early, support fellow designers, collaborate across functions, and share lessons learned and effective design practices.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of modeling methods, design reviews, checks, templates, workflows, and data quality.

Required qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, engineering technology, or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent experience.
  • Two to five years of experience in automotive or mechanical CAD, engineering design, or a related product-development environment.
  • Demonstrated experience using Siemens NX for parametric modeling, model organization, design intent, references, constraints, and model-quality practices.
  • Understanding of automotive or mechanical structural design and the ability to reason about load paths, stiffness, strength, joints, reinforcements, materials, and interfaces.
  • Experience with virtual integration, packaging, clearance studies, configurations, usage validation, or comparable design-integration activities.
  • Working knowledge of GD&T, tolerance concepts, and variation management.
  • Working knowledge of design for manufacturability and design for assembly.
  • Ability to interpret requirements, identify ambiguity or conflict, and maintain traceability from requirements through design, review, analysis, release, and issue closure.
  • Ability to complete assigned work accurately and on schedule while managing multiple interfaces and program commitments.
  • Strong technical communication, problem-solving, collaboration, ownership, and follow-through skills.
  • Willingness and ability to work onsite at the Warren Tech Center at least three days per week—Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday—or at another frequency determined by the manager.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience designing structural sheet-metal components, including stamping, forming, draw direction, flanges, hemming or joining interfaces, local reinforcements, springback, and process capability.
  • Knowledge of casting processes, including draft, wall thickness, ribs, fillets, porosity risk, machining, datum strategy, and process limitations.
  • Advanced Siemens NX experience, including complex surfacing, expressions, templates, checks, reusable modeling practices, or workflow improvement.
  • Broader NX Analysis experience and the ability to connect analysis results to design changes, performance, and risk.
  • Experience with joining strategies and the relationship between joint design, load transfer, durability, process capability, and production performance.
  • Experience with DFMEA, tolerance analysis, durability thinking, design optimization, or failure-mode anticipation.
  • Experience leading configuration or design changes across load paths, interfaces, tooling, joining, validation, and released data.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence technical decisions without formal authority through facts, alternatives, and practical recommendations.
  • Experience coaching or developing less-experienced designers in NX modeling, virtual integration, load-path reasoning, DFM/DFA, or review discipline.
  • Master’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline.

title: Project Management Assistant - cFSP
description:
Why Join Clinical Functional Service Partnerships (CFSP)?

At IQVIA, our Clinical Functional Service Partnership (CFSP) models offer the best of both worlds: the opportunity to work as an integrated member of a leading sponsor's team while benefiting from the global expertise, career development and support of IQVIA. CFSP roles provide the opportunity to develop specialist expertise on a dedicated program, with the flexibility to expand across sponsors and therapeutic areas as your career progresses.

Through our long-standing partnerships with top pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, you will contribute to the delivery of cutting-edge clinical research programs that bring innovative treatments to patients worldwide. Our professionals support studies across all phases of development and a broad range of therapeutic areas, gaining valuable experience in diverse and dynamic research environments.


Project Management Assistant

At IQVIA, as a Senior Project Management Assistant (PMA), you will play a critical role in the operational delivery of clinical trials, partnering closely with Clinical Trial Leads and global cross-functional teams to ensure studies are executed efficiently, compliantly, and inspection-ready. Acting as a senior member of the trial team, you will coordinate key study activities across systems, documentation, finance, training, and vendor oversight, driving operational excellence and consistency throughout the clinical trial lifecycle.


This is an exciting opportunity to join a leading sponsor environment where you will leverage your expertise in clinical operations, trial coordination, quality, and process improvement to support regional and global studies. Beyond study execution, you will serve as a trusted subject matter expert, mentoring colleagues, contributing to capability building across the PMA community, and helping shape best practices within one of the world's leading clinical research organizations.


Key responsibilities

• Establish and manage performance dashboards, analyze event triggers/alerts and determine appropriate follow up for Project Leader (PL) or other function(s) to act upon.

• Coordinate project schedule and ensure timely updates of all key milestone and partner with PL on related calls.

• Coordinate and support the risk and issue management process.

• Manage all aspects of the Project Finances including Estimate at Completion (EAC), monthly expenses, invoices and reconciliation.

• Demonstrate compliance with the Vendor and Purchase Order (PO) Management process.

• Implement and maintain baseline and change control processes.

• Ensure PL has timely and accurate data on areas including cost, schedule, scope, utilization, change orders and quality to support better decision-making.

• Develop and maintain relevant sections of Project Management Plans.

• Review and support project resource allocation within project budgeted for assigned portfolio/ projects.

• Prepare correspondence, including meeting minutes, for project team and/or customer.

• Organize and partner with PL in managing internal project team and customer meetings.

• Prepare project status reports and presentation materials for internal project team and customer meetings.

• Manage and coordinate core file reviews and support audits as needed. Drive e Trial Master File (eTMF) filing compliance focusing on completeness, timeliness and quality.

• Manage project specific eTraining and oversee compliance.

• Coordinate and support onboarding of new Key Project Team Members and system access.

• Monitor project metrics and make required updates in IQVIA systems to ensure accurate and timely reporting is available to senior management.

• Participate in regional initiatives to support Project Management Analyst (PMA) community and aid personal development.


What we’re looking for

• Bachelor's Degree Life sciences or other related field Req

• Minimum 2 years of prior relevant experience as a PMA.

• Communication - strong written and verbal communication skills including good command of English language.

• Problem solving - problem solving skills.

• Results-oriented approach to work delivery and output.

• Collaboration - ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with coworkers, managers and clients.

• Cross-collaboration - ability to work across geographies displaying high awareness and understanding of cultural differences.

• IQVIA Core Competencies - ability to demonstrate all IQVIA competencies (Client Focus, Collaboration, Communication, innovation, Ownership).


Build Your Future with IQVIA

If you're looking for a role that combines clinical trial delivery, project leadership, sponsor partnership and career growth, we would love to hear from you. At IQVIA, you will have the opportunity to work on innovative studies, collaborate with industry-leading sponsors, leverage cutting-edge technology and develop your career within a global organization dedicated to transforming healthcare and improving patient outcomes worldwide.

IQVIA is a leading global provider of clinical research services, commercial insights and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences and healthcare industries. We create intelligent connections to accelerate the development and commercialization of innovative medical treatments to help improve patient outcomes and population health worldwide. Learn more at

title: Data Domain Lead Corporate Functions (m/f/d)
description:
As a Data Domain Lead, Corporate Functions, you will drive and coordinate data governance across the corporate functions of Fresenius SE, ensuring clear ownership, stewardship, and accountability for critical data assets. Acting as the central governance coordinator, you will connect enterprise-wide standards with operational execution and establish consistent governance practices across functions, domains, and transformation initiatives.


You will collaborate closely with business and IT stakeholders, governance teams, and senior leadership to embed data quality, compliance, and lifecycle governance into daily operations and transformation initiatives. Your work will enable trusted, well-governed, and business-ready data that supports operational excellence and enterprise-wide decision-making.

Your responsibilities:

  • Act as the central point of coordination for data governance across the corporate functions of Fresenius SE, ensuring clear ownership, stewardship, and escalation paths.
  • Define and enforce governance policies, standards, and frameworks across data domains and stakeholders, with orchestration rather than delivery execution as the focus of the role.
  • Ensure enterprise governance standards are consistently applied in transformation programs and business-as-usual operations.
  • Coordinate execution across data quality, stewardship, lifecycle governance, and architecture alignment, while building additional execution capacity as demand grows.
  • Manage local data accountability across the central functions and maintain alignment with enterprise governance standards.
  • Own the orchestration and resolution of data quality, stewardship, and cross-domain governance issues, escalating to the Group Data Office where required.
  • Ensure lifecycle governance and audit compliance are aligned across architecture, data management, and enterprise data domains.
  • Advise business partners and senior stakeholders on complex governance requirements, translating them into reliable concepts and reviewing relevant solution proposals.
  • Manage governance risks, remediation activities, and governance reviews to strengthen accountability and continuously improve governance processes.


Your qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in data governance, stewardship, and enterprise data management.
  • Proven ability to lead and coordinate enterprise-wide data governance initiatives across multiple functions and stakeholders.
  • Experience managing cross-functional programs involving data quality, master data, metadata, and compliance requirements.
  • Strong governance orchestration and decision-making facilitation skills, with the ability to align business priorities, governance standards, and operational execution.
  • Experience coordinating complex initiatives in matrix organizations without direct authority.
  • Strong stakeholder management, negotiation, and conflict resolution capabilities, including collaboration with senior stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage governance risks, issue escalation, and remediation activities effectively, with a focus on standardization, accountability, and operational excellence.
  • Fluent German and English, written and spoken.

Drive the future of the Group Data Governance Office — join #futurefresenius and apply now through our online portal to make an impact!
